REQUIRED_EVIDENCE.BAYESIAN_FOLLOWUP: When these methods are used, disclose modeled hierarchy, model set and weights, approximation/mixing, and the claimed calibration target; use ESI-PROF-A006. No requirement to use all these methods.

EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.procedure: Under a linear Gaussian model, quadratic penalties and Gaussian priors yield related estimators; inspect likelihood-versus-prior influence, tune with an appropriate method and test plausible alternative commitments. Apply the four-state rule without converting missingness into failure.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.authoritative_outcomes: PASS: commitments and tuning are explicit and plausible sensitivity remains within the declared use tolerance. FAIL: a purported data-only claim changes materially under equally plausible prior choices or a false prior excludes known possibilities. UNKNOWN: sensitivity, hyperparameter uncertainty or likelihood adequacy is unexamined. INAPPLICABLE: no prior/penalty/constraining assumption affects the estimator.
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.cheap_path_semantics: The cost/cheaper-alternative field is a legitimate method choice. It is not automatically an inapplicable evaluation.

signature.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Conditional finite Gaussian calculations may be exact; hierarchy/model averaging can require approximate integration, truncation and convergence diagnostics. A theorem for a limiting posterior or sampler does not determine an arbitrary finite-run error. Independent field replication and application-specific coverage remain unestablished here.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.LIMIT: Read the positive/restricted alternative in that case; rejected overclaims have no positive universal witness.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.MECHANISM: Misspecified decay, stability, prior support or likelihood can bias results and make uncertainty misleading.

signature.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: For the method actually used, the required likelihood/prior/model conditions, uncertainty interpretation, approximation quality or consumer-relevant sensitivity/calibration evidence is unestablished.
signature.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: no prior/penalty/constraining assumption affects the estimator.
signature.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Regularized uniqueness mistaken for observational uniqueness; dismissing a useful well-justified prior solely because it is a prior.
signature.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Choose hyperparameters to produce narrow intervals while omitting sensitivity and validation failures.
signature.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Reassess after regime change, new prior knowledge, kernel or consumer loss change.
signature.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Hyperparameter tuning and sensitivity analysis add computation; elaborate kernels can hide assumptions. Use a simple low-order model or direct measured response when it performs adequately without elaborate hyperparameter fitting.
signature.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conditional linear-Gaussian identities, author simulation comparisons and an analytical prior-versus-likelihood discriminator.

signature.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Kernel and Gaussian-process regularization: Regularization can reduce variance and encode useful smoothness/stability, but the result remains conditional on prior support and tuning; narrow uncertainty is not evidence the prior is correct.
signature.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Impulse-response estimate with specified kernel, observation model and hyperparameters.; g:finite impulse-response coefficients or defined function space;L:known convolution operator;K,Sigma:covariances;y:data.
signature.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: g:finite impulse-response coefficients or defined function space;L:known convolution operator;K,Sigma:covariances;y:data. Kernel units are impulse-response covariance units; noise variance output².
signature.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Conditional expectation under the stipulated prior/likelihood; not a frequentist universal statement about physicalg.
signature.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: Impulse-response estimate with specified kernel, observation model and hyperparameters.
signature.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Dataset-conditional posterior; consistency or uncertainty coverage needs additional asymptotic/model conditions.
signature.ASSUMPTIONS: Known input/operator; specified Gaussian error model for exact Bayes interpretation; fixed or explicitly estimated hyperparameters; true behavior compatible with intended prior support.
signature.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Finite noisy data with high-dimensional impulse responses or uncertain order where a smooth stable class is plausible. Outside: No regularization/prior interpretation, or exact adequately conditioned finite regression.
signature.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For y=Lg+e, g~N(0,K),e~N(0,Sigma) independent and known K,Sigma, posterior mean is K L^T(L K L^T+Sigma)^-1 y when inverse exists; interpretation is conditional on this model. If hyperparameters are uncertain, the full posterior is the integral over p(η|D). A reported plug-in or joint-MAP result passes only its stated conditional/optimization semantics and must not be presented as that integral.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.PROVENANCE: Researcher-proposed operational specification derived from cited source distinctions; constructed formulas are labeled in the case ledger. It is not represented as verbatim source notation or an externally mandated rule.
SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.SOURCE_DEFINED_COMPONENTS: Specific theorem/definition/equation locators are in supporting links; a combined operational acceptance rule is researcher synthesis.

signature.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Record covariance/penalty and derive estimator; vary plausible kernels and hyperparameters, checking held-out target behavior. External observation correspondence remains distinct from stipulated model quantities.
REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Known input/operator; specified Gaussian error model for exact Bayes interpretation; fixed or explicitly estimated hyperparameters; true behavior compatible with intended prior support.
Record covariance/penalty and derive estimator; vary plausible kernels and hyperparameters, checking held-out target behavior.
Plug-in empirical Bayes covariance omits hyperparameter uncertainty unless separately accounted for.

Explicit prior and hyperprior, integration versus optimization choice, support, truncation, numerical convergence and sensitivity. For CL033-style block optimization, state that global optimality is not implied.
signature.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Record covariance/penalty and derive estimator; vary plausible kernels and hyperparameters, checking held-out target behavior. Evaluate applicability first; then expression; then external premise/representation support. Preserve contrary evidence.
signature.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact finite algebra in the explicitly constructed cases; Plug-in empirical Bayes covariance omits hyperparameter uncertainty unless separately accounted for. Operational qualitative rules require justified review rather than an assumed total decision algorithm.
signature.POSITIVE_WITNESS: CL010 proposition3 establishes the posterior-mean/regularization relation and proposition10 a stable prior construction.
signature.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: A stable kernel returns a stable estimate for an unstable actual plant and the analyst treats this as measured stability.
signature.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown covariance, unsupported prior support, tuning reused validation data or unexamined hyperparameter sensitivity.
signature.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No regularization/prior interpretation, or exact adequately conditioned finite regression.
signature.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Priors can create apparent identifiability and precision unsupported by data. A model PASS without external premise support is a false promotion; an overly broad guard can reject the legitimate cheap path: Use a low-dimensional unregularized fit when information and validation already suffice; no kernel is mandatory.
signature.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Selecting the target/envelope after seeing results, omitting material alternatives, or reporting the convenient model result while suppressing unknown covariance, unsupported prior support, tuning reused validation data or unexamined hyperparameter sensitivity.
signature.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Reassess after evidence of instability, different decay scales/noise, changed input distribution or target requiring omitted dynamics.
signature.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Kernel/hyperparameter selection and sensitivity checks cost computation; strong priors can mask weak data. Use a low-dimensional unregularized fit when information and validation already suffice; no kernel is mandatory.
signature.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conditional Bayes/regularization correspondence; no universal comparative superiority or external calibration.

PASS.MODEL: The conditional posterior/penalized estimator algebra holds.
PASS.EXTERNAL: Observed data and domain evidence support the prior/likelihood envelope; this support is defeasible.

FAIL.MODEL: An asserted estimator correspondence contradicts its covariance/penalty model. Calling a joint-MAP point estimate a fully integrated posterior without an additional integration procedure is an inferential mismatch.
FAIL.EXTERNAL: Known unstable behavior or noise mismatch invalidates the external prior-based claim.

UNKNOWN.MODEL: Unknown covariance, unsupported prior support, tuning reused validation data or unexamined hyperparameter sensitivity. The predicate is not thereby false. An unexamined MCMC mixing error or unresolved joint local optimum can leave the claimed numerical approximation unknown.
UNKNOWN.EXTERNAL: Unestablished observation, class or premise correspondence: Unknown covariance, unsupported prior support, tuning reused validation data or unexamined hyperparameter sensitivity.

INAPPLICABLE.MODEL: No regularization/prior interpretation, or exact adequately conditioned finite regression.
INAPPLICABLE.EXTERNAL: No regularization/prior interpretation, or exact adequately conditioned finite regression. Do not count inapplicability as positive evidence.

signature.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: SPECIFICATION_ONLY_FOR_EXTERNAL_TARGET; constructed/source witnesses separately evaluated in criticism.json.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Typed uncertainty and claim-specific calibration

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Frequentist confidence, Bayesian posterior uncertainty and deterministic feasible-set traditions
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: confidence region; credible region; feasible set; robust uncertainty set
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Express what can still be wrong about an estimate under an explicit uncertainty model.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Numerically similar intervals are treated as interchangeable assurances or omit structural uncertainty.
GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: No first-invention claim is made from retrospective similarity. Native vocabulary and the scope of later operational predicates remain distinct.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Every uncertainty object should state its probability/set semantics, assumptions, approximations and consumer consequence.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: An uncertainty statement linked to a model, data process and decision
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Numerically similar intervals are treated as interchangeable assurances or omit structural uncertainty.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Distinguish repeated-sampling coverage, posterior mass, deterministic error-bounded feasibility and a robust design envelope; separate parameter, model-structure and observation uncertainty.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Time-uniform finite-sample confidence and multi-output regression bounds refine asymptotics without removing their assumptions. Misspecification theory separates concentration on a pseudo-true target from coverage calibration; averaging does not erase omitted-family uncertainty.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Prevents an interval from granting a stronger reliability or safety claim than it carries.

PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE.EVIDENCE: Formal conditional bounds and semantics; no universal empirical calibration result.
PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE.UNPROVED: No universal cost-benefit advantage or target-system effect is asserted.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reader choosing a decision rule or composing the uncertainty with a controller.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: An explicit qualitative unknown or conservative engineering range can be more honest than an uncalibrated numerical probability.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.CANONICAL_COMMON_AND_DISTINCT_CONTENT: Both separate confidence coverage, posterior belief, deterministic sets and model uncertainty. A adds misspecification concentration and Bernstein-von-Mises limits; B adds averaging variance, prior model redundancy and dynamic model averaging with real mill data.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A bound, interval, probability or confidence statement is presented as evidence.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: An explicit qualitative unknown or conservative engineering range can be more honest than an uncalibrated numerical probability.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Data-generating law or deterministic bounds, target quantity, confidence/credibility level, time scope and approximation are specified.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: An uncertainty statement linked to a model, data process and decision; Coverage is conditional on the theorem’s model; Bayesian probability conditions on prior/likelihood; robust sets may be design choices rather than estimated sets.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Coverage is conditional on the theorem’s model; Bayesian probability conditions on prior/likelihood; robust sets may be design choices rather than estimated sets.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Technical or researcher-proposed assurance condition, not a universally mandatory norm. Any use as an acceptance gate requires a justified consumer requirement.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Bind the model class, data, observation semantics, policy, assumptions and thresholds to the claim. Data-generating law or deterministic bounds, target quantity, confidence/credibility level, time scope and approximation are specified.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.SEMANTICS: Listed dependencies are compositional candidates with directions specified in composition_relations, not an automatic all-required checklist.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Wrong noise tails, selected stopping time, prior misspecification, neglected hyperparameters or omitted structural error can invalidate interpretation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Calibration or sensitivity work may be expensive; choose uncertainty machinery proportional to the decision.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Reevaluate after data policy, stopping rule, noise model, prior or model class changes.

For a common estimand Δ, model averaging uses p(Δ|D)=Σ_k p(Δ|M_k,D)w_k, with w_k proportional to p(D|M_k)p(M_k). The total posterior variance is Σ_k w_k[Var(Δ|M_k,D)+(E(Δ|M_k,D)−E(Δ|D))²]. Averaging incompatible parameter coordinates lacks this common-estimand meaning; future output is a natural shared target.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Recursive estimation, forgetting and information retention

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Recursive identification predates modern online learning; exponential forgetting addresses change but can discard information in unexcited directions. Variable-direction and subspace tracking methods refine this tradeoff.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Recursive least squares; forgetting factor; covariance windup; variable-direction forgetting.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Exponentially weighted least squares discounts old errors; a recursion updates its information matrix. Direction-selective forgetting avoids erasing unrefreshed directions, but convergence still needs information and suitable drift/noise assumptions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Forgetting can create covariance windup and chase noise; remedies for boundedness can be mistaken for identification.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Online updating must track what information is being retained and lost; bounded parameters or frequent updates do not imply current true-parameter estimates.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A recursive estimator, information matrix, observation stream and drift/excitation conditions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Interpreting bounded coefficients under absentPE as proof that unknown dynamics have been learned.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Exponentially weighted least squares discounts old errors; a recursion updates its information matrix. Direction-selective forgetting avoids erasing unrefreshed directions, but convergence still needs information and suitable drift/noise assumptions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use direction-sensitive updates or finite-window tracking with explicit error tubes; permit freezing rather than mandatory adaptation. CL035 extends currentness from drifting coefficients to drifting candidate weights, using distinct discount factors. This permits an old model to regain weight, but posterior updates alone do not verify a changed external regime.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Adapt where beneficial while preserving information that new data do not replace.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Primary conditional results and constructed variance floor, not a field comparison of all forgetting schemes.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Plant changes enough to justify online adaptation and fresh data are informative about the changing directions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Use no forgetting or freeze an adequate model when the plant is stationary or the current window carries no new information.

EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.EXPRESSION: For scalar stationary-mean observations with iid noise variance sigma²>=0 and normalized exponential weights (1−lambda)lambda^j, j>=0, with fixed lambda in (0,1), the infinite-history variance is sigma²(1−lambda)/(1+lambda). It is strictly positive when sigma²>0 and equals zero when sigma²=0. The admissible positive-noise case refutes a general consistency guarantee from fixed forgetting alone; this does not assert failure in the noiseless case, for every estimator, or when lambda changes toward1.

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.justification_and_limit: Validation logic transfers through the target unit/information map, not by borrowing a time-series theorem for unrelated protocols, populations or interventions.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.justification_and_limit: A rigid validation checklist can waste data or miss subtle leakage; unknown dependence can defeat nominally independent splits.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.justification_and_limit: Declared prediction/transfer population; legitimate information at decision time; correct dependence treatment; preprocessing/feature selection/tuning isolation; reliable outcome oracle and metric.

IDENTIFIABILITY.justification_and_limit: Even valid predictive evaluation does not identify a unique generating law.

DATA_INFORMATIVENESS.justification_and_limit: Units/regimes must carry information about the claimed transfer.

ESTIMATOR_ASSUMPTIONS.justification_and_limit: Valid AR CV is conditional, not guaranteed by residual uncorrelatedness alone.

UNCERTAINTY_CALIBRATION.justification_and_limit: Variance/error estimates need sampling assumptions; iid intervals cannot be assumed.

EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.justification_and_limit: Held-out units, regimes or sites answer different questions.

Reconstruct what information each prediction may use; evaluate on prespecified cases and compare residuals/failures with model assumptions.
Finite tests have power limits; a low error can result from leakage or an easy unrepresentative regime.
signature.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Reconstruct what information each prediction may use; evaluate on prespecified cases and compare residuals/failures with model assumptions. Evaluate applicability first; then expression; then external premise/representation support. Preserve contrary evidence.
signature.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact finite algebra in the explicitly constructed cases; Finite tests have power limits; a low error can result from leakage or an easy unrepresentative regime. Operational qualitative rules require justified review rather than an assumed total decision algorithm.
signature.POSITIVE_WITNESS: XCL11 computes100-step output1.01^100≈2.7048 despite one-step error0.01; CL023 permits ordinaryCV under stated autoregressive assumptions.
signature.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Random row splitting with future-derived features leaks deployment-inaccessible information; conversely categorically rejecting all autoregressiveCV overstates dependence objection.
signature.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Undocumented tuning/test reuse, unknown feature timing, unrepresentative held-out data or insufficient test power.
signature.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No external predictive/use claim, e.g. an openly constructed algebraic example.
signature.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Validation rituals can optimize a proxy or enact a blanket time-split rule unrelated to the actual dependence/model. A model PASS without external premise support is a false promotion; an overly broad guard can reject the legitimate cheap path: For a modest in-regime one-step prediction task, a supported autoregressive validation scheme can suffice; no mandatory full physical reconstruction.
signature.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Selecting the target/envelope after seeing results, omitting material alternatives, or reporting the convenient model result while suppressing undocumented tuning/test reuse, unknown feature timing, unrepresentative held-out data or insufficient test power.
signature.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Repeat affected validation after model selection, feature leakage, regime, horizon, observation or consumer changes.
signature.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Independent experiments and long horizons cost time; overlarge validation programs can exceed decision value. For a modest in-regime one-step prediction task, a supported autoregressive validation scheme can suffice; no mandatory full physical reconstruction.
signature.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Specific tested prediction/behavior and statistically qualified generalization; not generating-mechanism truth.

PASS.MODEL: Protocol checks the stipulated target without violating its information assumptions.
PASS.EXTERNAL: Observed evaluation is relevant to deployment within stated uncertainty; passing finite tests remains defeasible.

FAIL.MODEL: A constructed protocol leaks prohibited information or tests the wrong horizon/quantity.
FAIL.EXTERNAL: Relevant held-out errors/counterexamples violate the acceptance claim; non-rejection does not prove universal adequacy.

UNKNOWN.MODEL: Undocumented tuning/test reuse, unknown feature timing, unrepresentative held-out data or insufficient test power. The predicate is not thereby false.
UNKNOWN.EXTERNAL: Unestablished observation, class or premise correspondence: Undocumented tuning/test reuse, unknown feature timing, unrepresentative held-out data or insufficient test power.

INAPPLICABLE.MODEL: No external predictive/use claim, e.g. an openly constructed algebraic example.
INAPPLICABLE.EXTERNAL: No external predictive/use claim, e.g. an openly constructed algebraic example. Do not count inapplicability as positive evidence.

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.justification_and_limit: No external standard or normative mandate is asserted for this mathematical/descriptive candidate. Proposed intake checks are researcher constructions.

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.justification_and_limit: Published procedures or supplied code establish inspectable mechanisms; this branch did not execute those research implementations.

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.justification_and_limit: Validation logic transfers through the target unit/information map, not by borrowing a time-series theorem for unrelated protocols, populations or interventions.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.justification_and_limit: A rigid validation checklist can waste data or miss subtle leakage; unknown dependence can defeat nominally independent splits.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.justification_and_limit: Declared prediction/transfer population; legitimate information at decision time; correct dependence treatment; preprocessing/feature selection/tuning isolation; reliable outcome oracle and metric.

IDENTIFIABILITY.justification_and_limit: Even valid predictive evaluation does not identify a unique generating law.

DATA_INFORMATIVENESS.justification_and_limit: Units/regimes must carry information about the claimed transfer.

ESTIMATOR_ASSUMPTIONS.justification_and_limit: Valid AR CV is conditional, not guaranteed by residual uncorrelatedness alone.

UNCERTAINTY_CALIBRATION.justification_and_limit: Variance/error estimates need sampling assumptions; iid intervals cannot be assumed.

EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.justification_and_limit: Held-out units, regimes or sites answer different questions.

ORACLE_OR_OBSERVATION_RELIABILITY.justification_and_limit: Wrong labels or inaccessible decision-time features invalidate apparent validation.

REPRESENTATION_CORRESPONDENCE.justification_and_limit: A valid predictive metric does not establish correct latent semantics.

DECISION_USE_VALIDITY.justification_and_limit: Loss, horizon and target population must match use.

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Different classical and modern results prove identifiability, consistency, covariance, finite error, realization or tracking under different classes. Their maturation does not create one interchangeable guarantee.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Consistency; asymptotic normality; finite-sample bound; confidence coverage; robust containment; tracking.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Type the conclusion, enumerate premises and connect them to acquisition/implementation evidence; distinguish a theorem being true from its assumptions being supported in deployment.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: A correct theorem can confer false certainty when its hardest assumptions are treated as verified by the theorem itself.

signature.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact finite algebra in the explicitly constructed cases; A premise can be mathematically precise yet externally unobservable; no boolean promotion from assumption to fact. Operational qualitative rules require justified review rather than an assumed total decision algorithm.
signature.POSITIVE_WITNESS: CL017 exact finite SPS region differs from its conservative outer ellipsoid; CL019 theorem2.1 requires fully observed nonexplosive Gaussian-driven states.
signature.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: CL018 bounded-supportO(1/T)-type shrinkage is presented as contradicting an unbounded-GaussianO(1/sqrtT) lower bound.
signature.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unestablished model/noise/support/initialization premise; abstract-only theorem; numerical implementation differs from analyzed algorithm.
signature.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No theorem/statistical guarantee invoked; a purely exploratory observation remains exploratory.
signature.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: A correct theorem can confer false certainty when its hardest assumptions are treated as verified by the theorem itself. A model PASS without external premise support is a false promotion; an overly broad guard can reject the legitimate cheap path: Use an honest empirical bounded claim when theorem assumptions cannot be established; no requirement for a theorem for every useful model.
signature.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Selecting the target/envelope after seeing results, omitting material alternatives, or reporting the convenient model result while suppressing unestablished model/noise/support/initialization premise; abstract-only theorem; numerical implementation differs from analyzed algorithm.
signature.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Re-evaluate after theorem/version, model class, observation/noise, algorithm approximation, sample regime or decision changes.
signature.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Premise checking can be hard or impossible; conservative theorem constants may be less useful than qualified experiments. Use an honest empirical bounded claim when theorem assumptions cannot be established; no requirement for a theorem for every useful model.
signature.EVIDENCE_CEILING: The precisely typed theorem plus evidence-supported applicability; no stronger external claim.

PASS.MODEL: The logical implication and implementation assumptions are valid in the specified mathematical domain.
PASS.EXTERNAL: Evidence supports the external bridge and material premises to the explicitly stated ceiling.

FAIL.MODEL: A conclusion or premise is misstated, or an explicit model counterexample violates the advertised implication.
FAIL.EXTERNAL: A known premise/representation mismatch invalidates the transferred guarantee; it need not refute the original theorem.

UNKNOWN.MODEL: Unestablished model/noise/support/initialization premise; abstract-only theorem; numerical implementation differs from analyzed algorithm. The predicate is not thereby false.
UNKNOWN.EXTERNAL: Unestablished observation, class or premise correspondence: Unestablished model/noise/support/initialization premise; abstract-only theorem; numerical implementation differs from analyzed algorithm.

INAPPLICABLE.MODEL: No theorem/statistical guarantee invoked; a purely exploratory observation remains exploratory.
INAPPLICABLE.EXTERNAL: No theorem/statistical guarantee invoked; a purely exploratory observation remains exploratory. Do not count inapplicability as positive evidence.

signature.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: SPECIFICATION_ONLY_FOR_EXTERNAL_TARGET; constructed/source witnesses separately evaluated in criticism.json.

CL031 contains simulated controller comparisons, CL033 reports hierarchical-MAP benchmark behavior and local-minimum outliers, and CL034 supplies primary criticism of model-averaging inference. These are bounded examples showing why different mathematical and empirical claims must be distinguished; they do not measure the field benefit of a guarantee-transfer procedure.

records.title: Rejected universal preference for continuous refitting

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Rejected universal preference for continuous refitting

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Online estimation enables adaptation; variable-direction forgetting and current benchmarks expose why update frequency is not itself a payoff.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Continuous refitting; exponential forgetting; update benefit; lifecycle comparator
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Automatically refresh model parameters whenever new data arrive.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Routine updates can amplify noise, forget informative directions, spend resources or destabilize use without improving the decision.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.SPECIFIC_CLAIM: Loss of excitation makes forgetting hazardous.
Current online method still has noise, slow-drift and field-validation limits.
Cheap baselines can remain competitive and some more complex fits are unstable.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: The rejected universal practice is not imputed to every adaptive-estimation author. No claim that fixed models are always better.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Candidate universal proposition: updating continuously always improves model use. Reject it; require a material change/benefit case and compare against retaining the validated model or a cheaper fallback.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A model update policy and its downstream decision/lifecycle cost
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Fresh parameters or lower training loss are substituted for improved useful behavior.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Actual useful adaptation responds to identifiable change with informative evidence; assess update error/cost against a fixed or simpler comparator before relying on it.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Triggered, information-aware updates with retained baseline, validated improvement and retirement/fallback conditions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Avoid needless computation and noise-driven degradation while preserving adaptation when it demonstrably helps.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Recent nonlinear baselines and FEM/PINN timing studies show why training, evaluation and method-specific costs must be compared; neither supplies a universal ranking of refitting policies. The constant-target risk calculation refutes an unrestricted always-better claim; RLS information recursion provides a separate direction-specific failure mechanism.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Update now, retain the current model, gather data or fall back.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.CANONICAL_COMMON_AND_DISTINCT_CONTENT: A tests the always-better proposition; B tests removal/rejection warrant and qualified update alternatives. Keep both targets and separate currentness, change detection, recursive mechanism and value. ESI-CA-001 operative repair: bind the original universal domain and claim parameters, require whole-target proof for a universal PASS, and allocate real-drift benefit only to its separately bounded target. Solely bounded claims are INAPPLICABLE to the universal evaluator; unknown premises of an asserted universal remain UNKNOWN unless a reliable in-domain falsifier decides FAIL.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A policy claims continuous updating is intrinsically beneficial regardless of drift, excitation, cost or decision.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A constant known target with a validated exact fixed estimate needs no noisy refit; a stable bounded use can retain that estimate. This cheaper alternative can falsify the asserted universal when admitted by its original domain. The universal evaluator is INAPPLICABLE only if no criticized universal is asserted; a solely bounded update claim has a separate target.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Any positive update-value claim requires a defined decision loss, currentness/information evidence, comparator, update cost and reuse horizon; different cost dimensions are not summed without an explicit conversion.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Total decision value of an update over a stated horizon, separate from in-sample estimator fit.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: No universal rejection of online adaptation; no arbitrary numerical utility from ordinal model scores or incomparable timing/currency units.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record old/new models, training and assessment data, detector/update policy, all tuning/validation costs and actual downstream use.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: C0110 currentness, C0111 honest comparison, C0101 regime and C0112 conditional guarantees. Frequent adaptation can conflict with stability and independence of evaluation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: No drift, no excitation, noisy observation or biased evaluation can make the new model worse; expensive training can erase inference savings.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Retain the validated fixed estimate until informative change warrants updating; use selective/event-triggered methods when justified
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Update when new justified change/information can alter the consumer’s decision; retire the policy when measured benefit no longer covers its declared costs.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Continuous updating weakly improves every admissible use
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: AlwaysBetter(U0,F0,D0,L0,H0,Q0), with update policy, fixed comparator, original environment/data domain, loss/benefit criterion, horizon and realization-versus-risk quantifier mode bound to the originally asserted universal.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Loss in declared units; data noise variance same squared units; time/use horizon specified; costs separately recorded
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Bind the original assertion before evaluating: update policy U0, fixed comparator F0, originally asserted environment/data domain D0, loss or benefit criterion L0, horizon H0, and whether the claim concerns every realization or expected risk under every claimed distribution. Require R(U0,e,L0,H0) ≤ R(F0,e,L0,H0) for every e in that original D0 with the original quantifier mode. A proof over a proper subclass D1 or a beneficial drift case cannot establish the original all-environment claim. Do not narrow D0, change the comparator, or replace the loss/horizon after inspecting results.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: update policy and predictive/decision risk
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Universal policy claim over specified class; not a finite observed-benefit assertion
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: A proof or falsifier must match the original policy/comparator, domain, loss, horizon and quantifier mode. The existing counterexample uses a known stationary target, an available exact fixed comparator and a mean-zero variance-one observation. Its admissibility in the originally asserted domain must be established. Unknown premises leave an asserted claim applicable and may require UNKNOWN; they are not guard-false conditions.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: The criticized always-better assertion is itself asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed: continuous refitting weakly improves every admissible use over the originally asserted environment/data domain. A separately bounded update-benefit claim alone does not activate this universal evaluator. Unknown domain details, premises or evidence for an asserted universal claim do not make the guard false.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: First bind the criticized universal to its originally asserted domain, policy/comparator, loss, horizon and data quantifiers. PASS only if a sound argument establishes that exact original universal over its entire original domain and premises. A restricted theorem-backed class, successful real-drift update or finite favorable comparison cannot supply that PASS. FAIL if a reliable admissible stationary/noisy-refit or other counterexample falsifies the originally asserted universal; for an expected-risk claim, establish the risk comparison rather than treating one unfavorable realization as an expectation. Additional cost refutes the claim only when the original criterion includes that cost in declared units or explicitly makes the corresponding resource guarantee. UNKNOWN when the universal claim is asserted but its scope, premises or evidence remain unresolved and neither a sound whole-domain proof nor a reliable in-domain falsifier is available. INAPPLICABLE when no criticized universal claim is asserted, relied upon or assessed, including a solely bounded update claim; assess that bounded claim separately. A qualified update PASS or rejection-warrant PASS is never a PASS for this universal.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.basis: ESI-RS0052 forgetting mechanism; source cost comparisons

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Bind the exact original assertion and admissible environment/data conditions. Compare old/new decision risk on the same loss and horizon using a valid analytical expectation or sufficiently warranted independent comparison. Keep costs in declared units and include them in a falsifier only when the original criterion includes them. Do not replace whole-domain evidence with training improvement or selected favorable regimes.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: The original universal assertion and its domain/quantifiers; original update and fixed policies, noise/data model, loss and horizon; a scope-matching proof or an admissible reliable falsifier. For a cost-inclusive claim, preserve measured units and any consumer-defined conversion. A bounded-benefit witness must retain its own restricted target.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Identify whether the criticized universal is actually asserted; if only a bounded update claim is made, return INAPPLICABLE here and assess that claim separately. For an asserted universal, freeze its original domain and claim parameters. Check proof coverage against that full target and check counterexample admissibility. In the stationary target-0 construction, fixed prediction 0 has expected squared loss 0 while refitting to mean-zero variance-one observation has expected squared loss 1; if admitted by the original claim, return FAIL. A beneficial real-drift update only establishes its restricted comparison. Use UNKNOWN when required scope or evidence remains unresolved without a decisive falsifier; never shrink the original domain to produce PASS.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact expectation in the constructed case; real total value requires empirical evidence and consumer valuation
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: No positive witness establishes the criticized unrestricted all-environment proposition. A positive truth witness would have to prove the exact original universal across its entire originally asserted domain and quantifiers. The original beneficial real-drift update is retained separately as a bounded-alternative witness and does not satisfy this positive-witness slot.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Existing analytical construction: target is fixed at 0; fixed prediction 0 has expected squared loss 0; refitting to one mean-zero variance-one observation has expected squared loss 1. This FAILs the universal when the original asserted domain admits that stationary/noisy context and the stated comparator and loss. It is not evidence that every adaptive policy is inferior.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The criticized universal is asserted but its originally claimed domain/quantifier mode, noise, comparator, loss, horizon, premise support or evidence is unresolved, and neither a reliable admissible falsifier nor a sound whole-domain proof decides it. Unknown drift or other premises are not grounds for INAPPLICABLE. A sufficient counterexample can still establish FAIL without resolving unrelated premises.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No criticized all-environment/always-better universal is asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed. A solely bounded theorem-backed or comparator-tested update claim is assessed separately and leaves this universal evaluator INAPPLICABLE. The presence of a conditional update alternative does not switch off an independently asserted universal.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False universal PASS from a favorable real-drift case, a theorem restricted to a smaller class, a changed comparator or training-only evaluation. False universal FAIL from an out-of-domain witness or from treating a single bad realization as an expected-risk result. Rejecting the universal must not be converted into a blanket refusal to adapt.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Narrowing the original domain after seeing a counterexample, relabeling a qualified descendant as the original claim, counting update frequency/model size/recency as benefit, or omitting failed updates and tuning costs. Preserve the originally asserted nonempty use domain rather than declaring an empty domain a practical superiority witness.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: A changed environment domain, policy, comparator, loss, horizon or quantifier mode defines a different scoped claim and requires its own evidence; it cannot retroactively turn FAIL or UNKNOWN on the original universal into PASS. New evidence can change that original verdict only while the original target remains fixed.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Retain the validated fixed estimate until informative change warrants updating; use selective/event-triggered methods when justified
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: The unrestricted always-better proposition is refuted by the admitted stationary/noisy construction. This does not rank all adaptive policies, establish a general numerical cost-benefit ratio, or refute a separately bounded update claim. No external target instance was evaluated.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: CRITICIZED_UNIVERSAL_PROPOSITION
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION_DETAIL: Truth of the originally asserted always-better refitting proposition, not the justification of a restricted update or of rejecting mandatory refitting.

EVALUATION_OUTCOMES.PASS: A sound argument establishes the exact criticized universal over its originally asserted entire domain, policy/comparator, loss, horizon and data quantifiers. No such positive witness is established for the unrestricted all-environment proposition here. A proof or benefit confined to a restricted class does not qualify.
EVALUATION_OUTCOMES.FAIL: A reliable counterexample within the original asserted domain makes the updated risk exceed the fixed-comparator risk under the original loss, horizon and quantifier mode. The stationary target/noisy-refit construction is such a witness when that context is admitted. Separate rejection-warrant assessment may PASS on the same witness.
EVALUATION_OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: The criticized universal claim is applicable, but original scope, premise support, observation correspondence or comparative evidence is unresolved and no reliable in-domain falsifier or whole-domain proof decides it. Unknown premises do not make the guard false.
EVALUATION_OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No criticized always-better universal is asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed. Only a bounded, conditional or particular update-benefit claim is made; evaluate that separate target within its own scope.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATION_PRIORITY_RULE: Select the criticized universal target and bind its originally asserted domain before applying any verdict. Preserve that target throughout evaluation. Restricted update benefit and warranted rejection are different evaluated propositions; neither can PASS the original universal. Apply the claim-presence guard before evidential premises, so unresolved premises remain UNKNOWN rather than INAPPLICABLE.

BOUNDED_ALTERNATIVE_WITNESS.description: When a parameter truly changes and informative observations identify it, a validated update can outperform stale prediction; no universal effect size asserted
BOUNDED_ALTERNATIVE_WITNESS.allocation: Existing qualified update-benefit alternative only; not a positive truth witness or PASS for the criticized universal. No new property or principal claim is introduced.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Ceremony of mandatory continuous refitting: A standing requirement to refit continuously is not a general property of good identification; update only when the information/change/decision case supports it.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: An operational refitting practice and its actual model consumer.; update policyU;baselineB;consumer lossL;costJ;regimeR;benefit criterion specified.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: update policyU;baselineB;consumer lossL;costJ;regimeR;benefit criterion specified. Costs and decision loss in declared units; cadence time; benefit can be qualitative with explicit witness.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Existence of a legitimate non-trigger context refutes universal necessity; per-case decision remains conditional.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: An operational refitting practice and its actual model consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Compare over a stated decision horizon, including delayed costs/benefits of drift detection.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: A live consumer and change/information model are required for a benefit claim; none follows from a schedule alone.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A proposed continuous or scheduled refitting rule without a demonstrated decision need. Outside: There is no imposed update practice, or a specific supported tracking requirement already governs updates.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Mandatory-refit claim is defeated when there is a relevant stationary/noisy context where a cheaper fixed/no-forgetting method meets the consumer need and refitting adds cost or variance without compensating benefit. This is a contextual counterexample, not a prohibition on adaptation.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.PROVENANCE: Researcher-proposed operational specification derived from cited source distinctions; constructed formulas are labeled in the case ledger. It is not represented as verbatim source notation or an externally mandated rule.
SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.SOURCE_DEFINED_COMPONENTS: Specific theorem/definition/equation locators are in supporting links; a combined operational acceptance rule is researcher synthesis.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Compare fixed versus updating alternatives under relevant observed/constructed drift and noise; examine whether each update is consumed. External observation correspondence remains distinct from stipulated model quantities.
REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A live consumer and change/information model are required for a benefit claim; none follows from a schedule alone.
Compare fixed versus updating alternatives under relevant observed/constructed drift and noise; examine whether each update is consumed.
Counterfactual benefit may remain uncertain; update counts alone measure activity rather than model value.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Compare fixed versus updating alternatives under relevant observed/constructed drift and noise; examine whether each update is consumed. Evaluate applicability first; then expression; then external premise/representation support. Preserve contrary evidence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact finite algebra in the explicitly constructed cases; Counterfactual benefit may remain uncertain; update counts alone measure activity rather than model value. Operational qualitative rules require justified review rather than an assumed total decision algorithm.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: XCL10 fixed forgetting has positive variance floor for a stationary mean; Åström1985 explicitly permits switching adaptation off under inadequate excitation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: A changing plant with informative measurements may require adaptation; CL030 gives a conditional tracking route, so blanket never-update is also unsupported.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: There is no imposed update practice, or a specific supported tracking requirement already governs updates.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Removing updates can leave a changing plant untracked; keeping them can create noise-driven churn and apparent freshness. A model PASS without external premise support is a false promotion; an overly broad guard can reject the legitimate cheap path: Freeze the adequate model, monitor relevant changes and refresh on material evidence; use batch sufficient statistics when appropriate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Selecting the target/envelope after seeing results, omitting material alternatives, or reporting the convenient model result while suppressing unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Retire automatic updates when marginal benefit disappears; re-enter when material drift plus useful observations and safe update conditions are established.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Compute, validation, operational churn and possible noise amplification; removal saves these but can miss real drift without monitoring. Freeze the adequate model, monitor relevant changes and refresh on material evidence; use batch sufficient statistics when appropriate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Refutation of universal necessity plus conditional alternatives; no organization-specific cost savings claimed.

PASS.MODEL: The contextual construction defeats necessity of constant refitting.
PASS.EXTERNAL: A comparable operational baseline demonstrates sufficient decision value without mandatory refresh; no such field experiment was run here.

FAIL.MODEL: The supposed cheaper baseline fails the same need or the comparison omits material drift.
FAIL.EXTERNAL: Observed decision loss from stale model defeats the local removal proposal; it does not justify universal continuous refitting.

UNKNOWN.MODEL: Unknown consumer, drift, update effect or cost; absent evidence cannot be turned into universal uselessness. The predicate is not thereby false.

RECONCILIATION.adjudication: A tests the always-better proposition; B tests removal/rejection warrant and qualified update alternatives. Keep both targets and separate currentness, change detection, recursive mechanism and value. ESI-CA-001 operative repair: bind the original universal domain and claim parameters, require whole-target proof for a universal PASS, and allocate real-drift benefit only to its separately bounded target. Solely bounded claims are INAPPLICABLE to the universal evaluator; unknown premises of an asserted universal remain UNKNOWN unless a reliable in-domain falsifier decides FAIL.
RECONCILIATION.discriminating_example: Bind the original domain before evaluating. In an admitted stationary target-0 case, fixed prediction 0 has risk 0 and a mean-zero variance-one noisy refit has risk 1: universal truth FAILs, while warranted rejection can PASS. A real-drift update can have a separate bounded PASS but cannot PASS the original all-environment claim. If only that bounded claim is made, the universal evaluator is INAPPLICABLE; if the universal is asserted with unresolved premises and no decisive proof or falsifier, it is UNKNOWN. Narrowing the domain after the counterexample does not change the original FAIL.
RECONCILIATION.evidence_limit: This does not prove fixed models are always best or that monitoring is unnecessary. Future update value is task-specific.
RECONCILIATION.reverse_inference_withheld: Shared claim vocabulary or a restricted PASS does not establish the stronger ancestor claim, universal usefulness, external truth or mandatory adoption.

bearer.value: A model update policy and its downstream decision/lifecycle cost
An operational refitting practice and its actual model consumer.

original_problem.value: Routine updates can amplify noise, forget informative directions, spend resources or destabilize use without improving the decision.
Removing updates can leave a changing plant untracked; keeping them can create noise-driven churn and apparent freshness.

claim.value: Candidate universal proposition: updating continuously always improves model use. Reject it; require a material change/benefit case and compare against retaining the validated model or a cheaper fallback.
A standing requirement to refit continuously is not a general property of good identification; update only when the information/change/decision case supports it.

mechanism.value: Actual useful adaptation responds to identifiable change with informative evidence; assess update error/cost against a fixed or simpler comparator before relying on it.
The claimed mechanism is responsiveness; it works only with meaningful drift and informative fresh observations. Otherwise updates can chase noise, erase information or perturb a safe controller.

consumer.value: Update now, retain the current model, gather data or fall back.
A proposed continuous or scheduled refitting rule without a demonstrated decision need.

historical_attribution.value: Online estimation enables adaptation; variable-direction forgetting and current benchmarks expose why update frequency is not itself a payoff.
Recursive estimation is a legitimate technique; “always refit to remain current” is a present criticized extrapolation, not a universal classical requirement.

model_information_initial_state_regime_a.value: Any positive update-value claim requires a defined decision loss, currentness/information evidence, comparator, update cost and reuse horizon; different cost dimensions are not summed without an explicit conversion.
A live consumer and change/information model are required for a benefit claim; none follows from a schedule alone.

environment_boundary.value: Total decision value of an update over a stated horizon, separate from in-sample estimator fit.
Does not reject online learning or tracking where its conditions hold. No universal maximum model age is proposed.

exclusions.value: No universal rejection of online adaptation; no arbitrary numerical utility from ordinal model scores or incomparable timing/currency units.
Refutation of universal necessity plus conditional alternatives; no organization-specific cost savings claimed.

trigger.value: A policy claims continuous updating is intrinsically beneficial regardless of drift, excitation, cost or decision.
A proposed continuous or scheduled refitting rule without a demonstrated decision need.

non_trigger_or_cheap_path.value: A constant known target with a validated exact fixed estimate needs no noisy refit; a stable bounded use can retain that estimate.
Freeze the adequate model, monitor relevant changes and refresh on material evidence; use batch sufficient statistics when appropriate.

authority.value: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.

input_provenance.value: Record old/new models, training and assessment data, detector/update policy, all tuning/validation costs and actual downstream use.

cost.value: Retain the validated fixed estimate until informative change warrants updating; use selective/event-triggered methods when justified

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Rejected identification of an unknown model by filtering alone

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Researcher-formulated boundary test distinguishing state estimation from model identification
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: filtering versus identification
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Adversarial proposition: a state-estimation recursion alone establishes the unknown system matrices and their physical meaning.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Famous filtering results are cited as model-identification or mechanistic-recovery theorems.
GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: No first-invention claim is made from retrospective similarity. The rejected proposition is an analytical discriminator, not attributed to a historical advocate.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: REJECTED: running the classical Kalman filter by itself identifies an unknown dynamical model.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: Claim about what a given-model filtering algorithm infers
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Famous filtering results are cited as model-identification or mechanistic-recovery theorems.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Classical filtering estimates a state conditional on transition/observation and noise assumptions. Unknown-model estimation requires an additional identification procedure and its information conditions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Filtering can be an ingredient of prediction-error/likelihood or joint state/parameter estimation, with extra hypotheses.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Preserves a historically and technically important target distinction.

PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE.EVIDENCE: Scope of the inspected primary filtering formulation; no survey of every adaptive Kalman variant.
PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE.UNPROVED: No universal cost-benefit advantage or target-system effect is asserted.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Reader of methods or historical accounts linking filtering to identification.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: If model matrices are already justified and only state is unknown, run the filter without an unnecessary identification project.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.CANONICAL_COMMON_AND_DISTINCT_CONTENT: A distinguishes a state-estimation recursion within supplied matrices from estimating unknown model matrices/physical meaning. B has source context but no separate property; retain this negative candidate.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A filter state estimate is used as evidence that the model itself was learned.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If model matrices are already justified and only state is unknown, run the filter without an unnecessary identification project.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Original filtering formulation conditions on a specified stochastic dynamical model.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Authorized and operationally admissible experimentation

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Identification during normal operation, admissible experiment design and robust safe-learning composition
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: admissible experiment; safe motion; bounded uncertainty
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Perturb a process enough to learn without violating its operating requirements.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: An informative or convergent experiment is treated as automatically legitimate or safe.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Information value and operational admissibility are separate obligations; an unavailable safe experiment can leave an inference unresolved.

records.title: Nonlinear adequacy and justified representation complexity

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Nonlinear adequacy and justified representation complexity

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: NARMAX input/output descriptions and nonlinear residual diagnostics coexist with block and state-space models. Founding report abstracts establish provenance only.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: NARMAX; nonlinear model validity tests; Hammerstein/Wiener models
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Recursive nonlinear input/output descriptions with stochastic innovations; higher-order residual tests for omitted nonlinear effects.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Linear descriptions and linear covariance checks can miss relevant nonlinear dynamics.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.SPECIFIC_CLAIM: Deterministic nonlinear recursive input/output model existence studied in report 251.
Stochastic NARMAX extends the deterministic report.
Higher-order tests explicitly respond to deficiencies of linear covariance tests.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: Reports 251/252 theorem bodies were not inspected; no priority claim over all nonlinear traditions. Block and feedback structures are alternatives, not stages in one inevitable ladder.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Validate the chosen behavioral class on the intended regime, horizon and observation protocol. Additional complexity requires a justified advantage over an adequate-access comparator under the predeclared consumer decision policy, subject to the applicable feasibility, risk and lifecycle-burden limits. Remedying consequential baseline inadequacy is one possible justification; a decision-relevant net benefit can also justify escalation when both models meet their hard tolerances.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A nonlinear input/output model and its claimed operating envelope
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Good fit near one operating point is mistaken for adequacy at saturation, under another excitation type, or during unobserved mode transitions.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Validate representation adequacy for the declared consumer, then compare the actual candidate and simple alternatives under the predeclared decision policy. Use informative matched evidence, explicit lifecycle burden and separate hard constraints. A pure satisficing policy can retain an adequate cheaper baseline; a policy valuing further consequential improvement can prefer a feasible candidate with warranted net benefit.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Validate the chosen behavioral class on the intended regime, horizon and observation protocol. Additional complexity requires a justified advantage over an adequate-access comparator under the predeclared consumer decision policy, subject to the applicable feasibility, risk and lifecycle-burden limits. Remedying consequential baseline inadequacy is one possible justification; a decision-relevant net benefit can also justify escalation when both models meet their hard tolerances.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Detect model inadequacy before a prediction or simulation decision depends on an untested regime.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: The 2026 benchmark reports method- and dataset-specific free-run outcomes, including unstable PNARX on ParWH; it does not establish a universally best nonlinear method. Original validation work derives tests under analytic/input-moment assumptions; the proposed envelope predicate is not a theorem.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Whether to use a linear, block, NARMAX, state-space or switched model for a specified prediction/simulation consumer.
ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Linear approximation on a bounded envelope
Separate local models with explicit switching
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_MECHANISM_AND_TARGET_DISTINCT: A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_SHARED_CONTENT: Purpose, regime, observation access and cheap alternatives determine adequacy; model size is not evidence.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Input amplitude/type, saturation, hysteresis or internal feedback materially changes the outcome relevant to use.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: A small-signal linear model validated inside |u|≤0.5 need not be replaced merely because the physical device saturates outside the authorized envelope.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: A: finite per-regime error vector and tolerance, with unstable runs explicit. B: matched baseline access, consequential improvement, cost/risk limits. A model may pass adequacy while escalation remains inapplicable or unjustified.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Observed input/output behavior and specified envelope; internal mechanisms may remain nonunique.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: A: finite per-regime error vector and tolerance, with unstable runs explicit. B: matched baseline access, consequential improvement, cost/risk limits. A model may pass adequacy while escalation remains inapplicable or unjustified.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record excitation design, sensor calibration, preprocessing fit only on training data, initial-state treatment and test regime labels.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: Depends on observation correspondence, informative excitation and C0111 validation; complex structures can conflict with C0115 cost and update stability.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Unvisited regimes remain unknown; correlated/noise-driven apparent nonlinearity can lead to wrong structure choice.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Start with a linear/simple-block baseline; collect targeted regimes only when the decision needs them
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Revalidate when excitation distribution, sensor nonlinearity, switching logic or consumer horizon changes; retire the unsupported part of the envelope.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RECONCILED_COMPOSITION_CONSEQUENCE: FR02 noise placement, FR03 mode evidence, CL18 validation and RT04 value constrain the same decision through different premises; none is implied by a local fit.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.VALUE_TYPE_AND_DOMAIN: Structured record with explicit observed, assumed, derived and missing components. Mixed categorical, time, physical-unit and currency fields; thresholds belong to the consumer.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.UNIT_OR_SCALE: Mixed categorical, time, physical-unit and currency fields; thresholds belong to the consumer.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.ALLOWED_VALUES_OR_CONSTRAINTS: Typed named components as specified; retain unknowns and evidence references. No aggregate ordinal maturity score.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.QUANTITATIVE_OR_QUALITATIVE: Mixed; quantities keep units and qualitative judgments retain their rationale.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.OBSERVED_DERIVED_ASSUMED_OR_STIPULATED: Each component must be marked separately: measured data are observed; equations/rank/contrasts may be derived; priors and inaccessible invariances are assumed; consumer tolerances are stipulated.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.MEASUREMENT_OR_DERIVATION_METHOD: Bind the use contract, decision policy and actual candidate/comparator access. Use evidence appropriate to the claim: matched held-out trajectories for the stated empirical comparison, or an explicitly stipulated finite population/valid derivation for a mathematical construction. Account separately for lifecycle burden, risk, coverage and uncertainty; a constructed comparison does not establish external plant performance.

SOURCE_OR_WITNESS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Published mixed benchmark results demonstrate that different datasets favor different model classes; this witnesses the need for conditional selection, not a blanket nonlinear win.
SOURCE_OR_WITNESS.NEGATIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: one-step prediction with frequent measured-output resets looks excellent, but the consumer needs a long free rollout that diverges.

ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.RESOLUTION_AND_UNCERTAINTY: Finite sampled regimes bound coverage; missing regime or comparator is unknown, not zero benefit.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.MISSING_UNKNOWN_NOT_APPLICABLE_DISTINCTI: MISSING means a required component was not supplied; UNKNOWN means available evidence cannot decide it; NOT_APPLICABLE requires the documented non-trigger: No nonlinear escalation or model-selection decision is under consideration.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.VALID_TIME_OR_VERSION: Bind to model/data/protocol versions and declared regime; research source cutoff 2026-11-09.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.DEPENDENT_ATTRIBUTES: The components in this record are evaluated jointly; no nonexistent external attribute dependency is asserted.
ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.CHANGE_IMPACT: Reassess after regime, controller, horizon or consequence changes; retire complexity whose incremental benefit disappears.
