PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Adequacy on a declared nonlinear envelope
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: Adequate(M,D_test,R,H,tau)
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: M model; R finite tested regime strata; H positive horizon in samples; tau_r≥0 in output units
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every declared tested stratum r∈R and requested horizon H; no universal quantification outside covered R
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: held-out traces mapped through declared sensor/units
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Finite empirical acceptance for the frozen model and current regime
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Correct grouping, uncontaminated preprocessing, tolerances set before final assessment
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A prediction/simulation use with a stated envelope and tolerance exists
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: PASS if every required stratum has usable evidence, no prohibited unstable rollout occurs, and its predeclared error criterion is met; FAIL on a measured violation; UNKNOWN for missing stratum/oracle; INAPPLICABLE without this use claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Measured output and model output share units, timestamps and initialization; error is evaluated at H, not silently substituted with one-step fit
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Frozen M, regime labels, held-out traces, metric/tolerance declaration and provenance
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Evaluate stratified errors and numerical stability; inspect nonlinear residual tests appropriate to input assumptions; log individual failures
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite test is computable; adequacy of all unseen trajectories is not decided
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Clipped actuator is exactly linear on tested |u|≤0.5; bounded local claim passes
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: M(u)=u fitted in |u|≤0.5 predicts 2 at u=2, while clip(u,-1,1)=1; expansion fails
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unobserved mode, unknown observation map, or unreported initial-state estimate
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No claim beyond a fixed observed lookup query
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False pass from missing rare modes; false rejection from a changed sensor rather than plant dynamics
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Averaging errors hides transition failure; choosing easier test inputs after seeing results
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Input envelope, sensor map, sample interval, initialization or model change requires re-evaluation
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Start with a linear/simple-block baseline; collect targeted regimes only when the decision needs them
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Empirical adequacy within tested envelope, not unique mechanism or global correctness
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Adequacy on a declared nonlinear envelope
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Nonlinear representation complexity is justified by its declared use and operating regime — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: JustifiedNonlinearity(candidate, baseline, use_contract, validation, cost_estimate)
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Mixed categorical, time, physical-unit and currency fields; thresholds belong to the consumer. Attribute ESI-RAT0119 supplies the structured arguments.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. No extrapolation from local prediction to global simulation or mechanistic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A model-selection decision and its use envelope
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The consumer decision policy, hard feasibility/tolerance conditions, risk and lifecycle-burden limits, intended output, horizon and operating range are stated before comparison. Candidate and comparator have matched observation access and are assessed for the same declared use; comparison need not claim global optimality over unexamined alternatives.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A nonlinear candidate is proposed for prediction, free simulation, control, diagnosis or explanation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Within a fixed use envelope and matched observation access, establish candidate feasibility and adherence to the declared risk/burden limits. Then determine whether the predeclared consumer policy warrants replacing the comparator. A consequential baseline tolerance failure remedied by the candidate can establish the feasibility route. When both are feasible, a warranted policy-relevant improvement after lifecycle burden can establish a net-benefit route. Under pure satisficing followed by minimum burden, an adequate cheaper baseline remains preferred. A merely smaller fit statistic, an unranked tradeoff or an invented cost exchange rate does not establish justification.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Bind the use contract, decision policy and actual candidate/comparator access. Use evidence appropriate to the claim: matched held-out trajectories for the stated empirical comparison, or an explicitly stipulated finite population/valid derivation for a mathematical construction. Account separately for lifecycle burden, risk, coverage and uncertainty; a constructed comparison does not establish external plant performance.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {decision including predeclared preference/feasibility policy and tie rule, predicted quantities and units, horizon, admissible inputs/states, measured-output access, hard tolerances, cheap comparator, lifecycle costs, risk/burden limits and their evidence/uncertainty}. Supporting source links are property-level context; a deployed judgment requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Identify whether this is a nonlinear escalation/model-selection justification claim; if absent, use INAPPLICABLE.
Bind actual versions, same-use/access correspondence, predeclared policy, hard constraints and evidence classes. Do not create a preference or silently monetize hard constraints.

If a decisive known premise refutes this scoped justification (unmatched comparison, infeasible candidate, inadmissible risk/burden or a policy that rejects the candidate), return FAIL with that reason. This does not prove every differently scoped candidate claim false.

Otherwise distinguish the feasibility-remediation route from the feasible-options comparative-benefit route; account for relevant uncertainty and cheaper alternatives. Give PASS only if sufficient evidence establishes a permitted justification under the declared policy; missing decisive evidence or an unresolved tradeoff remains UNKNOWN.
Return the outcome, decisive evidence, declared scope and remaining uncertainty. Do not convert a mathematical construction into an observed external benefit.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Matched evidence establishes that the candidate meets applicable hard constraints and risk/burden limits and is justified over the comparator by the predeclared policy. This can be remediation of consequential baseline inadequacy or a warranted net benefit when both are adequate; hard-tolerance failure is not necessary for the latter route.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A decisive known condition defeats this scoped justification: task/access is not matched as claimed, candidate feasibility or risk/burden limits fail, or the declared comparison policy does not justify the added complexity. This includes a cost-dominated/no-consequential-gain choice or an adequate cheaper baseline preferred by pure satisficing.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed, fixed-contract example: for x uniform on {-1,0,1} and y=x², the best affine predictor2/3 has expected loss9 under loss(81/2)(prediction−y)²; the quadratic has loss0 and incremental lifecycle burden2. Both meet hard tolerance10, burden2 meets allowance3, and equal admissible risks are stipulated. A policy minimizing loss plus commensurate burden prefers totals2 over9. The same data under pure satisficing then minimum burden prefer the adequate baseline. These are mathematical controls, not an external cost-effectiveness trial; mixed published benchmarks retain their separate limited support.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: one-step prediction with frequent measured-output resets looks excellent, but the consumer needs a long free rollout that diverges.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: expressiveness, a smaller fit statistic, mismatched access, speculative reuse or undeclared exchange rates are mistaken for decision benefit. False negative: hard-tolerance satisfaction alone is used to prohibit a demonstrated net-beneficial choice under a policy valuing that improvement, or local adequacy hides relevant untested regimes. Neither error justifies universal nonlinear escalation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Nonlinear models are universally superior.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Reassess after regime, controller, horizon or consequence changes; retire complexity whose incremental benefit disappears.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Count experiment, fitting, validation, deployment, monitoring, maintenance and downstream burden over the stated horizon. A stable local linear/lookup model can remain the justified choice when its adequacy and the declared policy give no warranted advantage to added complexity. Adequacy alone does not prove that no policy-relevant net benefit exists.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: No extrapolation from local prediction to global simulation or mechanistic truth. Choosing the consequence function and obtaining rare-regime data remain judgment-dependent. The 2019 roadmap supplies methodological rationale; the 2026 baseline paper supplies mixed family rankings. Neither is a universal cost-effectiveness theorem.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Nonlinear representation complexity is justified by its declared use and operating regime — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.RULE: Each predicate decides its explicitly named proposition. Applicability, model truth, external warrant, retention and completion are separate axes. There is no default AND across alternatives or inherited variants.

POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE.witness: Executed saturation example: M(u)=u equals clip(u,-1,1) for tested u∈{-0.5,0,0.5}. This supports the bounded local behavior claim only.

NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE.witness: The same unchanged model has absolute error 1 at u=2. The changed premise is the operating envelope, not the serialized model.

NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE.witness: A small-signal linear model validated inside |u|≤0.5 need not be replaced merely because the physical device saturates outside the authorized envelope.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Unobserved mode, unknown observation map, or unreported initial-state estimate
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Input envelope, sensor map, sample interval, initialization or model change requires re-evaluation

PROFILE_REFERENCES.specific_dependence: Behavioral class, modes and per-regime validation

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.RECONCILIATION_VARIANT_POLICY: Whole original specifications have explicit primary owners. Related clauses can appear in another child only with the declared target allocation. Original variants remain exact ancestry; operative changes are separately recorded.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.RECONCILED_WORKED_DISCRIMINATOR: A saturation witness: yhat=u agrees with clip(u,-1,1) at tested -0.5,0,0.5; absolute error 1 at u=2. The changed premise is the allowed envelope. This is not a nonlinear family ranking.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: A more expressive nonlinear model can overfit, simulate unstably and remain observationally nonunique; linear residual acceptance is not enough.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: The same unchanged model has absolute error 1 at u=2. The changed premise is the operating envelope, not the serialized model.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Use structured simple models, appropriate nonlinear diagnostics and targeted validation before increasing complexity.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: Rare-regime loss and total benefit remain use-specific. Compare the actual cheap model and candidate at the receiving horizon with declared observation access.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: A nonlinear label or mandatory global model is ceremony when a bounded linear model already supports the consumer.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Purpose, regime, observation access and cheap alternatives determine adequacy; model size is not evidence. A evaluates bounded per-regime adequacy. B evaluates whether escalation from a baseline earns its cost. Adequacy and incremental justification are different predicates, both retained.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Hybrid-mode discrimination and theorem-specific switching access

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: A ECC 2007 tutorial and B EJC 2007 tutorial are distinct editions. Both distinguish switched ARX, jump-Markov and partition-defined PWA structures; no common hidden-state lineage is inferred.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: SARX; PWARX; jump-Markov; switching sequence; mode assignment
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: A fit of several local dynamics is not an identified hybrid system until the claimed mode assignments, transition or partition law, and relevant regime coverage are supported separately.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Latent clustering is mistaken for a physical mode ontology, or a theorem with observed switching is applied when modes are hidden or state-dependent.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Switched ARX, jump-Markov and piecewise-affine models differ in switching assumptions and require dynamics/mode/partition distinctions.
LOCATORS: Sections 1–3; switched ARX, jump-Markov and piecewise-affine model definitions
Continuous dynamics, mode assignment, partition and mode-count estimation distinction
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ACCESS_CEILING: Four representative approaches do not exhaust hybrid identification; mixed physics/neural models are a different use of hybrid.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM: The finite-sample theorem assumes measured iid switching, hidden continuous states and strong common quadratic stability, with recovery up to similarity.
LOCATORS: Section II; Assumption II.1
Main finite-sample result and similarity-transformation qualification
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ACCESS_CEILING: Switching signals are observed; continuous states are hidden. Bounded independent input/noise, iid modes and strong common quadratic contraction are essential. No unknown-switch theorem inferred.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM: The pick-and-place case contains saturation/impact modes that a naive smooth first-order model misses.
LOCATORS: Section 5 pick-and-place derivative-state expansion
Section 6/Table 2 Bouc–Wen structural/metric disagreement
Section 7/Table 3 cascaded tanks hidden state
Section 8 limitations
HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.ACCESS_CEILING: Results refute specific naive deployments, not every sparse or latent-state discovery method.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: Do not project current vocabulary or guarantees backward. FR004’s partially observed means hidden continuous state, not unobserved switching. Its recovered matrices are only up to similarity.

Recovery is up to similarity. Hidden or state-triggered switching falls outside this theorem.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: A claimed hybrid-mode distinction has discriminating observation evidence
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: ModeDistinction(F,S_required,observation,D,noise_bound)
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: F declared finite candidate switched/PWA models; S_required finite mode/transition set; inputs/outputs in declared physical units; noise_bound nonnegative in output units
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For each mode/transition distinction actually needed by the consumer, within the explicitly enumerated candidate family; label permutations are equivalent unless externally grounded
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: hybrid candidate models, observation map and mode-conditioned traces
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Finite distinction claim for current modes/partition and observation regime; no unbounded behavioral-equivalence guarantee
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Declared mode law (exogenous/Markov/partition), candidate family and error bound; observation protocol can expose the alleged distinction
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A mode identity, partition or regime-specific behavior is claimed from partial observations
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: PASS only for the declared finite candidate class when observations/allowed probes distinguish every decision-relevant nonequivalent candidate and required modes have evidence; FAIL a unique-distinction claim if an explicit pair remains observationally identical but differs on the required behavior; UNKNOWN for unvisited modes, unbounded candidate search or unreliable assignments; INAPPLICABLE when only undifferentiated output prediction is claimed.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.basis: ESI-RS0037 §§II–III; this is not a theorem of general hybrid identifiability

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Map measurements and inputs to candidate mode-dependent outputs with the declared noise tolerance; inferred mode labels are not treated as independently observed truth
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Candidate models, mode/partition definition including boundary assignment, observation/sensor map, required regimes and discriminating trace/probe records
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Compare predicted observation sets under allowed inputs, accounting for label permutation and error bound; mark unvisited or inseparable candidates explicitly
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite explicitly enumerated candidates can be compared on specified experiments; arbitrary hybrid model identification/equivalence is not solved by this assessment
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed noise-free alternatives y=u and y=2u are distinguishable at u=1 if these are the declared competing modes; their physical names still need external grounding
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: At u=0 those alternatives yield identical output; arbitrarily many repetitions there cannot identify the active mode. An unvisited mode can retain arbitrary dynamics.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown candidate set, mode assignment, sensor map, switching law or noise bound; missing required mode/transition evidence
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No mode/partition distinction is required; validate a bounded output predictor instead
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False distinction from noise or sensor drift; false failure if an external mode sensor already supplies the needed information but was omitted
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Treat inferred labels as ground truth for evaluating the same inference; split one mode into many labels to inflate apparent structure
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New mode, altered partition/switching logic, sensor mapping or required input domain invalidates the distinction evidence
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use known mode labels or a direct diagnostic sensor when cheaper; do not infer unused hidden distinctions
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Decision-relevant distinguishability within a declared finite family, not general unique hybrid realization

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Every invoked hypothesis is supported, and claimed mode/transition behaviors have appropriate evidence; only the selected theorem’s conclusion transfers.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A contradicted hypothesis exists, such as hidden or state-dependent switching when applying FR004’s observed iid-mode bound.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Mode labels, rare-transition evidence or a required stability/independence witness is absent.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No hybrid behavior or hybrid theorem is part of the model claim.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR004 supplies a conditional single-trajectory finite-sample theorem for observed switching and hidden continuous state.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed transfer failure: replace the measured iid mode sequence with a state-triggered unobserved guard while retaining the same confidence claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Mode labels, rare-transition evidence or a required stability/independence witness is absent.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No hybrid behavior or hybrid theorem is part of the model claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Latent clustering is mistaken for a physical mode ontology, or a theorem with observed switching is applied when modes are hidden or state-dependent. False negative: Mode boundaries may be unidentifiable from available outputs; separate checking can expose but not resolve that limitation.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: The consumer only needs calibrated sequence predictions and does not use latent labels.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_MECHANISM_AND_TARGET_DISTINCT: A contributes explicit HMM theorem premises and a rank-domain predicate. B contributes a semantic-correspondence predicate accepting either invariant predictions or independently anchored hidden quantities. Neither predicate replaces the other. The outer trigger is the union of the retained Hsu-invocation and latent-interpretation targets. Rank/positivity/sampling conditions are assessed as the named theorem warrant, and physical labels are not required to invoke that assessment.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_SHARED_CONTENT: Prediction of observations and physical interpretation of latent state are different targets; similarity or permutation leaves observable behavior unchanged.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: The Hsu spectral guarantee is being claimed, including by a purely predictive HMM without semantic labels, or hidden-state models, encoders or HMMs are given semantic labels. Unestablished or violated theorem premises do not suppress assessment of an invoked guarantee.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked and no hidden-state semantic interpretation is being assessed. Calibrated observable prediction can be an adequate cheap route without physical labels, but an invoked Hsu guarantee still requires its own theorem-warrant assessment.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Hsu Condition 1: positive initial probabilities and full column rank of emission O and transition T for m hidden states. Theorem 6 bounds fixed-horizon observation-sequence L1 error under sample/conditioning conditions and independent sequences; stronger conditional KL result needs additional positivity. Do not infer physical coordinates or single-long-trajectory guarantees. These are conditions for the invoked theorem warrant, not prerequisites to assess the invocation. Independent semantic anchors are required only for an interpretation that needs them.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: No unrestricted transfer from linear/HMM observability to arbitrary nonlinear or agent internals.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Hsu Condition 1: positive initial probabilities and full column rank of emission O and transition T for m hidden states. Theorem 6 bounds fixed-horizon observation-sequence L1 error under sample/conditioning conditions and independent sequences; stronger conditional KL result needs additional positivity. Do not infer physical coordinates or single-long-trajectory guarantees.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Research-derived acceptance rule, not an imposed obligation. No universal standard or target authority is asserted. Any domain-specific authority must be supplied separately.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record {predictive target, observation map, allowed state transformations, horizon, rank/conditioning, independent semantic anchors}. Preserve source/data/model versions and separate observed facts from assumptions.

Two admissible observationally equivalent realizations with different claimed meanings and no distinguishing evidence defeat the separately asserted unique-meaning claim.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Assess the warrant for the exact invoked theorem. PASS requires pi_i>0 for every i, rank(O)=rank(T)=m, and the cited theorem’s conditioning, independent-sequence, horizon/error/confidence and sample-size premises to be established. FAIL requires a known violation of a required premise; UNKNOWN means a material premise is unestablished. INAPPLICABLE only when no Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked. A failed invocation is not itself a counterexample to prediction accuracy.

STEPS: Activate on the claimed theorem, regardless of physical labels or success of its premises.
Bind the exact theorem/version, target/horizon and mathematical HMM separately from the evidential warrant for population and sampling premises.
Return the outcome for theorem-invocation warrant; evaluate predictive accuracy or physical meaning separately.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The exact invoked Hsu theorem is warranted for the specified HMM, horizon, error/confidence target and protocol: positive initial probabilities, required ranks, conditioning, independent-sequence sampling and sample-size premises are established.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An established violation of a required premise defeats this theorem-invocation warrant. This does not by itself prove the underlying predictive result false or establish physical hidden-state nonidentifiability for every other method.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A material population, sampling, conditioning or sample-size premise remains unestablished, so the invoked guarantee is not yet warranted.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked; use of another estimator is a non-trigger only when that guarantee is not claimed for it.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked; use of another estimator is a non-trigger only when that guarantee is not claimed for it.

records.title: Regularized inverse solutions, posterior stability and target identification

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Regularized inverse solutions, posterior stability and target identification

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Inverse problems and Bayesian analysis are imported concepts, not claimed to descend wholly from control identification. Hansen and Stuart address different formulations.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Tikhonov regularization; discrete ill-posed problem; nullspace
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Minimize data residual plus a weighted prior/smoothness penalty.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Small residuals can coexist with unstable or nonunique inverse solutions.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.SPECIFIC_CLAIM: Numerical inverse recovery stabilizes a selected solution using a regularizer.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: The original Tikhonov/Hadamard historical bodies were not examined. No claim that all system identification descends from this manual.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Distinguish existence, numerical stability, uniqueness of a regularized solution, well-posed posterior inference and identification of the external target; regularization or a prior may select a useful answer without adding distinguishing observations.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: An inverse problem, regularizer and target claim
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: A unique smooth/minimum-norm optimizer is called the uniquely recovered physical object.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Expose the feasible data-equivalence class and the complete optimization problem, including domain, A, L, center and parameter; separate full-space rank reasoning from constrained existence/uniqueness and from physical target identification.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Distinguish existence, numerical stability, uniqueness of a regularized solution, well-posed posterior inference and identification of the external target; regularization or a prior may select a useful answer without adding distinguishing observations.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Stable numerical estimates without concealing what the data alone cannot determine.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Manual examples show numerical behavior, not an independently validated field payoff or universal error reduction. Hansen Eq.(2.39) gives unconstrained stacked least squares. For fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0 on R^n, the kernel-intersection iff follows by finite linear algebra. Feasible-class identifiability and the CASE-B003 constrained-domain discriminators are separate constructed arguments.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Which inverse estimate or range can support a physical conclusion or downstream action.
ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Use a target functional constant on the nullspace
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_MECHANISM_AND_TARGET_DISTINCT: A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_SHARED_CONTENT: A unique selected solution does not establish unique physical recovery. A target functional may already be identified although the full unknown vector is not.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Forward-map inversion is ill-conditioned, rank-deficient or prior-dependent.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If the consumer needs only x1+x2 and A=[1,1], that sum is identified; no unique x vector or elaborate regularizer is needed.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: For fixed finite A,L,b,x*, lambda>0 and domain R^n, the unconstrained Tikhonov minimizer is unique iff ker(A) intersects ker(L) only at zero. Constrained domains require separate existence/uniqueness arguments. Target q must be constant on a nonempty feasible class. Bayesian results retain prior, likelihood/potential and regularity assumptions; no automatic frequentist coverage.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Mathematical inverse solution versus the real object and the chosen target functional.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: For fixed finite A,L,b,x*, lambda>0 and domain R^n, the unconstrained Tikhonov minimizer is unique iff ker(A) intersects ker(L) only at zero. Constrained domains require separate existence/uniqueness arguments. Target q must be constant on a nonempty feasible class. Bayesian results retain prior, likelihood/potential and regularity assumptions; no automatic frequentist coverage.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record the exact objective and admissible domain, operator discretization, units/scaling, noise covariance, fixed penalty/center, λ-selection and tuning data; identify any separate constrained existence/uniqueness argument.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: Connects C0105 sparse priors, C0107 projection and C0109 known-physics inverse fitting; tension between stability and bias.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: A wrong penalty can stabilize the wrong answer; near-null directions remain practically unidentifiable.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Inspect nullspace/target first; a direct sum measurement avoids recovering every component
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Operator, noise regime, units, regularizer or requested target changes require a fresh sensitivity/equivalence assessment.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RECONCILED_COMPOSITION_CONSEQUENCE: FR06 causal action requires additional structural/intervention premises. FR17 physics priors do not cure inverse nonuniqueness. Root uncertainty rows preserve posterior versus feasible-set semantics.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: UniqueReg(A,L,lambda,b,x_star,D) and Identified(q,A,b,D)
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: A∈R^(m×n); L∈R^(p×n); b∈R^m; x,x*∈R^n; λ>0 with declared scaling; D⊆R^n; q has declared target units. The kernel iff test has guard D=R^n.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, minimizing J(x)=||Ax-b||²+λ²||L(x-x*)||² over all x∈R^n has a unique minimizer iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}. Do not extend that iff to arbitrary D. Separately, for nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b}, the target is identified iff q(x)=q(x′) for every x,x′∈F_b.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: specified finite linear inverse model
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Static claims for a fixed objective, observation equation, center and admissible domain; full-space and constrained optimization are distinct cases
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Finite real linear A,L, fixed b and center x*, fixed λ>0. The source stacked least-squares uniqueness test is restricted to unconstrained R^n; constrained D requires its own existence/uniqueness warrant. Target identification uses the declared nonempty feasible class and observation/noise interpretation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A linear regularized inverse claim is made
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Report optimization uniqueness and target identification separately. For D=R^n and fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, PASS uniqueness iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}; otherwise FAIL uniqueness. For constrained D, the full-space iff shortcut is INAPPLICABLE: use a separate domain-appropriate existence and uniqueness argument, with UNKNOWN when that argument is missing or unresolved. Separately PASS target identification only if nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b} has constant q; FAIL if an explicit feasible equal-data pair has unequal q; UNKNOWN if the operator, domain, nonemptiness or equivalence class is unresolved. Forward prediction without an inverse target is INAPPLICABLE.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.source: ESI-RS0039 §2.7.1 Eq.(2.39) supplies unconstrained stacked least squares and a sufficient rank condition; the full-space iff and feasible-class target test are elementary linear-algebra reconstructions

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: A maps physical parameter units to observations; q specifies the desired reported quantity
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A,L,λ,b, fixed center x*, exact objective, admissible domain D, target q and noise/precision statement; a separate constrained existence/uniqueness argument when D≠R^n
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: First identify D and fixed objective data. Apply the full-space kernel-intersection iff only on R^n; for constrained D assess existence and uniqueness with its own argument. Independently establish the nonempty feasible data class and q constancy; report the two conclusions separately.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The full-space rank test is finite linear algebra. General constrained existence/uniqueness and nonlinear target constancy require separate proofs or bounded analysis and may remain UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: For A=[1,1], q(x)=x1+x2 is constant across exact-data solutions; this target is identified
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: For A=[1,1], b=1, the feasible vectors (1,0),(0,1),(.5,.5) fit equally; minimum norm selects (.5,.5) without identifying x1. Existing CASE-B003 also contains two analytical-only constrained-domain discriminators for misuse of the full-space iff.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown operator/domain or feasible-class nonemptiness; unresolved constrained existence/uniqueness; noise tolerance without a declared compatible uncertainty set
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The full-space uniqueness shortcut is inapplicable when D≠R^n, while feasible-class target identification can still apply. The whole inverse-target assessment is inapplicable to forward prediction without an inverse claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False unique claim from rank tolerance or applying the full-space test to a nonconvex domain; false rejection of a unique constrained minimizer or an identified target functional
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Reporting narrow optimizer curvature as total physical uncertainty
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changes in A,L,b,λ,center x*,domain D,units,noise or q require reassessing the corresponding optimization or identification claim
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Inspect nullspace/target first; a direct sum measurement avoids recovering every component
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Uniqueness/stability within the specified inverse problem, not proof that the regularizer or forward model describes nature
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The stated mathematical property follows under verified assumptions, and any uniqueness claim is explicitly qualified or independently supported.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A stable regularized solution is claimed to prove uniqueness despite an exhibited observational nullspace or equivalent alternative.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR006’s Hellinger-continuity result supports stability of a conditional posterior under its hypotheses.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: y=theta1+theta2; a quadratic penalty selects a unique minimum, while infinitely many parameter pairs fit the same noise-free observation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Regularization-induced selection or posterior concentration is mistaken for data-determined uniqueness. False negative: Priors encode legitimate knowledge and can make an otherwise underdetermined decision useful.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. A well-posed posterior proves the true physical parameter is uniquely identified.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed forward model, prior, noise model, discretization or target quantity requires renewed analysis.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Posterior computation and prior-sensitivity studies; infinite-dimensional discretization control can be substantial. Cheaper path: A directly observed, well-conditioned quantity can be estimated with a transparent low-dimensional model.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Bayesian well-posedness does not itself validate the prior, likelihood, solver or physical forward model. Misspecified model classes can yield stable but wrong answers. FR006 proves posterior well-posedness and approximation results under stated hypotheses, not universal parameter recovery.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Inverse-problem well-posedness and regularization are distinct from unique external recovery — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.RECONCILED_WORKED_DISCRIMINATOR: A=[1,1], b=1 identifies the sum, not the vector; minimum norm chooses (1/2,1/2). A constrained line can remove a flat direction, while a nonconvex two-point domain can retain two minimizers despite full-space kernel triviality. Those latter constructions are analytical, not newly executed here.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Regularization can create persuasive precision by encoding an incorrect prior; small residuals and unique optima do not settle physical ambiguity.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: The same data admit (1,0),(0,1) and (.5,.5); choosing the minimum-norm vector cannot establish which physical vector generated them.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Disclose the prior and distinguish target functionals; vary the penalty/noise assumptions and collect a discriminating measurement if uniqueness matters.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: External model class and noise/prior correspondence can remain unknown. Seek a measurement outside the present nullspace or conduct prior/forward-model sensitivity for the actual target.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: Demanding a unique full reconstruction when only a measured functional is needed adds avoidable machinery.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: A unique selected solution does not establish unique physical recovery. A target functional may already be identified although the full unknown vector is not. A supplies finite deterministic Tikhonov/nullspace criteria. B supplies Bayesian posterior existence, Hellinger stability and approximation. These are complementary native claims and preserve different spaces, metrics and uncertainty meanings.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.justification_and_limit: Regularization can create persuasive precision by encoding an incorrect prior; small residuals and unique optima do not settle physical ambiguity.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.justification_and_limit: Known forward operator and observation/noise interpretation. For a constrained admissible domain D, establish existence and uniqueness by a separate domain-appropriate argument. Target identifiability is assessed on feasible data-equivalence classes within D.

UNCERTAINTY_CALIBRATION.justification_and_limit: Optimizer stability alone does not calibrate truth uncertainty.

records.title: Predictive equivalence versus intervention identification

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Predictive equivalence versus intervention identification

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Pearl1995 causal diagrams and Pearl2009 overview are distinct works. ICP and ObsNODE are qualified adjacent developments; analytical correspondence does not establish direct historical influence.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: do-intervention; causal identification; invariant prediction; observable normal form
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: An intervention replaces a structural equation; an estimand is identified if all observationally compatible allowed models agree on it.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: A predictor valid under one data-generating policy can fail under intervention or changed confounding.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.SPECIFIC_CLAIM: Identification is a model-class property of a causal estimand.
Invariant prediction gains a causal interpretation under structural intervention assumptions.
Observable normal form is explicitly combined with causal adjustment in a 2026 preprint.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: Pearl’s historical overview is not primary verification of all econometric origins. ObsNODE is a recent, unreplicated preprint and not the first connection between dynamics and causality.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: An intervention functional is identified only when admissible causal models consistent with the evidence agree on that functional; predictive fit under an observed policy does not itself supply this agreement.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A predictive dynamic model used for an intervention estimand
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Correlation, fit, state observability or invariant residuals are treated as sufficient proof of causal effects.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Define intervention semantics and the admissible causal model class; seek observationally equivalent models with different effects; use justified interventions, exclusions or adjustment conditions to remove that ambiguity.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: An intervention functional is identified only when admissible causal models consistent with the evidence agree on that functional; predictive fit under an observed policy does not itself supply this agreement.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Prevent a policy change from exploiting a spurious predictive association while permitting justified intervention prediction.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: The inspected sources contain method demonstrations; no universal transfer from predictive performance to intervention accuracy is established. Pearl defines identification; ICP Theorem 1 controls false positive inclusion under valid tests; ObsNODE Theorem 4.3 is an assumption-heavy preprint causal-adjustment result.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Whether to forecast the effect of an action rather than merely the next observed value.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_MECHANISM_AND_TARGET_DISTINCT: A adds ICP false-inclusion control and the 2026 observable-neural causal hybrid. B develops earlier structural-equation semantics and explicit controlled-input alternatives. Preserve these routes without equating architectural observability to identified causal parameters.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_SHARED_CONTENT: Observation and intervention have different semantics. A bounded predictor need not reconstruct an entire causal graph when no action/transport claim is made.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: The consumer changes an input/policy/mechanism or asks a counterfactual/causal question.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If the consumer only predicts observations under the same supported policy, a causal graph is not mandatory; label the claim predictive.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Define the intervention, model class, population/horizon, observation map and needed consistency, overlap, confounding/invariance or controlled-input premises. ICP can return an empty selected set while honoring its coverage; it does not promise all true parents.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Specified causal estimand in specified population/regime; prediction of observed outcomes is a different evidential target.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Define the intervention, model class, population/horizon, observation map and needed consistency, overlap, confounding/invariance or controlled-input premises. ICP can return an empty selected set while honoring its coverage; it does not promise all true parents.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record who/what assigned inputs, temporal order, measured confounders, hidden-state assumptions, intervention targets and environment-selection process.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: C0102 state reconstruction, C0111 evaluation and C0112 guarantee transfer are prerequisites only when their actual assumptions are met; none substitutes for causal identification.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Hidden confounding, target interventions that break invariance or lack of overlap can invalidate effect predictions despite good fit.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Use a predictive label when sufficient; collect the smallest permitted intervention distinguishing the disputed effect
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Changed policy, target population, intervention mechanism, observation history or confounding assumptions requires renewed identification analysis.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RECONCILED_COMPOSITION_CONSEQUENCE: FR22 forcing does not become manipulable/exogenous by being predictive; FR23 external agent behavior does not identify hidden intentions. Root control uses may obtain the necessary evidence by controlled inputs without compulsory causal-graph reconstruction.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Observed law is linked to measured variables and sampling policy; intervention replaces the designated mechanism
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Causal graph/equations or equivalent identification restrictions, observation policy, target and any intervention/environment evidence
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Search for an equivalent pair or apply a theorem with its assumptions stated; keep causal identification separate from statistical estimation
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Decidable for some finite graph classes; unrestricted nonlinear classes generally need expert reasoning and may remain UNKNOWN
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Under a valid randomized input and sufficient support, the outcome law conditional on assigned input can identify the specified intervention effect
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Executed pair X=Z,Y=X versus X=Z,Y=Z has identical X=Y observations but E[Y|do(X=1)] equals 1 versus 0
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown confounding, invalid exclusions, no overlap or uncertain intervention semantics
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No causal/intervention claim
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False pass from treating predictive tests as causal tests; false fail if adequate intervention evidence was omitted from the model class
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Empty ICP selected set has valid false-positive control yet can be presented as full discovery; clinical forecast accuracy can be mislabeled causal accuracy
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Policy, latent disturbance process, target intervention, population or sensor history changes invalidate the corresponding assumptions
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use a predictive label when sufficient; collect the smallest permitted intervention distinguishing the disputed effect
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Identified causal functional conditional on justified assumptions; neither finite-sample accuracy nor real-world causal truth follows from fit alone
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Causal target is invariant across compatible models
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Predictive identification does not by itself identify interventions or policy transport — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: InterventionClaimIdentified(model, intervention, assumptions, evidence)
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Intervention and probability expressions plus physical actions/units. Attribute ESI-RAT0130 supplies the structured arguments.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. Not all control models need a causal graph; known controlled inputs and physical mechanisms can supply different identification arguments.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A proposed interventional prediction or policy-change decision
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Structural invariances, intervention definition and relevant confounding/measurement assumptions must be defended.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A fitted model is used to change inputs/policies, explain causes or extrapolate to a changed environment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Determine whether all models admitted by the data and defended assumptions agree on the intervention target; otherwise report the remaining set or withhold the point claim.

OUTCOMES.PASS: An applicable identification argument or appropriate intervention evidence establishes the target within a stated scope.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: Admissible models agree observationally but disagree on the proposed intervention, while the result is presented as uniquely identified.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Required confounding/invariance assumptions or intervention evidence cannot be assessed.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: The claim is restricted to same-policy prediction and makes no causal or intervention assertion.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: A randomized input intervention with known assignment and appropriate measurement can distinguish response mechanisms that passive observations cannot.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed binary example: X=U,Y=X and X=U,Y=U have identical observed X=Y, but do(X=1) yields Y=1 in the first and Y=U in the second.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Required confounding/invariance assumptions or intervention evidence cannot be assessed.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The claim is restricted to same-policy prediction and makes no causal or intervention assertion.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Association under the training policy is treated as an invariant response to an externally changed action. False negative: Useful engineering interventions can be justified with physical structure without estimating every causal relation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Predictive fit demonstrates causality.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Policy, selection, mechanism or confounding changes reopen the transport claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Interventions can be costly or unsafe; observational adjustment requires substantive domain knowledge. Cheaper path: Prediction under the same validated policy and distribution does not need a full causal explanation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Not all control models need a causal graph; known controlled inputs and physical mechanisms can supply different identification arguments. Transport to new environments adds invariance obligations beyond within-environment identification. FR007 provides intervention semantics and graphical identification machinery; the discriminator here is an explicit analytic construction, not a field study.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Predictive identification does not by itself identify interventions or policy transport — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Sparse dynamics recovery within coordinates, library and informative observations

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: SINDy combines sparse regression with nonlinear function libraries; it does not originate every sparse approximation tradition. Its original paper includes coordinate/library failure discussion.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: SINDy; candidate library; weak residual; generalized least squares
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Solve derivative regression Xdot≈Theta(X)Xi under sparse coefficients; weak formulations integrate against test functions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Dense equation search, derivative noise and uninformative trajectories obscure a parsimonious dynamic model.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.SPECIFIC_CLAIM: Sparse equation coefficients are learned in a declared feature library.
Weak residual construction explicitly extends SINDy and earlier integral approaches.

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: Sparse regression and weak forms predate SINDy/WSINDy; original papers do not justify claiming invention of those mathematical traditions.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Interpret sparse coefficient recovery relative to a specified coordinate map, function library, sufficient observed state, numerical error model and informative trajectories; test any structural claim on discriminating regimes.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: Sparse dynamic model selection from observed trajectories
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: A concise fitted equation is called the law despite missing features, transformed coordinates, unobserved state or manifold-confined data.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Declare basis and coordinate units, assess informative variation, test off-training trajectories, and use weak residuals when derivative estimation dominates noise.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Interpret sparse coefficient recovery relative to a specified coordinate map, function library, sufficient observed state, numerical error model and informative trajectories; test any structural claim on discriminating regimes.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Obtain interpretable compact models when the system is sparse in an appropriate representation and the data distinguish terms.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: SINDy demonstrates selected dynamical examples and reports failures. Accessed WSINDy v3 gives ODE demonstrations but explicitly defers direct computational comparison with conventional SINDy. Weak identity follows integration by parts and source test-function assumptions; numerical quadrature and noisy nonlinear features still limit estimation.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Whether a selected equation supports prediction, interpretation or a designed experiment.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_MECHANISM_AND_TARGET_DISTINCT: A105 sparse-recovery component maps here; its weak-form numerical mechanism maps FR08. B adds hard-nonlinearity/hidden-state benchmarks and corrects the claim that linear-in-coefficient regression cannot represent products: a product can be a dictionary column. A sparse prediction or structural claim activates assessment before state/library sufficiency is established. The prediction and structural-warrant targets retain separate outcomes; an unknown premise affects only the claim that needs it, and a known structural counterexample cannot become INAPPLICABLE.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.RECONCILED_SHARED_CONTENT: Sparsity is representation-dependent, and more data on an uninformative manifold cannot determine missing terms or hidden dynamics.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A selected sparse equation is claimed to explain or predict dynamics, including a physical or structural interpretation, whether observed-state sufficiency, library adequacy or numerical premises are established, unknown or contradicted.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Only a known fixed law is fitted directly, with no selected sparse explanation, prediction or discovery claim to assess. A fitted predictor without structural interpretation removes only the structural target; a claimed selected sparse predictor still receives its bounded validation assessment.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Keep feature/coefficient units, rank and scaling, derivative/integral error, initial states and sampled transients. For structural recovery, justify sufficient observed state, library representability at the claimed accuracy and distinguishing data. For bounded prediction, assess the observation, numerical and held-out criteria material to that declared envelope. These are warrant/outcome conditions, not invocation gates; identifiability in one library is not all-library or all-coordinate uniqueness.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Equation recovery within a representation/envelope; this can be an effective reduced law rather than a unique physical law.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Keep feature/coefficient units, rank and scaling, derivative/integral error, initial states and sampled transients. Identifiability of one selected library is not all-library or all-coordinate uniqueness.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No external normative authority asserted. Mathematical claims are conditional; proposed acceptance procedures need a consumer-defined tolerance.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Store coordinate transform, units, dictionary terms, derivative/test functions, quadrature, thresholds, trajectory/initial-condition provenance and selection/validation separation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: C0103 regularization, C0106 dictionary validation and C0111 independent evaluation interact; more library terms can reduce conditioning.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: An actual omitted-state/library counterexample that contradicts the advertised structure or required trajectory yields FAIL of that claim. An unproved or violated merely sufficient proof premise alone leaves the underlying claim UNKNOWN unless the evaluated target is explicitly that premise or warrant. A failed structural warrant does not automatically negate a directly checked bounded predictive result.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Use known-family estimation first when justified; weak integration trades derivative noise for quadrature/test-function design
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Changed dictionary, coordinates, sensing, sample rate or target transient/regime requires support selection and validation to be reconsidered.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RECONCILED_COMPOSITION_CONSEQUENCE: FR04 state correspondence and FR08 weak numerical control are independent premises for a structural conclusion. FR09 rejects promotion of the resulting sparse fit to unique law.
