predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For finite T, evaluate exactly ∀t∈T:φ(a(t)) on the declared applicable observations, retaining extraction, missingness and denominator. For a broader D, evaluate ∀x∈D:φ(x), or the explicitly conditional proposition H⇒φ in the stated model M, without changing the target. A sound proof or analysis must cover that exact domain and semantics. Finite support alone does not establish the broader claim; explicitly empty T yields only vacuous finite consistency and no evidence of broader validity.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: Only instrumented values/events and executed conditions initially support the candidate; unexecuted paths remain open.
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Finite observed executions first; universal “always” only with an additional proof in a stated program model.
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Candidate language, program points, trace/test generation, missingness and statistical/filter choices must be adequate for the asserted scope. Broader proof claims retain their model, premises and applicability obligations. Unresolved premises affect the verdict rather than cancelling the truth-claim guard.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A truth or bounded-support claim for an inferred candidate φ is asserted, relied upon, or expressly assessed over a declared finite trace set T or a broader declared domain D. A claim confined to T suffices; extrapolation beyond T is not required. Missing evidence or unresolved premises do not by themselves make this guard false.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: First identify the candidate truth claim and its declared T or D. For finite T, PASS exactly when every declared applicable observation is interpretable and satisfies φ under the stated extraction map; explicitly empty T establishes only the vacuous finite statement. For a broader D, PASS only with a sound proof or analysis covering the exact claim and its premises; a conditional theorem establishes only its stated conditional target unless applicability of its premises to the receiving subject is established. FAIL when a reliable in-domain witness falsifies that exact candidate claim. Missing observations, ambiguous semantics, inconclusive proof, timeout, or an unestablished or invalidated proof premise yield UNKNOWN in the absence of a reliable in-domain falsifier; loss of a proof warrant alone does not prove ¬φ. INAPPLICABLE only when no candidate truth/support claim is asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed. Evaluate truthful reporting separately; its PASS neither proves φ nor overrides φ’s FAIL or UNKNOWN.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: Native set/conditional-conformance structure where identified; application guards and four-valued verdict discipline are this research’s operational reconstruction.

OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Inspect templates, trace extraction and filter settings.
Re-evaluate candidate on traces with explicit missingness; record where static/proof checks add scope.
REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: The exact candidate φ, asserted or assessed finite T or broader D, extraction map a, program points, versions and applicable observation boundaries.
All relevant support and falsifier records with missingness, selection/filter settings and denominators; a reliable in-domain counterexample may decide FAIL without establishing every other premise.
For a broader claim, a sound proof/analysis tied to the declared model and explicit premises; distinguish a proved conditional theorem from applicability of its premises to the receiving subject.
Observed regularity is descriptive. Intended requirements and acceptability require the separate normative-adoption basis of ESI-RC-BH10.
predicates.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Select the candidate truth claim and its exact finite T or broader D before evaluating. Check reliable in-domain falsifiers and declared observation/proof coverage. Return finite-T PASS only for that set, broader PASS only for a valid scope-matching argument, FAIL only for an actual falsifier of the exact target, and UNKNOWN for unresolved warrant without such a falsifier. Do not turn a missing premise into INAPPLICABLE or a failed proof into ¬φ. Assess the report of this result separately.
predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Checking a predicate on a finite trace set is decidable when its predicates are executable. Universal program invariance is not generally decided by dynamic inference.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.DESCRIPTION: EMPIRICAL BH006: candidate templates are eliminated by observed counterexamples and surviving statements are labeled likely. Constructed finite-domain discriminator: φ is x>0 and explicitly declared T contains x=2 and x=3 with reliable extraction; ∀t∈T φ(t) PASSes without any claim beyond T.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.DESCRIPTION: EMPIRICAL/EXAMPLE BH006: a test-suite-induced array-length range does not characterize all legal inputs. Constructed truth discriminator: φ is x>0 over declared T containing x=0; candidate truth FAILs even when the report faithfully says REFUTED. A proof-premise violation without such an in-domain falsifier leaves truth UNKNOWN.

predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: A truth/support claim applies, but observations, semantics, proof warrant, premise applicability or coverage are unresolved and no reliable in-domain falsifier is available. An invalidated premise defeats that proof warrant without by itself refuting φ. Explicit unknown premises are UNKNOWN for the affected truth claim, not INAPPLICABLE; a conditional theorem retains only its exact conditional scope.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No candidate truth/support claim over finite T or broader D is asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed. A status-only report or uninterpreted stored proposal can leave this predicate INAPPLICABLE even if reporting fidelity is assessed.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: Vacuous preconditions, rare-event filtering and selecting tests after seeing the candidate can inflate support.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Vacuous preconditions, rare-event filtering and selecting tests after seeing the candidate can inflate support. A checker/diagram/oracle interface existing is never itself the property witness.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Invalidate candidate support after code/instrumentation/test-distribution change; retain counterexamples and versions.

COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE.COST: Instrumentation, executions, candidate explosion, spurious-rule triage and proof/review effort.

predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Finite observed support plus specific additional proofs/cases; empirical frequency is not a universal quantifier.

EVALUATION_SEMANTICS.PASS: The exact finite-T statement holds on every declared applicable observation with adequate interpretation, or the exact broader/conditional statement has a sound proof or analysis with the required premises and scope. Finite-T PASS does not establish a broader D or normative requirement.
EVALUATION_SEMANTICS.FAIL: A reliable witness within declared T or D falsifies the exact candidate truth claim. For an H⇒φ target, the witness must satisfy H and falsify φ. An invalidated proof premise alone is not such a witness.
EVALUATION_SEMANTICS.UNKNOWN: The candidate truth claim applies but relevant observations, semantics, domain coverage, proof warrant or premise applicability are unresolved, and no reliable in-domain falsifier decides it. A failed proof or timeout is not candidate falsity.
EVALUATION_SEMANTICS.INAPPLICABLE: No candidate truth/support claim over T or D is asserted, relied upon or expressly assessed; a stored proposal or status-only report without an underlying truth claim does not trigger this predicate.

PASS when the stated decision and supported coverage, omission assessment, value or applicable scoped mandate justify that particular claim; a justified scoped graph or cheaper replacement remains applicable and can PASS. predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: a dependency decision concerns one module. The proposed graph states that boundary, includes the decision-relevant relations, exposes exclusions and has current witnesses supporting the claimed coverage and use. Its scoped adequacy claim is PASS. A justified scoped edge table proposed to replace an unnecessary whole-system graph can likewise PASS while that replacement claim is being assessed.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: a report asserts that its architecture graph contains every deployment dependency, but a witnessed active plugin dependency is omitted. predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Local comparative effects, not all protocols/languages or intended behavior validity. The operational review is evidence-bounded; it must not claim a complete decision procedure beyond the selected model/theorem.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: a fixed task suite, outcome criterion and total resource budget are declared. An independent held-out check accepts more non-vacuous useful candidates from the assisted pipeline than from the relevant baseline, and all failed attempts and material costs remain in the comparison. A claim confined to that evidenced suite, metric and budget is PASS.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: a pipeline claims lower total cost for producing the same required exact model, but a matched comparison establishes that the classical method produces that model at lower total cost than the LLM pipeline. The asserted cost advantage is FAIL, not INAPPLICABLE. A separate failure occurs when higher verifier-pass rate is obtained by deleting meaningful postconditions while claiming better specification adequacy.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: A comparative-benefit claim is present, but an adequate comparator, independent outcome evidence, complete attempt denominator, relevant resource accounting or uncertainty assessment is absent or inconclusive. The result is UNKNOWN even if a proposal bottleneck has not been established. An established contrary comparison is FAIL.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No comparative-benefit claim about LLM assistance is made or relied on. Merely choosing a classical method, or discovering that it is cheaper, does not make an asserted LLM-benefit claim inapplicable.

FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS.FALSE_POSITIVE: Favourable benchmark, training overlap, proxy coverage and un reported cost can create apparent benefit.

predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Optimizing an empty contract or response-code count avoids the intended consumer benefit.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New models, prompts, tool versions, protocol families or budgets require re-evaluation.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Include prompting/tokens, latency, solver execution, harness setup and rejected outputs, not only successful call counts. Cheaper route: Use a classical learner/fuzzer, hand-selected example, direct assertion or static template when adequate. If such a route is an evidenced comparator that contradicts an asserted LLM advantage, the comparative claim is FAIL. If the comparison is not yet established, it is UNKNOWN. INAPPLICABLE requires absence of the comparative claim/use, not a cheap alternative.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Local comparative effects, not all protocols/languages or intended behavior validity.

predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Within a fixed use envelope and matched observation access, establish candidate feasibility and adherence to the declared risk/burden limits. Then determine whether the predeclared consumer policy warrants replacing the comparator. A consequential baseline tolerance failure remedied by the candidate can establish the feasibility route. When both are feasible, a warranted policy-relevant improvement after lifecycle burden can establish a net-benefit route. Under pure satisficing followed by minimum burden, an adequate cheaper baseline remains preferred. A merely smaller fit statistic, an unranked tradeoff or an invented cost exchange rate does not establish justification.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.

Use evidence appropriate to the claim: matched held-out trajectories for the stated empirical comparison, or an explicitly stipulated finite population/valid derivation for a mathematical construction. Account separately for lifecycle burden, risk, coverage and uncertainty; a constructed comparison does not establish external plant performance.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {decision including predeclared preference/feasibility policy and tie rule, predicted quantities and units, horizon, admissible inputs/states, measured-output access, hard tolerances, cheap comparator, lifecycle costs, risk/burden limits and their evidence/uncertainty}. Supporting source links are property-level context; a deployed judgment requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Identify whether this is a nonlinear escalation/model-selection justification claim; if absent, use INAPPLICABLE.
Bind actual versions, same-use/access correspondence, predeclared policy, hard constraints and evidence classes. Do not create a preference or silently monetize hard constraints.

If a decisive known premise refutes this scoped justification (unmatched comparison, infeasible candidate, inadmissible risk/burden or a policy that rejects the candidate), return FAIL with that reason. This does not prove every differently scoped candidate claim false.

Otherwise distinguish the feasibility-remediation route from the feasible-options comparative-benefit route; account for relevant uncertainty and cheaper alternatives. Give PASS only if sufficient evidence establishes a permitted justification under the declared policy; missing decisive evidence or an unresolved tradeoff remains UNKNOWN.
Return the outcome, decisive evidence, declared scope and remaining uncertainty. Do not convert a mathematical construction into an observed external benefit.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Matched evidence establishes that the candidate meets applicable hard constraints and risk/burden limits and is justified over the comparator by the predeclared policy. This can be remediation of consequential baseline inadequacy or a warranted net benefit when both are adequate; hard-tolerance failure is not necessary for the latter route.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A decisive known condition defeats this scoped justification: task/access is not matched as claimed, candidate feasibility or risk/burden limits fail, or the declared comparison policy does not justify the added complexity. This includes a cost-dominated/no-consequential-gain choice or an adequate cheaper baseline preferred by pure satisficing.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed, fixed-contract example: for x uniform on {-1,0,1} and y=x², the best affine predictor2/3 has expected loss9 under loss(81/2)(prediction−y)²; the quadratic has loss0 and incremental lifecycle burden2. Both meet hard tolerance10, burden2 meets allowance3, and equal admissible risks are stipulated. A policy minimizing loss plus commensurate burden prefers totals2 over9. The same data under pure satisficing then minimum burden prefer the adequate baseline. These are mathematical controls, not an external cost-effectiveness trial; mixed published benchmarks retain their separate limited support.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: one-step prediction with frequent measured-output resets looks excellent, but the consumer needs a long free rollout that diverges.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: No decisive known refutation applies, but the decision policy, matched comparator, regime coverage, costs, risks or other decisive evidence is missing/unknown, or uncertainty/incomparable tradeoffs prevent the declared policy from deciding the justification.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No nonlinear escalation or model-selection justification decision is under consideration.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: expressiveness, a smaller fit statistic, mismatched access, speculative reuse or undeclared exchange rates are mistaken for decision benefit. False negative: hard-tolerance satisfaction alone is used to prohibit a demonstrated net-beneficial choice under a policy valuing that improvement, or local adequacy hides relevant untested regimes. Neither error justifies universal nonlinear escalation.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Nonlinear models are universally superior.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Reassess after regime, controller, horizon or consequence changes; retire complexity whose incremental benefit disappears.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Count experiment, fitting, validation, deployment, monitoring, maintenance and downstream burden over the stated horizon. A stable local linear/lookup model can remain the justified choice when its adequacy and the declared policy give no warranted advantage to added complexity. Adequacy alone does not prove that no policy-relevant net benefit exists.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: No extrapolation from local prediction to global simulation or mechanistic truth. Choosing the consequence function and obtaining rare-regime data remain judgment-dependent. The 2019 roadmap supplies methodological rationale; the 2026 baseline paper supplies mixed family rankings. predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed analytically: if y=(x+w)^2 with zero-mean w and variance sigma², E[y|x]=x²+sigma²; the variance term is represented rather than silently discarded.

predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: ModeDistinction(F,S_required,observation,D,noise_bound)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: F declared finite candidate switched/PWA models; S_required finite mode/transition set; inputs/outputs in declared physical units; noise_bound nonnegative in output units
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For each mode/transition distinction actually needed by the consumer, within the explicitly enumerated candidate family; label permutations are equivalent unless externally grounded
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: hybrid candidate models, observation map and mode-conditioned traces
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Finite distinction claim for current modes/partition and observation regime; no unbounded behavioral-equivalence guarantee
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Declared mode law (exogenous/Markov/partition), candidate family and error bound; observation protocol can expose the alleged distinction
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A mode identity, partition or regime-specific behavior is claimed from partial observations
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: PASS only for the declared finite candidate class when observations/allowed probes distinguish every decision-relevant nonequivalent candidate and required modes have evidence; FAIL a unique-distinction claim if an explicit pair remains observationally identical but differs on the required behavior; UNKNOWN for unvisited modes, unbounded candidate search or unreliable assignments; INAPPLICABLE when only undifferentiated output prediction is claimed.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Finite explicitly enumerated candidates can be compared on specified experiments; arbitrary hybrid model identification/equivalence is not solved by this assessment
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed noise-free alternatives y=u and y=2u are distinguishable at u=1 if these are the declared competing modes; their physical names still need external grounding
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: At u=0 those alternatives yield identical output; arbitrarily many repetitions there cannot identify the active mode. An unvisited mode can retain arbitrary dynamics.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown candidate set, mode assignment, sensor map, switching law or noise bound; missing required mode/transition evidence
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No mode/partition distinction is required; validate a bounded output predictor instead
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False distinction from noise or sensor drift; false failure if an external mode sensor already supplies the needed information but was omitted
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Treat inferred labels as ground truth for evaluating the same inference; split one mode into many labels to inflate apparent structure
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New mode, altered partition/switching logic, sensor mapping or required input domain invalidates the distinction evidence
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use known mode labels or a direct diagnostic sensor when cheaper; do not infer unused hidden distinctions
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Decision-relevant distinguishability within a declared finite family, not general unique hybrid realization
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: A claimed hybrid-mode distinction has discriminating observation evidence

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Hybrid identification separates dynamics, mode evidence and switching law assumptions — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: HybridGuaranteeApplicable(model, mode_log, theorem, evidence)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Categorical mode labels, matrices with physical units, probabilities in (0,1], and Boolean/unknown hypotheses. Attribute ESI-RAT0122 supplies the structured arguments.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. FR004’s partially observed means hidden continuous state, not unobserved switching. Its recovered matrices are only up to similarity.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A switched or hybrid model, including its mode variable and switching semantics
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: For FR004 specifically: observed iid modes with positive probabilities; bounded iid input/noise and required independences; minimal realization; common P>0 satisfying A_qᵀPA_q < (gamma²/n_Q²)P for gamma<1.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Operating regimes switch, saturation/impact occurs, or a finite-sample switched-model guarantee is invoked.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Conjoin the selected theorem’s explicit mode-observation, stochastic, rank/minimality and stability conditions; separately evaluate switching-law adequacy if that law is part of the intended claim.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Read the actual theorem; trace each hypothesis to experimental mode logs, excitation and stability evidence.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {mode observability, label semantics, mode count, switching law, within-mode data, transition coverage, realization equivalence, theorem hypotheses}. Supporting source links are attached at property level; a deployed judgment additionally requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: Every invoked hypothesis is supported, and claimed mode/transition behaviors have appropriate evidence; only the selected theorem’s conclusion transfers.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A contradicted hypothesis exists, such as hidden or state-dependent switching when applying FR004’s observed iid-mode bound.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Mode labels, rare-transition evidence or a required stability/independence witness is absent.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No hybrid behavior or hybrid theorem is part of the model claim.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR004 supplies a conditional single-trajectory finite-sample theorem for observed switching and hidden continuous state.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed transfer failure: replace the measured iid mode sequence with a state-triggered unobserved guard while retaining the same confidence claim.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Mode labels, rare-transition evidence or a required stability/independence witness is absent.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No hybrid behavior or hybrid theorem is part of the model claim.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Latent clustering is mistaken for a physical mode ontology, or a theorem with observed switching is applied when modes are hidden or state-dependent. False negative: Mode boundaries may be unidentifiable from available outputs; separate checking can expose but not resolve that limitation.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Partial observation means the switching signal may be missing.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New mode, changed switching policy, mode-label semantics or contraction violation invalidates the inherited guarantee.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Rare-mode experiments and switching-boundary coverage; joint mode/dynamics optimization can be combinatorial. Cheaper path: A single local model covers all visited regimes, or known mode labels permit independent fits without learned switching.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: FR004’s partially observed means hidden continuous state, not unobserved switching. Its recovered matrices are only up to similarity. Unknown mode count, hidden switching and safety-constrained exploration remain difficult. FR003 gives the structural distinctions; FR004 proves a finite-sample result only with measured iid switching and other explicit conditions.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Hybrid identification separates dynamics, mode evidence and switching law assumptions — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: HMM rank-conditioned guarantee is invoked within its domain
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: RankDomain(pi,O,T,m,sampling)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: pi probability vector; O,T dimensionless probability matrices; m hidden-state count; sampling protocol nominal
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: All m states under the specified HMM; Theorem 6 fixes horizon and error/confidence separately
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: mathematical HMM and data collection protocol
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: State of a model/protocol version; not future constancy of emissions
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Correct HMM family and observation alphabet
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: The Hsu spectral guarantee is being claimed, including for a purely predictive HMM without semantic labels. Unknown or violated premises remain assessable.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Assess the warrant for the exact invoked theorem. PASS requires pi_i>0 for every i, rank(O)=rank(T)=m, and the cited theorem’s conditioning, independent-sequence, horizon/error/confidence and sample-size premises to be established. FAIL requires a known violation of a required premise; UNKNOWN means a material premise is unestablished. INAPPLICABLE only when no Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked. A failed invocation is not itself a counterexample to prediction accuracy.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Observed sequence counts estimate observable moments; a fitted full-rank matrix alone does not certify population rank
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Model specification or justified parameter bounds, sampling/reset record, exact theorem target/horizon and sample size

STEPS: Activate on the claimed theorem, regardless of physical labels or success of its premises.
Bind the exact theorem/version, target/horizon and mathematical HMM separately from the evidential warrant for population and sampling premises.
Return the outcome for theorem-invocation warrant; evaluate predictive accuracy or physical meaning separately.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The exact invoked Hsu theorem is warranted for the specified HMM, horizon, error/confidence target and protocol: positive initial probabilities, required ranks, conditioning, independent-sequence sampling and sample-size premises are established.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An established violation of a required premise defeats this theorem-invocation warrant. This does not by itself prove the underlying predictive result false or establish physical hidden-state nonidentifiability for every other method.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A material population, sampling, conditioning or sample-size premise remains unestablished, so the invoked guarantee is not yet warranted.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked; use of another estimator is a non-trigger only when that guarantee is not claimed for it.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Exact specified matrices allow algebraic rank; finite noisy estimates require tolerance and cannot prove exact population rank
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: O=[[.9,.1],[.1,.9]] has determinant .8; a separately specified full-rank T and positive pi can satisfy the rank part
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Identical columns O=[[.5,.5],[.5,.5]] have determinant zero; hidden states are not separated by this observation map
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Population rank, initial probabilities, conditioning, sampling independence or sample-size/horizon conditions are unestablished. Known dependent sampling violates the cited independent-sequence warrant; undocumented sampling gives UNKNOWN.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No Hsu spectral guarantee is invoked; use of another estimator is a non-trigger only when that guarantee is not claimed for it.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False pass from roundoff or invented independence; false fail when a different learnable representation does not require this rank condition
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Calling all states identifiable because an optimizer returned m columns
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changing emission, transition, initial distribution, alphabet or hidden-state dimension invalidates theorem-domain check
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use observable prediction without physical labels when sufficient; add sensors only for a decision requiring the missing distinction
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conditional learning of observation-sequence distributions, not unique physical hidden-state recovery. A FAIL here is a failed theorem invocation, not proof that the predictor is inaccurate or that another representation cannot learn.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: THEOREM_INVOCATION_WARRANT: the invoked Hsu spectral guarantee is supported by its exact model, positivity, rank, conditioning, horizon and sampling premises.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Predictive latent realizations do not uniquely determine physical hidden-state meaning — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.

predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Symbolic transformation class and calibrated probability/error units. Attribute ESI-RAT0124 supplies the structured arguments.

predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Hidden-state models, encoders or HMMs are given semantic labels.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For a claimed latent meaning, test whether all observationally equivalent admissible realizations preserve that meaning; if not, require evidence that excludes the alternatives.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Derive invariance of output law and inspect independent state measurements or interventions.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {predictive target, observation map, allowed state transformations, horizon, rank/conditioning, independent semantic anchors}. Supporting source links are attached at property level; a deployed judgment additionally requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The claim is restricted to invariant predictive behavior, or independent anchors separate the interpretation-relevant alternatives.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: Two admissible observationally equivalent realizations have different claimed meanings and no distinguishing evidence is supplied.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: The equivalence class or available anchor reliability cannot be established.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: The model has no latent variables and no hidden-state interpretation is proposed.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR005’s observable-operator formulation learns sequence probabilities without requiring a physical name for every hidden coordinate.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: relabel the states of an HMM and permute transition/emission parameters; the output law is unchanged while an unanchored state name changes.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The equivalence class or available anchor reliability cannot be established.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The model has no latent variables and no hidden-state interpretation is proposed.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Prediction error is promoted into evidence that a latent coordinate equals a physical mechanism or internal state. False negative: Physical priors can break symmetries; the limitation should not be mistaken for impossibility under all additional information.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. An encoder has discovered the actual hidden physical state.

Unseen interventions can still distinguish models that agree under the observed policy. predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: UniqueReg(A,L,lambda,b,x_star,D) and Identified(q,A,b,D)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: A∈R^(m×n); L∈R^(p×n); b∈R^m; x,x*∈R^n; λ>0 with declared scaling; D⊆R^n; q has declared target units. The kernel iff test has guard D=R^n.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, minimizing J(x)=||Ax-b||²+λ²||L(x-x*)||² over all x∈R^n has a unique minimizer iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}. Do not extend that iff to arbitrary D. Separately, for nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b}, the target is identified iff q(x)=q(x′) for every x,x′∈F_b.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: specified finite linear inverse model
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Static claims for a fixed objective, observation equation, center and admissible domain; full-space and constrained optimization are distinct cases
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Finite real linear A,L, fixed b and center x*, fixed λ>0. The source stacked least-squares uniqueness test is restricted to unconstrained R^n; constrained D requires its own existence/uniqueness warrant. Target identification uses the declared nonempty feasible class and observation/noise interpretation.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A linear regularized inverse claim is made
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Report optimization uniqueness and target identification separately. For D=R^n and fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0, PASS uniqueness iff ker(A)∩ker(L)={0}; otherwise FAIL uniqueness. For constrained D, the full-space iff shortcut is INAPPLICABLE: use a separate domain-appropriate existence and uniqueness argument, with UNKNOWN when that argument is missing or unresolved. Separately PASS target identification only if nonempty F_b={x∈D:Ax=b} has constant q; FAIL if an explicit feasible equal-data pair has unequal q; UNKNOWN if the operator, domain, nonemptiness or equivalence class is unresolved. Forward prediction without an inverse target is INAPPLICABLE.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.source: ESI-RS0039 §2.7.1 Eq.(2.39) supplies unconstrained stacked least squares and a sufficient rank condition; the full-space iff and feasible-class target test are elementary linear-algebra reconstructions

predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: A maps physical parameter units to observations; q specifies the desired reported quantity
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: A,L,λ,b, fixed center x*, exact objective, admissible domain D, target q and noise/precision statement; a separate constrained existence/uniqueness argument when D≠R^n
predicates.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: First identify D and fixed objective data. Apply the full-space kernel-intersection iff only on R^n; for constrained D assess existence and uniqueness with its own argument. Independently establish the nonempty feasible data class and q constancy; report the two conclusions separately.
predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The full-space rank test is finite linear algebra. General constrained existence/uniqueness and nonlinear target constancy require separate proofs or bounded analysis and may remain UNKNOWN.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: For A=[1,1], q(x)=x1+x2 is constant across exact-data solutions; this target is identified
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: For A=[1,1], b=1, the feasible vectors (1,0),(0,1),(.5,.5) fit equally; minimum norm selects (.5,.5) without identifying x1. Existing CASE-B003 also contains two analytical-only constrained-domain discriminators for misuse of the full-space iff.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown operator/domain or feasible-class nonemptiness; unresolved constrained existence/uniqueness; noise tolerance without a declared compatible uncertainty set
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The full-space uniqueness shortcut is inapplicable when D≠R^n, while feasible-class target identification can still apply. The whole inverse-target assessment is inapplicable to forward prediction without an inverse claim.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False unique claim from rank tolerance or applying the full-space test to a nonconvex domain; false rejection of a unique constrained minimizer or an identified target functional
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Reporting narrow optimizer curvature as total physical uncertainty
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changes in A,L,b,λ,center x*,domain D,units,noise or q require reassessing the corresponding optimization or identification claim
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Inspect nullspace/target first; a direct sum measurement avoids recovering every component
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Uniqueness/stability within the specified inverse problem, not proof that the regularizer or forward model describes nature
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Penalized uniqueness is distinguished from target identifiability
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Inverse-problem well-posedness and regularization are distinct from unique external recovery — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: InverseClaimSupported(forward_model, prior, likelihood, claimed_property, evidence)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Function spaces, measures, Hellinger or specified norm; no universal dimensionless score. Attribute ESI-RAT0127 supplies the structured arguments.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. Bayesian well-posedness does not itself validate the prior, likelihood, solver or physical forward model.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: An inverse map or posterior over physical/dynamic unknowns

predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {forward map, data operator, observational equivalence, prior/penalty, topology/metric, posterior or solution, target functional}. Supporting source links are attached at property level; a deployed judgment additionally requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The stated mathematical property follows under verified assumptions, and any uniqueness claim is explicitly qualified or independently supported.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A stable regularized solution is claimed to prove uniqueness despite an exhibited observational nullspace or equivalent alternative.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR006’s Hellinger-continuity result supports stability of a conditional posterior under its hypotheses.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: y=theta1+theta2; a quadratic penalty selects a unique minimum, while infinitely many parameter pairs fit the same noise-free observation.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Forward-map hypotheses, prior sensitivity or approximation error are unverified.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No inverse-recovery or stability claim is being made.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Regularization-induced selection or posterior concentration is mistaken for data-determined uniqueness. False negative: Priors encode legitimate knowledge and can make an otherwise underdetermined decision useful.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. A well-posed posterior proves the true physical parameter is uniquely identified.

predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Posterior computation and prior-sensitivity studies; infinite-dimensional discretization control can be substantial. Cheaper path: A directly observed, well-conditioned quantity can be estimated with a transparent low-dimensional model.

FR006 proves posterior well-posedness and approximation results under stated hypotheses, not universal parameter recovery.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Inverse-problem well-posedness and regularization are distinct from unique external recovery — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Executed pair X=Z,Y=X versus X=Z,Y=Z has identical X=Y observations but E[Y|do(X=1)] equals 1 versus 0
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Unknown confounding, invalid exclusions, no overlap or uncertain intervention semantics
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No causal/intervention claim
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False pass from treating predictive tests as causal tests; false fail if adequate intervention evidence was omitted from the model class
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Empty ICP selected set has valid false-positive control yet can be presented as full discovery; clinical forecast accuracy can be mislabeled causal accuracy
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Policy, latent disturbance process, target intervention, population or sensor history changes invalidate the corresponding assumptions
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use a predictive label when sufficient; collect the smallest permitted intervention distinguishing the disputed effect
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Identified causal functional conditional on justified assumptions; neither finite-sample accuracy nor real-world causal truth follows from fit alone
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Causal target is invariant across compatible models
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Predictive identification does not by itself identify interventions or policy transport — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: InterventionClaimIdentified(model, intervention, assumptions, evidence)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Intervention and probability expressions plus physical actions/units. Attribute ESI-RAT0130 supplies the structured arguments.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. Not all control models need a causal graph; known controlled inputs and physical mechanisms can supply different identification arguments.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A proposed interventional prediction or policy-change decision
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Structural invariances, intervention definition and relevant confounding/measurement assumptions must be defended.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A fitted model is used to change inputs/policies, explain causes or extrapolate to a changed environment.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Determine whether all models admitted by the data and defended assumptions agree on the intervention target; otherwise report the remaining set or withhold the point claim.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Derive target distribution from structural assumptions or compare interventions held out from estimation.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {target intervention, changed mechanism, observed policy, causal/structural assumptions, adjustment or experiment, transport scope}. Supporting source links are attached at property level; a deployed judgment additionally requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Check applicability before substantive evaluation.
Bind the attribute record to actual versions and classify observed versus assumed components.
Apply the specific operational rule and inspect the stated counterexample class.
Return one outcome with the decisive evidence and remaining scope.

OUTCOMES.PASS: An applicable identification argument or appropriate intervention evidence establishes the target within a stated scope.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: Admissible models agree observationally but disagree on the proposed intervention, while the result is presented as uniquely identified.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Required confounding/invariance assumptions or intervention evidence cannot be assessed.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: The claim is restricted to same-policy prediction and makes no causal or intervention assertion.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: A randomized input intervention with known assignment and appropriate measurement can distinguish response mechanisms that passive observations cannot.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed binary example: X=U,Y=X and X=U,Y=U have identical observed X=Y, but do(X=1) yields Y=1 in the first and Y=U in the second.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Required confounding/invariance assumptions or intervention evidence cannot be assessed.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The claim is restricted to same-policy prediction and makes no causal or intervention assertion.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Association under the training policy is treated as an invariant response to an externally changed action. False negative: Useful engineering interventions can be justified with physical structure without estimating every causal relation.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Predictive fit demonstrates causality.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Policy, selection, mechanism or confounding changes reopen the transport claim.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Interventions can be costly or unsafe; observational adjustment requires substantive domain knowledge. Cheaper path: Prediction under the same validated policy and distribution does not need a full causal explanation.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Not all control models need a causal graph; known controlled inputs and physical mechanisms can supply different identification arguments. Transport to new environments adds invariance obligations beyond within-environment identification. FR007 provides intervention semantics and graphical identification machinery; the discriminator here is an explicit analytic construction, not a field study.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: Predictive identification does not by itself identify interventions or policy transport — evaluate the precisely scoped claim, including its rejection where applicable.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: The selected sparse equation satisfies its declared bounded prediction or structural-recovery criterion.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: SparseClaim(claim_target,M,Theta,coordinates,D_train,D_test,R)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: claim_target is BOUNDED_PREDICTION or STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY; Xi coefficients have term-specific units; R is the declared regime set; error tolerance is in output units; support-set equality is nominal.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Across the specified independent trajectories and sensitivity alternatives, not every possible coordinate system
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: equation model and fitted/held-out trajectories
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Finite evidence for current representation; no universal recovery claim
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Recorded library, measurements, numerical derivative/weak quadrature and intended use
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A selected sparse equation is claimed to explain or predict dynamics. Unknown or contradicted state sufficiency or library adequacy does not disable evaluation.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Select the actual claimed target before evaluation. For bounded prediction, document terms/coordinates, consider identifiable design alternatives and test the frozen equation against predeclared held-out transient/regime criteria. For structural recovery, additionally assess the state/observation correspondence, dictionary adequacy and distinguishing evidence needed by that structural claim. Missing material state/library support gives UNKNOWN for recovery, not INAPPLICABLE. A concrete same-training/different-required-trajectory or omitted-state structural counterexample gives FAIL of the target it contradicts; an invalidated sufficient proof premise alone does not. Do not transfer a predictive PASS to unique physical-law recovery.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: State measurements feed features; derivatives or integrated weak residuals carry their own noise/quadrature transformation
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Feature/coordinate specification, informative training trajectories, independent initial conditions, noise/error treatment, selection path

STEPS: Activate on the asserted selected sparse equation and record BOUNDED_PREDICTION or STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY.
Compare predictive trajectories and selected structure under justified perturbations; distinguish support instability from equivalent parameterization.
Evaluate only the premises material to the selected target; report separate outcomes if both targets are asserted.

OUTCOMES.PASS: For BOUNDED_PREDICTION, documented terms/coordinates, considered design alternatives and the frozen equation meet the predeclared held-out transient/regime criterion. For STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY, the defended representation, observation/state sufficiency and distinguishing structural evidence also support the stated recovery claim.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An applicable concrete trajectory or structural counterexample contradicts the selected claim, including an omitted-state witness against advertised autonomous structure. A missing or false merely sufficient proof premise alone does not establish falsity of the underlying claim.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Evidence material to the selected target remains unresolved: for structural recovery this includes sufficient-state correspondence, library adequacy and discriminating regimes; a separate bounded predictive result can still be decided on its own evidence.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: Only a known fixed law is fitted directly and no selected sparse prediction, explanation or recovery claim is asserted.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Computable on finite alternatives; exhaustive library/coordinate sufficiency and global law recovery are not decided
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Original SINDy includes canonical sparse systems recovered in appropriate coordinates with informative transients
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: SINDy cylinder-flow slow-manifold-only data produce an erroneous off-manifold form; another coordinate transform can destroy sparsity
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Evidence material to the selected target remains unresolved: for structural recovery this includes sufficient-state correspondence, library adequacy and discriminating regimes; a separate bounded predictive result can still be decided on its own evidence.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: Only a known fixed law is fitted directly and no selected sparse prediction, explanation or recovery claim is asserted.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False pass from canonical memorized tasks or redundant feature library; false fail from equivalent symbolic forms
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Select a library after seeing the desired law, or call high R² exact mechanism recovery
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Coordinate, feature, preprocessing, derivative/test function or sampling-envelope change invalidates support/recovery evidence
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use known-family estimation first when justified; weak integration trades derivative noise for quadrature/test-function design
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: A conditional sparse effective equation on tested regimes; not universal or unique generating mechanism
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: The selected sparse equation meets the explicitly claimed BOUNDED_PREDICTION or STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY criterion within the declared representation and test regime; name the target with the outcome.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: The advertised sparse structural interpretation has a warranted representation, observation and validation basis.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: SparseStructureSupported(data, coordinates, library, estimator, validation)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: Function list, coefficient units, singular values and physical prediction errors. Attribute ESI-RAT0133 supplies the structured arguments.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared model, input/observation regime, horizon and claim scope. Linear in coefficients permits nonlinear products as library columns; failure of a selected dictionary is not failure of all sparse regression.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A sparse-regression equation discovery claim
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: State/observation sufficiency, representability at the claimed accuracy, reliable derivative/weak estimates and informative regressors are assessed requirements of the defended structural warrant, not prerequisites for invoking this assessment.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Physical or structural interpretation is attached to a sparse learned equation, including when observed-state sufficiency or dictionary adequacy is unknown or contradicted.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Assess the stated structural-recovery warrant: check compatible state/observation semantics, representation of the defended structure, distinguishability of rival supports and validation outside the fitting trajectory. Unestablished state/library support gives UNKNOWN while the claim remains applicable. A concrete omitted-state structural falsifier gives FAIL. An established violation of an explicitly required support criterion can FAIL this warrant, but an invalidated merely sufficient proof premise alone is not falsity of the underlying structural equation.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Inspect selected columns and residual dependence; compare support stability across informative resampling and alternative plausible libraries.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {coordinates, observed/latent variables, library functions and units, derivative/weak estimator, sampling, support, rank/conditioning, separating validation}. Supporting source links are attached at property level; a deployed judgment additionally requires its own target evidence.

STEPS: Activate on the structural interpretation, without requiring its premises to pass first.
Bind coordinates, observations, library, numerical treatment and intended structural scope.
Distinguish an actual structural falsifier from missing support or failure of a merely sufficient proof route.
Return the warrant outcome and state separately whether an actual underlying-claim falsifier is known.

OUTCOMES.PASS: The scoped coefficient/support interpretation survives specified rival structures and independent regimes with justified observation/state, library and numerical evidence.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: A concrete omitted-state/term, observationally equivalent rival structure or regime counterexample invalidates the defended structural interpretation; or an established violation of an explicitly required support criterion defeats this named warrant. The latter alone does not declare the underlying equation false.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: State sufficiency, library adequacy, derivative bias or structural distinguishability material to the claim cannot be resolved. Failure of a merely sufficient theorem premise without an actual contradiction or violated required warrant criterion also leaves the claim unresolved.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No sparse physical or structural interpretation is claimed; an explicitly bounded fitted predictor has a separate target.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR023 Appendix F.3 reports SINDy as best on oscillator 2 with its chosen library; this is an author-reported conditional comparison.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: FR010 Bouc–Wen and tanks examples show hidden dynamics and library choices can yield misleading structure even with useful fit.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: State sufficiency, library adequacy, derivative bias or structural distinguishability material to the claim cannot be resolved. Failure of a merely sufficient theorem premise without an actual contradiction or violated required warrant criterion also leaves the claim unresolved.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No sparse physical or structural interpretation is claimed; an explicitly bounded fitted predictor has a separate target.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: An omitted nonlinear term or latent state is mistaken for an absent physical mechanism; collinear trajectory features create ambiguous supports. False negative: Requiring evidence that the true equation is in the library can be impossible; useful discovery often begins with an incomplete hypothesis class.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Products of nonlinear functions cannot be expressed by linear-in-coefficient sparse regression.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: New regime, omitted variable, changed coordinate or dictionary invalidates prior support claims.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Dictionary growth increases conditioning, search and validation burdens; expert feature design is real labor. Cheaper path: A predictive surrogate is sufficient, or the known equation structure only requires coefficient fitting.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Linear in coefficients permits nonlinear products as library columns; failure of a selected dictionary is not failure of all sparse regression. Sparse recovery guarantees do not establish physical truth under misspecified observations. FR008 demonstrates the method; FR010 documents hidden-state and hard-nonlinearity failures; FR023 itself reports an appropriate-library SINDy win.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY_WARRANT: the advertised sparse coefficient/support interpretation is supported within the declared coordinates, observation semantics, library and regime.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Weak-form evidence supports the explicitly selected numerical-adequacy or recovery-warrant claim.
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: WeakFormAdequate(claim_target,data,test_functions,quadrature,noise_model,tuning,observation_model,library)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: claim_target is NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY or RECOVERY_WARRANT. Keep time units, integration weights, covariance units and tuning provenance. The weak-form error-budget attribute supplies numerical arguments; observation_model and library are additionally required only to the extent needed by the asserted recovery claim.
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Only the declared measurements/model, windows, noise assumptions, regime, horizon and tolerance. NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY concerns the stated identity/error/tuning relation; RECOVERY_WARRANT additionally concerns the defended coefficient/support or structure. Noise robustness is not structural identifiability or hidden-state reconstruction.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A weak-form dynamic regression procedure
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Epistemic acceptance at the specified version; it is not a temporal safety invariant unless a cited theorem explicitly says so. Evidence remains valid only within its stated horizon and assumptions.
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: For NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY, establish the regularity, boundary treatment, quadrature resolution, noise/covariance control and permitted tuning information needed by the stated weak-identity/error claim. RECOVERY_WARRANT additionally needs justified state/observation sufficiency, library adequacy and informative data for the defended recovery scope. These conditions are assessed after invocation; numerical control cannot supply missing structural information.
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Weak forms are used for a noisy derivative-regression problem and their numerical adequacy or an associated recovery warrant is assessed. State sufficiency, library adequacy and numerical premises may be established, unknown or violated; they are not invocation gates.
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Select NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY or RECOVERY_WARRANT. Validate the integral identity and boundary terms for the chosen windows, quantify discretization/noise/covariance effects and disclose tuning information. A numerical claim can PASS on those bounded checks without establishing sufficient physical state. An asserted recovery warrant additionally requires supported state/observation, library and identifying-data conditions; unknown state sufficiency gives UNKNOWN, while an actual omitted-state structural counterexample defeats the warrant. Never use those success conditions as invocation guards or transfer numerical PASS to recovery.
predicates.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: RESEARCHER_RECONSTRUCTION of a guarded evaluation rule from the cited sources; not represented as a source-authored formula. Exact source theorem/identity terms, when used, are identified by source and locator.
predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Compare discretizations and noise realizations; separate observed-data tuning from ground-truth-assisted benchmark tuning.
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Record {test functions, support windows, boundary treatment, quadrature, measurement noise, residual covariance, tuning information}, with versions, units, thresholds and the selected claim target. RECOVERY_WARRANT additionally needs the observation/state map, library and distinguishing-data evidence relevant to its scope; see ESI-RC-FR07. Source links do not substitute for evidence about an actual assessed target.

STEPS: Activate when weak forms are used for a noisy derivative-regression problem.
Name the actual numerical-adequacy or recovery-warrant target; report both separately if both are claimed.
Check the numerical identity, boundary/error budget and allowed tuning information.
Check state/library/informativity requirements only for the recovery inference that needs them; preserve missingness.
Return the selected outcome, distinguishing an actual structural falsifier from failure of a warrant or merely sufficient proof premise.

OUTCOMES.PASS: NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY: the stated weak identities, boundary treatment and error controls hold at the required resolution, and tuning uses allowed information. RECOVERY_WARRANT: those applicable numerical conditions and the state/library/informativity evidence needed by the specific recovery claim are established. A numerical PASS alone grants no structural recovery.
OUTCOMES.FAIL: An actual identity, boundary/quadrature-error or tuning-access violation contradicts the selected numerical claim; for RECOVERY_WARRANT, an actual omitted-state/library structural counterexample or established violation of its explicitly required support criterion defeats that warrant. A false merely sufficient proof premise alone does not falsify the underlying solution or recovered law.
OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: Evidence material to the selected target is unavailable or unresolved. Unestablished noise/covariance, resolution, boundary or tuning evidence affects the corresponding numerical claim; unknown state sufficiency, library adequacy or identifying information additionally leaves recovery warrant UNKNOWN while it remains applicable. A correctly bounded numerical claim may be decided separately.
OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No noisy derivative-regression problem is present or weak forms are not used.

predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: A finite protocol audit or numerical comparison is decidable for supplied artifacts; universal continuous-domain equality, causal uniqueness or physical correspondence may require theorem reasoning and need not be decidable from finite data. Numerical checks establish only their sampled/bounded claim.
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: FR009 moves derivatives to test functions and evaluates noisy canonical ODE data.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: A threshold selected from the smallest true coefficient is not available in a blind unknown-law task; reproducing that score does not establish blind applicability.
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Evidence material to the selected target is unavailable or unresolved. Unestablished noise/covariance, resolution, boundary or tuning evidence affects the corresponding numerical claim; unknown state sufficiency, library adequacy or identifying information additionally leaves recovery warrant UNKNOWN while it remains applicable. A correctly bounded numerical claim may be decided separately.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No noisy derivative-regression problem is present or weak forms are not used.
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: Noise amplification by numerical derivatives prevents useful coefficient recovery. False negative: Weak integration can smooth away fast events or merge regimes.
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: An attribute’s existence, a source citation or a small aggregate metric is not satisfaction. Weak forms solve noisy identification independently of dictionary, sampling and observation conditions.
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Changed sample spacing, noise dependence, window length or library requires renewed calibration.
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Window/test-function selection, numerical quadrature and covariance modeling. Cheaper path: Accurate derivatives or low-noise dense measurements already support a simpler regression.
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Numerical noise robustness is distinct from structural identifiability or hidden-state reconstruction. Hard switching and hidden variables need additional modeling. The inherited source demonstrations and true-coefficient tuning limits are unchanged. A supported numerical identity/error claim is not evidence that absent state has been recovered.
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: The selected NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY or RECOVERY_WARRANT claim is supported for the declared weak-form regression problem; retain separate outcomes if both are asserted.
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY.TARGET: The explicitly bounded weak identity, numerical error or admissible-tuning claim on the named measurements, windows and tolerances.
NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY.PASS: The claimed identity/error relation and relevant boundary, quadrature, noise and tuning controls are established. Unknown full physical-state sufficiency does not block this bounded target when it is not a premise of that target.
NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY.FAIL: An actual relation/error violation or forbidden tuning contradicts the numerical claim.
NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY.UNKNOWN: A material numerical, measurement or tuning condition is unestablished; a merely failed sufficient error proof without a known violation leaves this target UNKNOWN.
NUMERICAL_ADEQUACY.LIMIT: No inference of structural identifiability, hidden-state reconstruction or unique physical law.

RECOVERY_WARRANT.TARGET: The evidence warrants the specifically asserted coefficient/support or structural recovery from weak regression.
RECOVERY_WARRANT.PASS: The selected numerical treatment and state/observation, library and identifying-data conditions needed by this recovery claim are justified.
RECOVERY_WARRANT.FAIL: An actual omitted-state or library counterexample contradicts the defended recovery structure, or an established violation of an explicitly required support criterion defeats the recovery warrant. Warrant failure without an actual structural falsifier is not a declaration that the underlying recovered equation is false.
RECOVERY_WARRANT.UNKNOWN: State sufficiency, library adequacy, information or another material recovery requirement is unresolved, absent a decisive falsifier.
RECOVERY_WARRANT.LIMIT: A numerical PASS cannot discharge this target; broader sparse structural assessment remains in ESI-RC-FR07.

predicates.EVALUATION_PRIORITY_RULE: Applicability follows the noisy derivative-regression use of weak forms, not successful premises. Identify the selected target; an applicable decisive contradiction or known violation of its required warrant criterion yields FAIL, complete support yields PASS, and otherwise material unresolved evidence yields UNKNOWN. A different unasserted target is not silently conjoined. Do not turn failure of a merely sufficient proof into underlying truth FAIL.

predicates.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Original universal simplicity-to-unique-law proposition
predicates.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: UniqueSimpleLaw(D,F,complexity,physical_equivalence)
predicates.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: D observations with units; F admissible laws; complexity grammar-dependent count; equivalence declared
predicates.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: All laws attaining the declared simplicity/fit criterion must belong to one relevant generating-mechanism equivalence class Keep the original universal domain fixed; a restriction is a different evaluated proposition.
predicates.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: expression class and observation regime
predicates.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Universal sufficiency candidate; counterexample at one regime refutes it
predicates.ASSUMPTIONS: Admissible class contains the rival laws and observed trajectory is correct
predicates.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Uniqueness is inferred from simplicity/fit alone
predicates.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: Evaluate only the original, explicitly stated universal proposition. PASS requires a valid argument for its entire original quantified domain with its original premises. FAIL requires a valid in-domain counterexample. UNKNOWN means the proposition or required evidence remains unsettled; lack of proof alone is not falsity. INAPPLICABLE when no such universal proposition is asserted. A restricted descendant with added premises is evaluated under a different named target and cannot establish this universal.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.basis: ESI-RS0042 representation/information limits; ESI-RS0055 oracle distinctions

predicates.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Observed variables and initial conditions define what the laws must reproduce; physical interpretation requires more than string equality
predicates.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Data, grammar/complexity rule, rival law search and a declared mechanism-equivalence relation

EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.evaluated_proposition: UNIVERSAL_PROPOSITION: simplicity/fit alone uniquely identifies the generating law
EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE.procedure: Evaluate only the original, explicitly stated universal proposition. PASS requires a valid argument for its entire original quantified domain with its original premises. FAIL requires a valid in-domain counterexample. UNKNOWN means the proposition or required evidence remains unsettled; lack of proof alone is not falsity. INAPPLICABLE when no such universal proposition is asserted. A restricted descendant with added premises is evaluated under a different named target and cannot establish this universal.
