predicates.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Counterexample exact; exhaustive symbolic uniqueness is generally not decided by finite search
predicates.POSITIVE_WITNESS: No positive witness for the unrestricted admitted proposition is asserted after the retained counterexample. Restricted successful mechanisms are preserved under ESI-RC-FR09:QUALIFIED_STRUCTURE_LICENSE.
predicates.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: In the stipulated one-term family x′=a x with a∈{−1,+1}, both laws have the same term-count complexity and generate x(t)=0 for x(0)=0; at x(0)=1 they generate e^t and e^-t
predicates.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: The original admissible class, physical-equivalence relation or evidence is insufficient to establish either a full universal argument or a valid in-domain counterexample. Lack of exhaustive symbolic search does not override an already established pair of compatible, physically different laws.
predicates.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No physical-law uniqueness claim
predicates.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False uniqueness from restricted grammar; false mismatch from algebraically equivalent expressions or gauge conventions
predicates.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Report numerical R² as symbolic recovery or optimize the grammar after seeing the answer
predicates.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Coordinates, grammar, simplification, oracle, initial-state coverage or interpretation changes invalidate recovery claim
predicates.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use a compact predictor without physical interpretation when enough; collect one discriminating initial condition when feasible
predicates.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Rejects uniqueness from simplicity alone; supports no universal statement that symbolic recovery is impossible
predicates.EVALUATED_PROPOSITION: UNIVERSAL_PROPOSITION: simplicity/fit alone uniquely identifies the generating law
predicates.ACTUAL_EVALUATION_STATUS: EXTERNAL_TARGET_NOT_EVALUATED; constructed and source-reported witnesses are separate evidence.

BOUNDED_FINAL_ARTIFACT.TARGET: The specified frozen model achieves the directly observed named benchmark result or satisfies a stated execution/training-repeatability criterion on the declared data and environment.

BOUNDED_FINAL_ARTIFACT.FAIL: Actual execution, metric or repeatability evidence contradicts the named bounded criterion.
BOUNDED_FINAL_ARTIFACT.UNKNOWN: The artifact, data, relevant runtime/training procedure, metric or required repeatability evidence is missing or unreliable.

INDEPENDENT_GENERALIZATION.TARGET: The evaluation evidence warrants the specifically claimed independent prospective-generalization conclusion.

REPEATED_SEARCH_REPRODUCIBILITY.LIMIT: Execution of the same frozen artifact is not another stochastic search; repeated-search results do not establish independent generalization without that target’s separate evaluation boundary.

SOURCES_AND_LOCATORS.CLAIM: Hierarchical stable-kernel identification integrates hyperparameter uncertainty; actual computation and reported performance retain the source-specific limits.

FIELDS.MISSPECIFIED_CONCENTRATION: R012 Theorem2.1 assumes iid data, a dominated family, KL-minimizer regularity, sufficient prior mass and testing/entropy bounds. The asymptotic concentration target can be a best approximation within a wrong family; relevant semimetrics and nonunique minima need care.
FIELDS.CALIBRATION_LIMIT: R013 §2.1 assumes local asymptotic normality, a nonsingular local matrix, a locally positive continuous prior and the stated posterior-contraction condition. Its posterior covariance generally differs from sampling covariance under misspecification; credible mass alone is not calibrated confidence.
FIELDS.MODEL_AVERAGING: R014 §1 weights supplied model posteriors by their posterior model probabilities. This addresses uncertainty within that set. Model/prior choice and approximate search remain consequential. Its Table10 reports improved held-out coverage in one example; no general physical correctness or uniform superiority follows.

BAYESIAN_HIERARCHY.DETAIL: Eqs. 10–17: conditionally independent Gaussian predictor-response vectors, covariance λ_k²K_α, K_α(i,j)=α^max(i,j); α uniform on (0,1), improper scale priors p(λ_k²)∝1/λ_k² and p(σ²)∝1/σ². FB integrates η=(α,λ²,σ²); EB plugs in marginal-likelihood maximizers (Algorithm 1). The mixture varies effective complexity within fixed truncation m.
BAYESIAN_HIERARCHY.COMPUTATION_AND_LIMITS: Algorithm 2 marginalizes θ for the α Metropolis update, addressing near-reducibility of conditioning on θ. Proposition 1 gives almost-sure convergence as M→∞, not a finite-run mixing bound. Materials and Methods reports 10,000 draws meeting a Raftery–Lewis quantile-precision criterion; this is a diagnostic, not universal assurance.

FIELDS.BAYESIAN_COMPARISON_CEILING: Two 1,000-run simulated ARMAX studies, DCM-simulated BOLD and real building-temperature data support reported predictive gains. PEM-Or uses validation data for order selection. EB uses separate decay rates; a multiple-rate FB check reports similar results (p. 10). General superiority and uncertainty-coverage gains were not established.

profiles.TITLE: Nonlinear input/output and hybrid mode boundary

CONTENT.STRUCTURE: Distinguish NARMAX innovation models, Hammerstein/Wiener static–dynamic compositions, nonlinear state-space feedback and PWA/SARX switched forms. These structures can represent different behavioral classes.
CONTENT.MODES: Record mode count, whether observed, exogenous, Markov, or determined by a partition; define boundary assignment for PWA regions.
CONTENT.LATENT_VARIABLES: Internal block signals, continuous state, noise innovation and discrete mode can all be unobserved; fitting an input/output map need not name their physical realization.
CONTENT.OBSERVATION_MAP: Specify measured outputs, actuator inputs, sensor nonlinearities, sampling and missingness. A nonlinear sensor can mimic a nonlinear plant.
CONTENT.IDENTIFIABILITY: State the equivalence class being distinguished. Mode labels are at least permutation-ambiguous; unvisited modes and internal block arrangements can remain indistinguishable.
CONTENT.OPTIMIZATION: Known partitions reduce to local regression; unknown partition/order/mode assignment creates joint structure estimation. A converged optimizer does not settle this structural ambiguity.
CONTENT.PHYSICAL_CONSTRAINTS: Include saturation, hysteresis, conservation and feasible inputs only with a physical warrant; black-box expressiveness alone supplies none.
CONTENT.VALIDATION_PER_REGIME: Partition evidence by excitation amplitude/type, operating mode, transition, initial state and horizon. Evaluate the intended prediction or simulation use; mark unvisited regimes unknown.
CONTENT.CHEAP_PATH: If a linear or simple block model meets a declared tolerance on the relevant envelope, extra modes or state coordinates need a decision benefit.
CONTENT.INVALIDATION: Changed sensor map, actuator saturation, switching logic, sample interval or requested operating envelope requires re-evaluation of the dependent claims.

CONTENT.TARGET: Finite-horizon distribution of observation sequences, rather than named physical hidden states.
CONTENT.STATE_AND_OBSERVATION: m hidden states; discrete observations; O emission and T transition matrices; positive initial probability vector.
CONTENT.EQUIVALENCE: Observable operators are similarity transforms of latent operators; their internal vectors need not be probability distributions over physical states.
CONTENT.ASSUMPTIONS: Hsu Condition 1: O,T rank m and positive initial probabilities. Theorem 6 depends on smallest singular values; Theorem 7 adds strict positivity.
CONTENT.DATA_PROTOCOL: The stated proof uses independent sequences starting from the same initial distribution. Reusing a long dependent trajectory needs its own concentration/mixing argument.
CONTENT.REALIZATION_RELATION: Predictive sufficiency of observable operators does not uniquely identify O,T or the meaning of hidden state labels.
CONTENT.VALIDATION: Evaluate joint or conditional observation probabilities at the stated horizon and metric; calibration and support must match the theorem invoked.
CONTENT.FAILURE_WITNESS: Two hidden states with identical emission columns violate the rank separation; adding samples under the same indistinguishable observation map cannot fix that structural defect.
CONTENT.CURRENTNESS: A changed emission mechanism or transition regime changes the target distribution and can invalidate old rank and accuracy evidence.

profiles.TITLE: Selected inverse solution versus identified intervention

CONTENT.NATIVE_TRADITIONS: Regularized inverse problems recover an unknown from a forward map; structural causal models identify effects of specified interventions. They share inverse reasoning without sharing every estimand or assumption.
CONTENT.TARGET: Inverse x in A x≈b, or causal Q=P(Y|do(X=x)); these are separate targets.
CONTENT.ASSUMPTIONS: Inverse: declare domain D, noise model and fixed objective coefficients/center. The Tikhonov kernel iff is for fixed A,L,b,x*,λ>0 over R^n; constrained existence/uniqueness needs its own argument. Causal: structural equations/intervention semantics and restrictions making Q invariant across observationally equivalent models.
CONTENT.EQUIVALENCE: Compare feasible inverse solutions with the same observations within the declared domain, and causal models with the same observational law; these equivalence classes remain explicit.
CONTENT.INTERVENTION_EVIDENCE: Randomized or natural/environmental perturbations can distinguish models when their intervention semantics and exclusions are justified. ICP needs invariant target mechanism and valid tests; observed invariance alone is not an unqualified causal certificate.
CONTENT.OBSERVABILITY_INTERFACE: ObsNODE is an explicit 2026 hybrid: observable normal form plus causal adjustment assumptions. Approximate finite noisy state reconstruction and serial confounding remain limitations.
CONTENT.UNSUPPORTED_EXTRAPOLATIONS: Unique regularized optimum→true parameter; predictive accuracy→causal effect; state observability→identified unknown parameterization; clinical forecast validation→counterfactual accuracy.
CONTENT.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Exhibit two compatible models with different Q, or supply interventions/structural restrictions ruling one out; for inverse recovery, obtain observations outside the current nullspace.

profiles.TITLE: Sparse and weak-form equation inference

CONTENT.INFORMATION: Sampled trajectories must distinguish candidate terms, including transient directions if the use includes them. Long samples on one invariant manifold need not distinguish off-manifold terms.

CONTENT.ORACLE: Synthetic equation recovery can use known generating equations; real-data predictive validation cannot supply that oracle.
CONTENT.CHEAP_PATH: A fixed, known equation family with a few coefficients may need ordinary parameter estimation rather than open-ended library search.

profiles.TITLE: Koopman/DMD and projected operator targets

CONTENT.REPRESENTATION: DMD fits A=YX† to snapshot pairs; Koopman lifts observables; operator inference estimates polynomial operators in a chosen reduced basis.
CONTENT.INDUCTIVE_BIAS: Finite observable dictionary or reduced projection space, rank truncation and polynomial operator class.
CONTENT.INFORMATION: Snapshot coverage and design-matrix rank depend on coordinates, scaling and input/initial-state variation. Large raw sample counts do not imply rank or stable conditioning.
CONTENT.CONSTRAINTS: For exact finite Koopman closure, the selected span must be invariant. For OpInf, the theorem target is the intrusive projected operator of a supplied full model.
CONTENT.EMPIRICAL_SCOPE: Demonstrations of finite-data models and residual checks; source-specific fluid/simulation examples are not universal accuracy evidence.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY: Separate sampling, truncation, quadrature, derivative and full-model discrepancy. Residual spectral inclusion is not physical uncertainty calibration.
CONTENT.VALIDATION: Hold the selected dictionary fixed under the invoked quadrature limit and reject interpolation-forced residuals. §3.3.2 permits independent random splitting, suitable fresh quadrature points, or an initial-segment dictionary with an expanding ergodic prefix; overlap is allowed in the last route. Predictive transfer still needs claim-matched trajectory/horizon evaluation.
CONTENT.GUARANTEE: ResDMD asymptotic pseudospectral inclusion and OpInf n→N/time-step→0 statements are distinct and not interchangeable.
CONTENT.CHEAP_PATH: An already adequate low-dimensional linear predictor need not be relabeled as a recovered infinite-dimensional operator.

profiles.TITLE: Evidence-sensitive online update

CONTENT.VALIDITY_ENVELOPE: State input/mode envelope, sensor calibration, noise/feedback policy, sample interval and intended horizon for each retained claim.
CONTENT.DRIFT_INDICATORS: Changes in residual distribution, input support, sensor calibration or mode occupancy are separate signals; distinguish parameter drift from observation drift.
CONTENT.RECALIBRATION: Use a specified detector and estimator only after examining whether new data identify the affected parameter directions. Recalibration is not automatically better.
CONTENT.EVIDENCE_REUSE: Preserve earlier informative observations when the corresponding mechanism remains current; retain dependence on source regime and timestamp.
CONTENT.INVALIDATION: Invalidate the claims whose assumptions changed, rather than deleting every old result or blessing the whole model because bytes did not change.
CONTENT.RETIREMENT: Retire a predictive/control use when its tolerance, observation integrity, regime support or update stability lacks evidence; re-enter after targeted validation.
CONTENT.FALLBACK: A validated fixed model, bounded lookup/rule, direct measurement or abstention is possible when new online estimates are uninformative.
CONTENT.COST: Additional excitation and false resets incur operating cost; forgotten information can be expensive to reacquire.
CONTENT.CALIBRATION_LIMIT: Sequential alarms need their own false-alarm/delay analysis; a fixed-test asymptotic p-value is not automatically a lifetime error bound.

profiles.TITLE: Claim-matched validation under dependence

CONTENT.CLAIM: Name same-regime one-step prediction, free simulation, unseen unit, unseen input policy, parameter recovery or intervention prediction before selecting a split.
CONTENT.PARTITION: Separate fitting, preprocessing, feature/dictionary selection, tuning and final assessment. Split at the unit whose transfer is claimed.
CONTENT.INDEPENDENCE: Temporal order is necessary for some forecasting claims; stationary AR cross-validation can be valid under explicit conditions. Group dependence and shared trajectories need their own treatment.
CONTENT.NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: Compare a cheap baseline; use irrelevant channels or shuffled assignments only when the null preserves the relevant dependence; test invariance to solver refinement where appropriate.
CONTENT.METRICS: Use output units and horizon; report per-regime failures, stability and symbolic/parameter outcomes separately from aggregate prediction error.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY: State sampling population, repetition unit, calibration assumptions and uncertainty interval method; no iid standard errors for dependent samples without justification.

profiles.TITLE: Typed guarantee and transfer obligations

CONTENT.DECISION_LIMIT: A correct guarantee about an estimator does not establish desirability of a control action or completeness of the user objective.

profiles.TITLE: Refitting and representational complexity as decisions

CONTENT.DECISION: Whether a new model/update/representation changes a specified operational action sufficiently to justify its total cost.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY_BEFORE_AFTER: Compare relevant prediction/parameter/decision uncertainty and regime support; do not substitute model count or in-sample loss.
CONTENT.TOTAL_COST: Data acquisition and safe excitation, sensor calibration, training/tuning, validation, reviewer correction, deployment, monitoring, maintenance and consequences of wrong decisions.
CONTENT.CONSEQUENCES: Errors at sensitive thresholds or over unstable free simulations can dominate average error; a harmless interpolator has a cheaper acceptance path.
CONTENT.COMPARATOR: Validated existing model, linear model, lookup table, bounded rule, direct observation and no additional model are admissible comparators.
CONTENT.REUSE_HORIZON: Count offline cost against the actual number and distribution of downstream evaluations, not an assumed infinite amortization.
CONTENT.RETIREMENT_RULE: Stop refitting or retire a complex representation when it cannot improve the consumer’s evidence/decision relative to its cost; re-enter when a material regime or use changes.
CONTENT.OBJECTIVE_BOUNDARY: A model can rank options under an objective without validating the objective, constraints or authority to act.

profiles.TRANSFORMATION_CLASS: Extraction records; abstraction groups; inference generalizes; interpretation assigns meaning; formalization specifies a predicate; adoption grants a normative role. These are distinct transformations.
profiles.PRESERVED_CLAIM: Only explicitly checked relation, such as accepted trace, mapped call edge or witnessed action under the declared context.
profiles.LOSS: Hidden state, data distinctions, unlogged work, un selected predicates, alternative meanings and counterfactual behavior can be lost.
profiles.INTRODUCED_ASSUMPTIONS: Determinism, case identity, regularity, code-to-deployment correspondence and analyst categories are not raw observations.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Keep observation ally compatible alternatives or an explicit open question if available evidence cannot choose.
profiles.CORRESPONDENCE_CHECK: Round-trip serialization checks formatting only. Semantic checks use trace replay, observation-map audit, static reasoning or comparison with participant/context records.
profiles.COUNTEREXAMPLE: Two distinct TLS states can share a response code; two workflow nets can share directly-follows relations; identical observed behavior can satisfy different intentions.
profiles.AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY: Descriptive translation does not authorize a requirement, deployment or workplace intervention.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

NATIVE_GUARANTEES.positive_text: No universal eventual exact learner for superfinite class under arbitrary positive presentation.
NATIVE_GUARANTEES.exact_queries: Minimal DFA with polynomial resource bound under MAT.
NATIVE_GUARANTEES.timed: One-clock exact language learning under specified reset information.
NATIVE_GUARANTEES.stochastic: Asymptotic almost-sure convergence under sampling/test modifications.
NATIVE_GUARANTEES.source_extraction: Deterministic relation computation under chosen parser/mapping, not runtime completeness.
NATIVE_GUARANTEES.finite_validation: Consistency or discovered counterexample within actual tests; proof failure may remain unknown.

profiles.QUANTIFIERS: Name all targets, every permitted presentation, almost surely, or sampled trials explicitly; they are not interchangeable confidence levels.
profiles.TRANSFER_REQUIREMENTS: A representation map plus evidence that real subject meets target-class, oracle, reset, stationarity and context conditions. Changing target, observations or quantifier needs a new argument.
profiles.NON_TRANSFER: DFA theorem does not prove a concurrently accessed adaptive service has a unique learned machine; formal proof of generated contract does not prove it captures user intent.
profiles.COMPUTATIONAL_LIMIT: Identifiability is separate from feasible queries/solver budget. Practical termination may mean budget exhausted.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.DECISION: Find a protocol flaw, explain a particular dependency, validate a candidate contract or compare bounded test strategies.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY_BEFORE_AFTER: Record the rival hypotheses or decision states actually eliminated; number of nodes, invariants or generated pages alone is not information gain.
profiles.TOTAL_COST: Data/instrumentation, resets/side effects, expert interpretation, query/model calls, solver computation, validation and recurring maintenance.
profiles.MAINTENANCE: Changing implementation, mappings, inputs, deployment or purpose can invalidate the result; keep a bounded currentness envelope.
profiles.CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVES: Direct property tests, documentation, known examples, focused source slice, or consciously bounded uncertainty may dominate full reconstruction.
profiles.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE: Case feasibility and benchmark improvements support domain-specific benefit; no universal net-benefit comparison across all reconstruction methods was found. C034 v2 has model-specific scaffold benefit and harm; its 23.5% excess queries applies only to successful 8–9-state runs, not total monetary cost.
profiles.RETIREMENT: Stop maintaining an explicit model if its consumer disappears or cheaper evidence gives the required discrimination, while preserving evidence needed for unresolved decisions.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.CLAIM: Distinguish execution consistency, whole-model correspondence, generated-spec adequacy and externally desired behavior.
profiles.PARTITION: Separate training/generation/feedback from evaluation by actual input/context and leakage analysis; a new evaluation label copied from the same defective program is not independent normative evidence.
profiles.CHALLENGE: Known violations, changed inputs, output mutants, state-depth probes, independent requirements, alternative de compositions and adversarial instrumentation cases.
profiles.OUTCOME: PASS for the scoped condition and evidence; FAIL for a witnessed breach; UNKNOWN for insufficient data or inconclusive proof; INAPPLICABLE for a false declared trigger. Benchmark zero-credit policy is separate from logical falsity.
profiles.COVERAGE: Keep invalid outputs, failed runs and missing tasks in declared denominators; report unknown/un evaluable separately and avoid success-only averages. C034 v2 excludes malformed calls from the query budget and separates successful-run query summaries from full success-rate denominators; retain that counting policy explicitly.
profiles.COST: Decisive counterexamples can be cheaper than exhaustive reconstruction; broadening tests requires a decision-relevant remaining uncertainty.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.VALIDITY_ENVELOPE: Bind source/build/deployment, adapter/instrumentation, input/data distribution, oracle/verifier/model version and intended consumer.
profiles.DRIFT_INDICATORS: Replay disagreement, changed labels, unexplained edges, newly missing events, increased invalid outputs or altered proof semantics.
profiles.INVALIDATION: A material change invalidates dependent claims; unrelated artifact changes need not force total reconstruction.
profiles.REENTRY: Re-run the smallest discriminating experiment or correspondence check; full relearning only when local evidence cannot restore the decision claim.
profiles.FORMALIZATION_PROVENANCE: Researcher operationalization of the demonstrated context dependence, not a claimed universal historical protocol.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.profile_role: Reusable research assessment profile, not an evaluated target installation.
profiles.purpose: Separate prediction, explanation, intervention, control, diagnosis, conformance, migration and documentation; bind only the actual consumer question.
profiles.boundary: Declare entity/configuration, environment, initial conditions, excluded regimes and observation pipeline.

variables.input: Manipulable signal/query or passive covariate with units and policy identity.
variables.state: Possibly latent coordinate; physical interpretation requires extra evidence.
variables.disturbance: Unmodeled environmental effects, possibly correlated with input.
variables.noise: Measurement/model noise whose assumed law or bound is recorded.

profiles.observation_map: Record sensor/log meaning, calibration, units, clocks, sampling, synchronization, antialiasing/filtering, missingness, quantization, saturation and censoring; a filter can change both noise and dynamics.
profiles.accessible_interventions: Only experiments actually available and permitted. Passive observation cannot be upgraded to an intervention record.
profiles.excluded_regimes: Explicit set; unknown reachability is an evidence limit rather than a favorable exclusion.
profiles.intended_consumer: Named decision or question with prediction horizon and tolerable error; no target-specific consumer was inspected.
profiles.claim_type: State separately model truth, empirical correspondence, likelihood/causal claim, normative obligation and authority.
profiles.weakest_sufficient_model: Direct calibrated reading for one current value; lookup/linear model for a bounded relation; richer dynamics only when needed for the named decision.
profiles.complexity_increase_reason: Show a material failure of the cheaper alternative and a relevant validation plan before increasing state/order/representation size.
profiles.use_shift_discriminator: A model adequate for the mean under a fixed policy may not be adequate for tail constraints or a changed policy; reuse requires new information/validation reasoning.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.source_subject: Raw measurements, traces, artifacts or a mathematically implicit constraint; distinguish these before choosing a representation.
profiles.target_representation: Event table, trace language, input-output model, constraint set, graph, explanation or executable check selected for one consumer.
profiles.preserved_claim: Define q on the source and q′ on the target; claim q′∘T=q only on the declared domain, or give an explicit approximation/refinement relation.
profiles.loss: Trace counts erase order; normalization may erase units; a selected solution branch may discard alternatives; a learned graph may omit unobserved transitions.
profiles.introduced_assumptions: Interpretation, closed domain, query language, abstraction/reset semantics, solver branch and any statistical model introduced by the transformation.
profiles.uncertainty: Retain unresolved interpretations or model sets; an explicit single representation is not evidence that alternatives were discriminated.
profiles.correspondence_check: Finite fiber test for a finite construction, formal simulation/trace inclusion where justified, or independent empirical validation for external correspondence. These checks have different ceilings.
profiles.counterexample: AB and BA collapse under event-count projection yet disagree on which action came first; 32 F round-trips but is misread as 32 C; local errors sum beyond aggregate tolerance.
profiles.authority_boundary: No extraction or descriptive correspondence creates a requirement or permission to mutate the represented system.
profiles.cheap_path: Retain raw trace or a small claim-relevant table; keep a stable implicit mathematical constraint when an explicit solution is unnecessary.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.decision: Choose whether to collect more data, construct/enlarge a model, maintain it or retire it for a named decision.
profiles.uncertainty_before_after: Compare uncertainty of the decision-relevant quantity, including structural alternatives; reduced parameter variance is not automatically useful.
profiles.total_cost: Acquisition, instrumentation, experiments, expert time, compute, human correction, validation, deployment monitoring, upkeep and retirement over an explicit horizon.
profiles.consequences: Decision loss under the intended environment, plus hard constraints which are not converted into arbitrary exchangeable costs.
profiles.comparator: A fair feasible baseline: direct measurement, bounded rule, lookup, existing specification, fixed model or no additional machinery.
profiles.reuse_horizon: State duration/use count and evidence for reuse; speculative future consumers are not guaranteed benefit.
profiles.retirement_rule: Retire or narrow the model when the receiving question disappears, validity cannot be maintained or a cheaper adequate alternative dominates.
profiles.quantitative_rule: Within feasible authorized options, compare expected decision loss plus lifecycle cost in declared common units; overlapping uncertain intervals can leave the choice UNKNOWN.
profiles.worked_example: Constructed common-unit comparison: baseline loss10+cost0=10; useful model loss6+cost2=8. The reduction4 covers incremental cost2, assuming all relevant consequences are included. Constructed common-unit comparison: baseline loss10+cost0=10; costly model loss8+cost5=13. A smaller decision loss alone does not establish better total value.
profiles.evidence_ceiling: Primary economic reasoning, a cost-estimation example and a success-selected longitudinal field case; no universal realized return-on-investment estimate. Access limitations are source-specific.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.PURPOSE: Distinguish prediction, simulation, explanation, intervention, diagnosis and control. Each consumer determines a different loss, horizon and relevant uncertainty.
profiles.BOUNDARY: Declare included plant, actuator, sensor, controller/operator and environmental pathways; an approximately closed boundary is a modeling assumption. A deliberate input/output partition is specific to the experiment, not a universal ontology.

VARIABLES.INPUT: Delivered stimulus, not merely command. State whether externally set, feedback-generated or observationally recorded.
VARIABLES.OUTPUT: Measured quantity with units/calibration and clock.
VARIABLES.STATE: Internal coordinate of the model; physical meaning needs an independent map.
VARIABLES.NOISE: Observation/process error with law or bound and independence assumptions.
VARIABLES.INITIAL_CONDITION: Known, estimated, randomized, constrained or nuisance; affects identifiable behavior.
VARIABLES.ENVIRONMENT: Operating conditions and external agents whose changes can alter the observation or response law.

profiles.OBSERVATION_MAP: x(t),u(t) -> sensor/actuator transformation -> filtering/quantization/saturation/censoring -> sample clock -> missingness/preprocessing -> recorded data. Timing, units and each material transformation must be accounted for. No target calibration was performed.
profiles.ACCESSIBLE_INTERVENTIONS: State permitted input ranges, duration, resets, sensor access and operation constraints. A mathematical experiment is not authorization to disturb a real installation.
profiles.EXCLUDED_REGIMES: Unexcited frequencies, new amplitudes/input distributions, unmeasured states, different controller, sampling/hold changes, saturation and rare disturbances remain outside unless separately covered.
profiles.INTENDED_CONSUMER: A named controller/predictor/analyst and the decision they will make; not a generic need for more explicit models.
profiles.CLAIM_TYPE: Conditional behavior/prediction, identifiable parameter combination, physical mechanism, or control certificate must be named separately.
profiles.WEAKEST_SUFFICIENT_MODEL: A gain, sign, lookup table, FRF over a required band or compatible-model set may suffice. Richer state/nonlinear structure needs a demonstrated decision-relevant error or ambiguity.
profiles.OBSERVATION_TO_INTERVENTION_SHIFT: A correlation-based predictor may fail under a changed policy; feedback/noise pathways and accessible interventions need renewed justification.
profiles.AVERAGE_TO_TAIL_CONTROL_SHIFT: Average MSE does not bound tail errors, unmodeled resonance, stability margin or constraints. Add suitable uncertainty/robustness evidence.
profiles.CASE: XCL09 sensor-scale change and XCL11 horizon mismatch.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Observation and purpose requirements are source-grounded synthesis; no universal calibration procedure or external target assessment.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.CANDIDATE_MODEL_CLASS: Explicit Theta including admissible structures/order, parameter domains, initial states, observation map and stochastic laws. Distinguish fixed structure parameter recovery from structure selection.
profiles.EQUIVALENCE_RELATION: theta~theta_prime iff permitted experiments yield identical ideal observed trajectories or identical observation laws; one observed trace alone is not equality of laws.

SCOPE_VARIANTS.GLOBAL: Every candidate in the declared class is distinguished up to the stated equivalence.
SCOPE_VARIANTS.LOCAL: Uniqueness in a stated neighborhood; remote branches may remain.
SCOPE_VARIANTS.GENERIC: Except an identified exceptional set; not a statement about every parameter value.
SCOPE_VARIANTS.PRACTICAL: Finite noisy data precision for a chosen target/tolerance. Raue uses interval-boundedness terminology; Söderström/Stoica uses estimator-convergence terminology for system identifiability.

DISTINCT_CONCEPTS.OBSERVABILITY: For a known model and inputs, distinguish initial states from outputs; does not by itself identify unknown parameters.
DISTINCT_CONCEPTS.CONTROLLABILITY: Ability to reach states through admissible inputs in the model; distinct from observing them.
DISTINCT_CONCEPTS.DISTINGUISHABILITY: A pair of candidates has different allowed observation consequences.
DISTINCT_CONCEPTS.ESTIMABILITY: Precision/recovery of a target under a sampling scheme; statistical usage must be stated.
DISTINCT_CONCEPTS.CONDITIONING: Sensitivity of a numerical inverse to perturbations, relative to scaling; full rank does not imply good conditioning.

profiles.INFORMATION_CONDITIONS: For exact regression, nullspace directions must not change the target. Dynamical conditions additionally depend on order, initial state, excitation and observation channels.
profiles.IDENTIFIABLE_QUANTITIES: XCL01 g=a+b; XCL02 input/output Markov parameters and minimal realization class under appropriate conditions.
profiles.UNIDENTIFIABLE_QUANTITIES: Individual a, b in y=(a+b)u; arbitrary latent basis; hidden unobservable/uncontrollable modes from the stated interface.
profiles.CONDITIONING: XCL03 rank 2 matrix with near-collinear columns has condition number≈4002 in the declared unit scaling; scaling changes this number.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Profile/set geometry and target uncertainty are separate from structural uniqueness; a prior can select along a ridge without adding experimental information.
profiles.DISCRIMINATING_EXPERIMENT: For sum-only model add a channel measuring a−b, or an intervention that changes one component coefficient independently. More of the same sum-channel data cannot help.
profiles.CLASS_MISSPECIFICATION: Uniqueness within a wrong class may be externally misleading; preserving several classes can be more honest.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Bellman 1970 and Rothenberg 1971 full proofs were inaccessible. Exact equivalence witnesses and later inspected texts support retained claims; no universal information-matrix criterion is asserted.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.DISCRIMINATING_QUESTION: Which alternatives change the target decision and remain observationally compatible? Design a measurement/input that makes their predictions differ above uncertainty.
profiles.ALLOWABLE_INPUTS_INTERVENTIONS: Amplitude, energy, rate, duration, bandwidth, resets, reference commands and measured delivered signals; authority and operational limits declared by the installation/study, not supplied by this research.
profiles.MODEL_ASSUMPTIONS: Known target class/order/lag bounds where required; fixed versus changing parameters; noise support/law; initial-state knowledge; feedback.
profiles.INFORMATION_CRITERION: Rank/nullspace for exact linear target, minimum directional information/conditioning, Fisher information under statistical premises, target variance, feasible-set diameter or expected decision loss. These criteria are not interchangeable.
profiles.PERSISTENT_EXCITATION: Söderström/Stoica p120 gives asymptotic covariance PE and separately notes sliding-window adaptive-control usage. Specify order and horizon rather than writing a barePE flag.
profiles.MULTIVARIABLE_INPUTS: Multiple channels may be individually rich but jointly collinear. Test the full regressor/cross-channel information needed by the target.
profiles.FINITE_SAMPLE_CONDITIONS: Simchowitz 2018 uses finite-time Gramian/small-ball reasoning for nonexplosive fully observed Gaussian dynamics. Camlibel 2025 shortest experiment assumes exact minimal LTI data and complexity bounds. Neither is a universal noisy-data rank test.
profiles.SAFETY_AUTHORITY_LIMITS: Do not infer permission or safe operation from a theoretically informative signal. An input can be mathematically excellent yet excite omitted dynamics or exceed actuator/state limits.
profiles.STOPPING_CONDITION: Stop when the target decision is supported at required tolerance or marginal information value falls below cost; data-dependent stopping requires its own statistical accounting.
profiles.NUISANCE_EFFECTS: Transient response, feedback-induced dependence, temperature/operating-point drift, input uncertainty, sensor changes, nonlinear distortion and experiment-induced regime changes.
profiles.CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Use existing informative data, a scalar gain experiment, passive covariance, or a compatible-model robust decision. Unique model recovery is unnecessary for every action.
profiles.NEGATIVE_OR_UNAVAILABLE_CASE: If required excitation is operationally impermissible, retain uncertainty or narrow the use; do not falsely mark identification complete.
profiles.SEQUENTIAL_DUAL_CONTROL_BOUNDARY: CL031 §§2–4 treats action as changing both the physical state and future information. Belief-state expected cost, rather than parameter variance alone, assigns value to future learning. The local Gaussian/quadratic approximation is computationally tractable in the inspected simple examples, but is prior-, horizon- and cost-relative. It does not establish hard safety or general field superiority. Feldbaum/Tse antecedents were traced through explicit citations, not original-body reading.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Oshima 2025 follow-up explicitly addresses a prior single-trial limitation but full methods inaccessible; its reported percentage improvements are withheld.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.GENERAL_MODEL: A(q)y=[B(q)/F(q)]u+[C(q)/D(q)]e, or y=G(q)u+H(q)e with q a declared shift convention. Orders/delays and initial-state treatment are part of the model.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: Time-series prediction/likelihood with no external input: Ay=e, y=Ce, Ay=Ce. Autocovariance/innovations encode stochastic output dynamics.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Colored/nonstationary errors, wrong order/invertibility or treating a purely observational stochastic model as an intervention law.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: Useful forecasting need not reveal physical excitation or mechanism.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: Minimize sum(y−phi^Ttheta)^2; ARX Ay=Bu+e shares the process denominator with noise; FIR A=1 has finite input regressors.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Regressor/error correlation, weak excitation, noisy inputs or misspecified lag/order.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: Linear optimization simplicity does not guarantee consistency.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: Ay=Bu+Ce; minimize prediction errors using modeled colored innovations; nonlinear parameter estimation generally required.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Wrong noise dynamics, shared-pole restrictions, local minima, underexcitation.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: More noise flexibility can reduce bias but adds estimation burden.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: y=(B/F)u+e, H=1; fit simulated plant output to measured output.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Colored output disturbance or input/error dependence invalidates naive efficient-likelihood claims; feedback matters.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: Simulation-error objective differs from one-step prediction objective.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: y=(B/F)u+(C/D)e; distinct process/noise parameters permit separate pole structure.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Higher variance/order selection and incorrect closed-loop assumptions; flexible noise does not certify plant structure.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: Useful when disturbance enters differently, but shared true poles can be estimated more efficiently by a justified shared structure.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: PEM minimizes explicitly weighted innovations; under suitable Gaussian law and correct covariance/initial treatment it corresponds to likelihood.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Distribution/noise misspecification, optimizer failure and regime dependence.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: PEM is not automatically ML and neither is mechanism truth.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: Solve z-weighted residual moments; exogeneity and relevance replace ordinary LS orthogonality.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Invalid/weak instruments and unmodeled feedback pathways.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: Can identify plant with less noise-model detail, but efficiency and finite-sample precision require further conditions.

MATERIAL_FAMILIES.OBJECTIVE_MECHANISM: Estimate external responses or spectra with controlled input/repeats; spectral ratio needs sufficient power and appropriate disturbance independence or closed-loop correction.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.BREAKS: Leakage, transient contamination, sampling ambiguity, low-frequency resolution, nonlinear ensemble changes and feedback.
MATERIAL_FAMILIES.CONSEQUENCE: A simple nonparametric band estimate can suffice without a high-order latent realization.

profiles.MODEL_ORDER_AND_REGULARIZATION: Order trades approximation bias and variance. Compare residual and decision performance; stability constraints and regularization encode additional assumptions, not observed truth.
profiles.FREQUENCY_DESIGN: Use settled periodic records of integer periods to suppress leakage where feasible; windowing has resolution/variance tradeoffs; document excitation power, amplitude distribution and spectral resolution.
profiles.ONE_STEP_MULTI_STEP_CONTROL: XCL11: one-step 0.01 error can coexist with 100-step 1.7048 error. Controller stability/constraints additionally need closed-loop robustness evidence.
profiles.NONLINEAR_LINEAR_FIT_CASE: XCL05 cubic BLA gain changes from 1.3 to2.2 solely when Gaussian input variance changes 1→4.
profiles.SAMPLING_REFINEMENT: CL021 known continuous multisine and nonoverlap conditions allow specific above-Nyquist FRF estimation; this does not remove general aliasing/unknown-input concerns.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Methods are not ranked globally. Book selected sections and frequency tutorial mechanisms were inspected; original Box/Jenkins book and complete early spectral priority history were not.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.COORDINATE_CONVENTION: x_next=Ax+Bu, y=Cx+Du, with initial-state convention. State basis may be canonical, balanced or algorithm-selected; none is a physical ontology by itself.
profiles.ORDER: Minimal externally represented dimension under stated interface/class; finite/noisy order evidence is a singular-value/validation assessment, not exact nonzero rank of raw noisy matrices.
profiles.OBSERVABILITY_CONTROLLABILITY_ASSUMPTION: Known-model ranks characterize state visibility/reachability. Only externally excited and observed behavior is recoverable without extra sensors/priors; an invisible unstable physical mode is not excluded by a stable minimal transfer model.
profiles.IDENTIFIABILITY_CLASS: Minimal LTI realizations are compared up to similarity under standard conditions. XCL02 gives TAT^-1,TB, CT^-1,D correspondence with transformed initial state.
profiles.NOISE_MODEL: Innovation/state/output noise locations and correlation; a Kalman state estimate presumes model parameters, whereas identification estimates the governing class/parameters from data.
profiles.SUBSPACE_MECHANISM: Data block projections estimate state sequences; QR/SVD factor observed behavior; recover matrices through shift structure/least squares. N4SID finite-past approximation trades computation for bias.
profiles.ORDER_SELECTION_EVIDENCE: Report horizon lengths, normalized singular values, noise thresholds, candidate orders and out-of-sample predictions; small unexcited modes can remain undetected.
profiles.VALIDATION_OBLIGATIONS: Compare basis-invariant outputs/Markov parameters and required long-horizon/control properties. Physical state meaning needs independent state-sensitive observations.
profiles.MODEL_REDUCTION: Reduction discards behavior according to a selected criterion. A good average fit or stable prior does not preserve every stability margin/constraint-relevant mode; Pillonetto proposition 4 is conditional Bayes reduction, not universal preservation.
profiles.EXTENSIONS: Closed-loop dependence must be handled separately; GREAT tracks behavioral subspaces with bounded errors/drift/information and close initialization. Missing-data and large-scale/constrained realization algorithms were not deeply inspected in this lane.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Ho–Kalman original available only as metadata; inspected 1971/1989 expositions and 1994 primary algorithms supply mechanism.2026 autonomous subspace paper abstract only, not used for a quantitative guarantee.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.DATA_GENERATING_POLICY: u=r−Ky or explicit nonlinear/time-varying/controller/operator policy. Disturbance-dependent input must not be relabeled exogenous.
profiles.FEEDBACK_ASSUMPTIONS: Loop well-posedness/stability, delay, controller knowledge, reference independence and measured signals; explain if saturation or operator actions alter them.
profiles.DIRECT_INDIRECT_JOINT: Direct fits plant/noise to closed-loop data with suitable predictor; indirect uses known controller and closed-loop transfer; joint models input/output together. None uniformly dominates.
profiles.RELEVANT_UNCERTAINTY: Controller-band gain/phase, omitted high-frequency dynamics, time delay, disturbances, nonlinear saturation, model class and transient state; prediction MSE alone is insufficient.
profiles.CONTROLLER_MODEL_COUPLING: Controller determines excitation/data; estimated model changes controller, which changes subsequent data distribution. A successful regulator can suppress the information needed for parameter convergence.
profiles.OPERATING_ENVELOPE: Specify frequencies, reference/disturbance amplitudes, initial conditions and state/input constraints actually covered.
profiles.INTERVENTION_AUTHORITY: Theory neither authorizes opening a loop nor proves safe probing. Actual operational permission and limits are external premises.
profiles.VALIDATION: Analyze combined estimator/controller dynamics, stress omitted dynamics and disturbance paths, distinguish nominal asymptotic tracking from finite-time constraints.
profiles.NEGATIVE_CASE: Rohrs etal 1985 source simulations show instability/parameter drift with specified omitted second-order dynamics and references/disturbances. Åström commentary disputes complete infinite gain explanation, highlighting insufficient excitation and curve drift.
profiles.FIXED_MODEL_CHEAP_PATH: Validated fixed conservative controller/robust envelope and adaptation freeze can be preferable when fresh data lack information. Preserve monitoring/reentry rather than mandatory learning.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Rohrs/Åström remain source-authored analytical and simulation evidence, not field incident statistics. Dual control was examined through CL031 primary mechanisms and limitations; original 1960s/1973 derivations and a broad safe-exploration survey were not independently inspected.
profiles.DUAL_CONTROL: Record joint physical/belief dynamics, objective, horizon and inference/planning approximation. CL031’s cautious controller may turn off learning; its dual approximation can favor useful future information. Neither optimal expected cost nor favorable simulated behavior supplies all-plants safety. A robust/fixed controller may remain the appropriate cheap path.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.INTERPRETATION: All parameters consistent with each residual lying in a known error set W and correct model class.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.BOUNDS_SOURCE: Physical/calibration bound or explicit assumption; data-estimated bound requires additional statistical treatment.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.CALIBRATION: Containment is deterministic conditional on valid support/class; no nominal confidence level.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.APPROXIMATION: Outer bounds preserve containment if constructed soundly but may be too conservative.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.FAILURE: Wrong bound/class may exclude truth or make intersection empty.

UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.INTERPRETATION: Procedure covers fixed true parameter with stated probability over repeated data (and algorithm randomization if present).
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.CALIBRATION: SPS exact 1−q/m under its assumptions; outer ellipsoid at least nominal. Asymptotic normal intervals are not automatically finite-sample exact.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.FAILURE: Dependent regressors/noises, selection or regime mismatch may invalidate it.

UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.INTERPRETATION: Posterior probability under prior and likelihood conditional on data.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.BOUNDS_SOURCE: Prior covariance/support, likelihood and hyperparameter treatment.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.CALIBRATION: Not generally repeated-sampling confidence under misspecification; CL015 posterior versus sandwich covariance.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.APPROXIMATION: Empirical Bayes plug-in, truncation and posterior approximation omit uncertainty unless accounted for.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.FAILURE: Narrow posterior can be confidently wrong or prior-determined along nonidentified directions.

UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.INTERPRETATION: Future output/closed loop property under specified candidate set and noise/process conditions.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.BOUNDS_SOURCE: Propagated parameter/structural uncertainty plus disturbance/initial state envelopes.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.CALIBRATION: A parameter region does not automatically bound nonlinear prediction or controller behavior.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.APPROXIMATION: Outer propagation can be conservative; local linearization can be unsound outside its domain.
UNCERTAINTY_OBJECTS.FAILURE: Omitted model classes, hidden modes or future regime changes.

profiles.STRUCTURAL_UNCERTAINTY: Keep multiple orders/structures or observationally equivalent candidates when data cannot discriminate. Conditional parameter uncertainty does not include omitted structure by default.
profiles.SENSITIVITY: Vary plausible priors, kernels, noise bounds, orders and observation maps; report whether downstream decision changes rather than averaging incompatible uncertainty meanings.
profiles.CONSUMER: A parameter interpreter, predictor or robust controller with specific tolerance/constraint; a wide valid set can be more honest than a narrow unjustified one.
profiles.CASE: XCL07 credible/confidence mismatch; XCL08 empty feasible set; CL018 deterministic containment versus stochastic shrinkage. ESI-RCA0070: delayed rolling-mill prediction under dynamic model uncertainty, with chronology limits.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Bounded primary mechanisms, negative results and a published physical-data case now cover hierarchy and averaging. No external target was assessed. No comprehensive hierarchical-model taxonomy, original BMA proof reconstruction, full MCMC convergence audit or independent prospective calibration was performed.
profiles.HIERARCHICAL_MODELS: Specify likelihood, conditional prior and hyperprior. Distinguish fixed hyperparameters, empirical-Bayes plug-in, joint MAP and posterior integration. CL032 integrates with adaptive Metropolis; CL033 optimizes a hierarchical Cholesky-cone model by alternating convex blocks. The latter does not supply integrated posterior uncertainty or guaranteed global optimization.
profiles.MODEL_AVERAGING: Choose a common target Δ; combine p(Δ|M_k,D) with weights proportional to marginal likelihood times model prior. Preserve within-model and between-model variation. Assess prior mass on redundant model neighborhoods, candidate omissions, numerical/subset approximation and model-class sensitivity. Do not average arbitrary state coordinates or incompatible parameters.
profiles.DYNAMIC_MODEL_AVERAGING: CL035 separately discounts coefficient information and model probabilities and predicts the same delayed output across candidates. ESI-RCA0070 is a physical-data example; full-data prior initialization and no independent deployment test bound its payoff evidence.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.VALIDITY_ENVELOPE: Model class/structure, observation map, calibration/timebase, data interval, input ensemble, controller, operating regime, consumer/loss and algorithm version.

CHANGE_TYPES.PARAMETER_DRIFT: May be tracked under rate/information bounds.
CHANGE_TYPES.STRUCTURAL_CHANGE: Wrong dimension/mode/class may invalidate a fixed-class tracker.
CHANGE_TYPES.OBSERVATION_CHANGE: Calibration/clock/filtering changes can alter data semantics with unchanged plant.
CHANGE_TYPES.POLICY_CHANGE: Changes feedback and excitation; old inference assumptions may fail.
CHANGE_TYPES.PURPOSE_CHANGE: Different horizon/tail risk/controller can require new fidelity.
CHANGE_TYPES.REPRESENTATION_CHANGE: Invertible coordinate change can preserve behavior despite different bytes.

profiles.FRESHNESS_EVIDENCE: Relevant residual/change observations plus supported dependency continuity; not elapsed time or a recent fit timestamp alone.
profiles.ONLINE_UPDATE_MECHANISM: RLS forgetting trades old information for responsiveness; directional selective forgetting protects unrefreshed directions but boundedness is not truth. GREAT tracks subspaces under assumptions 1–4.
profiles.TRACKING_GUARANTEE_LIMITS: GREAT requires bounded errors, bounded chordal drift, sufficient projected signal singular values, close initialization and compatible steps/window/iterations. These involve unknown true quantities and need independent justification.
profiles.REUSE_RULE: Preserve conclusions unaffected by change, transport evidence through a justified correspondence, or revalidate affected claims. Replacing all evidence after every edit is unnecessary.
profiles.INVALIDATION_SIGNALS: Sensor/clock change, reference/control change, unexplained relevant residuals, loss of excitation, drift bound violation, new structure or consumer.
profiles.CHEAP_PATH: Freeze an adequate model, monitor material premises and update on evidence. A stable model may remain valid indefinitely within a maintained envelope.
profiles.RETIREMENT: No remaining consumer; unsupported required premise; replacement offers adequate lower cost; or update policy has no marginal benefit.
profiles.CASE: XCL09 unchanged bytes/wrong units and coordinate change/preserved behavior; XCL10 noise variance floor.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Semantic currentness is researcher synthesis; currentness monitoring was not empirically evaluated in a live organization.

profiles.CLAIM: Specify one-step forecast, free simulation, frequency band approximation, mechanistic interpretation, intervention or closed loop stability; no single score settles all.
profiles.TRAIN_VALIDATION_PARTITION: Record data used for fitting, order/kernel/tuning, feature construction and evaluation; independence must match statistical protocol rather than be presumed from filenames.
profiles.INDEPENDENCE_ASSUMPTIONS: Temporal dependence matters; ordinary CV can be valid for appropriately specified autoregression under CL023 conditions. Future-derived features or changed policies can still invalidate evaluation.
profiles.NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: Known constant/simple baseline; fit shuffled irrelevant channels where appropriate; alternative equivalent mechanism; fixed model against continuous refit; wrong horizon comparison. These are proposed controls, not performed user experiments.
profiles.METRICS: Loss/horizon in consumer units, calibration/coverage, free-run error, input-residual dependence, frequency response repeats and constraint violations when relevant.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Confidence/test power, multiple comparisons/model selection and regime distribution; nonrejection of residual correlation does not prove independence.
profiles.COUNTEREXAMPLE_SEARCH: Change excitation amplitude/distribution, probe weak directions, test sensor/clock changes, simulate omitted modes or compare long horizon behavior.
profiles.ACCEPTANCE_LIMITS: Prespecified tolerance and scope; observe failures rather than redefining the target after results; finite evidence supports finite/qualified claims.
profiles.CASE: XCL11 one-step versus 100-step divergence; CL014 BLA ensemble dependence.
profiles.CHEAP_PATH: A small targeted falsification test may be more useful than a large generic dashboard; added validation burden needs a consumer.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Primary method theory and analytical cases; no actual target validation or universal best split method established.

profiles.GUARANTEE_SIGNATURE: Subject/target, model class, algorithm, observation map, sample count/horizon, norm, probability space, conditioning, quantifiers, premises and implementation approximation.
profiles.ASSUMPTION_WITNESSES: Each premise marked observed/derived/assumed/unknown/contradicted, with source or measurement. A theorem does not verify its own plant/noise premises.
MATERIAL_EXAMPLES: SPS: exact finite coverage over data and algorithm randomization under independent symmetric noise and deterministic full rank regressors; outer ellipse conservative.
Simchowitz 2018: fully observed states, zero initial state, iid isotropic Gaussian noise, spectral radius≤1,finite-time Gramian/sample condition.
Li 2024: correct known bounded-noise support gives deterministic containment; iid bounded noise, excitation and tight bound premises give stochastic diameter shrinkage.
Ziemann tutorial theorem 5.3: Markov-parameter error under predictor/noise/excitation conditions; not physical state identification.
Camlibel 2025: shortest experiment for exact minimal LTI data with order/lag bounds and admissible input choices; not noisy safe online experiment.
GREAT: bounded measurement errors/drift, information and close initialization yield deterministic tracking tube; noise-free stationary case yields convergence.
profiles.OBSERVATION_IMPLEMENTATION_BRIDGE: Check sensor/time semantics, delivered input, numerical tolerances, filter/horizon/order changes and whether approximation preserves the analyzed algorithm.
profiles.EVALUATION: PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/INAPPLICABLE are separate for model and external claim. A missing premise is UNKNOWN transfer, not theorem false.
profiles.CHEAP_PATH: State a bounded empirical claim when mathematical premises cannot be supported; avoid pretending no useful decision is possible without a theorem.
profiles.EVIDENCE_LIMIT: Selected theorem sections inspected, not all proofs reproduced. Abstract-only frontier papers are discovery gaps, not load bearing guarantees.

profiles.DECISION: The specific action, ranking, forecast or constraint check the model changes.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY_BEFORE_AFTER: Use comparable target uncertainty under each method; do not compare credible interval width to deterministic feasible width as if equivalent.
profiles.TOTAL_COST: Instrumentation, experiments, operating disruption, computation, expert interpretation, validation, maintenance and wrong decisions; record cost units and unmeasured components.
profiles.CONSEQUENCES: Prediction error, controller instability, unnecessary intervention or missed drift according to actual consumer; average fit alone is not benefit.
profiles.COMPARATOR: Direct measurement, lookup table, scalar gain, band FRF, fixed robust model, existing documentation, compatible-model set or no additional model.
profiles.REUSE_HORIZON: Time/regimes/decisions over which construction cost can be amortized; changes in semantics may shorten it.
profiles.RETIREMENT_RULE: Stop refitting or retire model when no consumer remains, marginal decision value is unsupported, or cheaper adequate alternative exists; preserve monitoring for reentry.
profiles.OBJECTIVE_CONSTRAINT_AUTHORITY_LIMIT: A model can rank decisions within stipulated objective/constraints without validating whether those objectives are appropriate or actions authorized.
profiles.CASE: C0020/XCL10 reject mandatory continuous refit; C0001 allows weakest adequate model.

profiles.NAME: Language and behavioral model learning under explicit information access

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: An identification claim must be indexed by target class, available information and success criterion; changing any of these can change learnability.
No-counterexample evidence inherits the test domain or sampling assumptions; it becomes exact equivalence only with the additional completeness and target-in-domain argument.
Learning must account for the actual state-start and observation process; an assumed reset can be replaced only by a mechanism whose own access assumptions are justified.
An abstraction is adequate only for a stated observable claim; symbolic predicates and registers address different data distinctions and retain theory-specific learnability limits.
The model, observation and guarantee must use matching timing/nondeterminism/probability semantics; an extension removes only the limitation it explicitly addresses.

For LLM output h, task t, reference/oracle o, evaluation E, use d, this profile makes explicit the target language/model, presentation and actual query or state-access contract. Apply it only to the property’s stated claim and ceiling: Task-specific published experiments with documented limitations; no universal or timeless LLM capability judgment.

profiles.APPLICATION_STATUS: No user target or production system evaluated by this research. Source cases and constructed discriminators are labeled.

TARGET_CLASS.FOUNDATION: Regular languages represented by DFAs; finite reactive deterministic behavior represented by Mealy or Moore machines. Moore output-on-state and Mealy output-on-transition conventions must be normalized before comparing observations. This lane did not independently reconstruct every conversion proof.
TARGET_CLASS.RICHER_CLASSES: Symbolic finite automata over effective Boolean algebras; finite-register automata over specified data theories; output-determined I/O automata; partial nondeterministic IOTS; Mealy machines with timers; stochastic Mealy machines. These are distinct assumption packages, not a common unbounded learner.

QUERY_OR_DATA_MODEL.PASSIVE: Gold distinguishes positive text, informants and other naming/presentation regimes; finite positive/negative RPNI data and state-merging are a separate passive route. BH037 was available only at publisher abstract level, so characteristic-sample details are not certified here.
QUERY_OR_DATA_MODEL.ACTIVE: Angluin uses membership and exact equivalence queries with counterexamples. Observation tables enforce closure/consistency; discrimination/classification trees organize distinguishing experiments in later learners. Their data structure changes query efficiency, not the physical truth of answers.
QUERY_OR_DATA_MODEL.PRACTICAL: An interface called equivalence may run finite W/Wp/HSI-style tests, random walks or other counterexample search; its negative result retains those limits.

ALPHABET.FINITE: Alphabet choice is part of target definition. A TLS message symbol may hide cryptographic parameters and unmodeled variants.
ALPHABET.SYMBOLIC: Symbolic guards partition large/infinite current-input domains; alphabet predicate learnability is a separate assumption.
ALPHABET.REGISTER: Registers retain prior data values and enable equality/order-dependent behavior. A symbolic predicate over the current input alone is not an equivalent memory model.

CONTENT.RESET_ASSUMPTIONS: Membership from a distinguished initial state requires a justified reset/restart contract. Rivest–Schapire provides a no-reset probabilistic result using homing and strong connectivity, generally retaining a counterexample teacher. Without those access properties a run may become trapped in a terminal component. A reset-free theorem does not prove unrestricted black-box recovery.
CONTENT.OBSERVATION_NOISE: Deterministic learners require consistent answers under their abstraction. Timeouts, packet loss, scheduling and persistent state can introduce apparent or real nondeterminism. Nondeterministic and stochastic learners require their own output-coverage or sampling premises; silently choosing the majority answer changes the target.
CONTENT.ORACLE_QUALITY: Exact MAT answers are mathematical premises. Fault-domain completeness additionally needs the actual implementation to belong to the domain. Statistical tests yield distribution/test-specific claims. Incomplete-output IOTS produces table-relative under/over approximations. Unknown teacher quality remains UNKNOWN.

TERMINATION_AND_IDENTIFICATION_GUARANTEE.GUARANTEE: Identification in the limit is eventual stable correctness for an admissible presentation, not a known finite stopping certificate. Superfinite-class nonidentifiability is tied to the stated text/naming regime.

Exact regular-language learning with polynomial learner/query complexity in minimal state count and longest counterexample, conditional on exact answers; sampling replacement gives epsilon/delta relative to the chosen fixed distribution.

SLλ finite-index register learning uses MAT/tree-query assumptions; theorem7 complexity counts oracle activity and is theory dependent. Efficient comparison over a learned model does not certify a live target.

CONTENT.PRACTICAL_COUNTEREXAMPLE_SEARCH: Record tested sequence lengths, access sets, bounds, reset counts, random seeds/distribution and budgets. Vaandrager–Melse shows that no finite suite certifies arbitrary unrestricted complete deterministic Mealy behavior, and defines k-A fault domains for conditional completeness. An untested late divergence remains possible outside the domain.
CONTENT.COST: Learner CPU, number and length of queries, resets, transport/timeouts, experiment effects and human mapper/oracle work differ. SLλ live MbedTLS exploration was interrupted after three weeks without convergence; the comparative results relearned 24 intermediate hypotheses with a white-box model checker.

STATUS_DISTINCTION.LEARNED_MODEL: A hypothesis fitted to the available answers under a declared class.
STATUS_DISTINCTION.CONFORMANCE_TESTED_MODEL: A hypothesis with explicit bounded test evidence or a conditional completeness theorem.
STATUS_DISTINCTION.VERIFIED_INTENDED_SPECIFICATION: Requires a normative source and a proof/test argument for its formal interpretation; learning alone supplies neither.

CONTENT.IDENTIFIABILITY_AND_NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: When hypotheses remain observationally equivalent under permitted queries, report the equivalence class or a separating experiment. Do not infer source-code identity, unique architecture or internal beliefs from language equivalence.
CONTENT.NON_TRIGGER: For a single historical incident, recorded trace replay can satisfy the consumer without learning a complete machine.

profiles.NAME: Protocol/API models bound to a harness, version and permitted experiments

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: Learning must account for the actual state-start and observation process; an assumed reset can be replaced only by a mechanism whose own access assumptions are justified.
A protocol reconstruction is bound to the implementation/version, role, configuration, reachable state, observation map and authorized effects actually investigated.

profiles.APPLICATION_STATUS: No user target or production system evaluated by this research. Source cases and constructed discriminators are labeled.

CONTENT.IDENTIFICATION_TARGET: Externally observable behavior of a specified implementation role, version and configuration through a declared harness. The protocol name alone does not identify the target.
CONTENT.EXPERIMENT_AUTHORITY: Before active use, establish permission for the particular messages, authentication context, accounts, resets, resource use and persistent effects. This is the present engineering authority boundary, not a right conferred by a learning theorem. This research performed no probes against third-party systems.
CONTENT.STATE_LIFECYCLE: Distinguish socket/session, process, device/account/database and external-service state. The TLS case launches fresh clients and manages server sessions; it also performs an initial ClientHello outside the visible learner alphabet in one harness path. A process restart does not establish restoration of every external state.
CONTENT.OBSERVATION_AND_ABSTRACTION_MAP: Record concrete message construction, cryptographic state, parameter abstraction, output parsing, response window and quiescence convention. In BH011, Empty is the result of a harness timeout selected between 100 and 1500 ms; it does not establish permanent protocol silence.
CONTENT.PASSIVE_AND_ACTIVE_RELATION: Passive API traces expose observed usage and selection bias, as in X11/Perracotta mining. Active TLS exploration can test unusual orderings but is limited by its mapper, initial state and permitted input sequences. More active access does not supply normative intent.
CONTENT.EXPLORATION_COVERAGE: BH011 studied nine implementations in the selected TLS1.0/1.2 roles/configurations listed in its Table1. Its modified bounded conformance procedure and runtime results apply to those harnesses. Hidden handshakes, concurrency, persistent authentication, unsupported message families and versions remain outside any stronger blanket claim.
CONTENT.EFFECT_BOUNDARIES: Treat connect/retry/reset and API actions as operations with effects. For a shadow model, explicitly compare dependencies, timing and persistent state with production; fidelity is an evidence obligation, not inferred from having a simulator.
CONTENT.VERSION_BINDING: Bind implementation/library version, protocol options, build flags, server/client role, harness/map and test date. Renew the claim when any influences the observed language.
CONTENT.VALIDATION: Separate learner consistency, repeated harness checks, bounded conformance tests and independent violation validation. BH011 reports three security flaws across selected GnuTLS, JSSE and OpenSSL implementations; that success neither proves all learned transitions correct nor generalizes to all protocol implementations.
CONTENT.REMAINING_UNCERTAINTY: Asynchronous responses, concurrent clients, retries, unobservable transitions and state outside reset control can invalidate a deterministic model. Protocol state learning is often a deliberately restricted view.
CONTENT.CHEAPER_COMPARATORS: A documented contract plus a few discriminating examples, a recorded incident trace, or a targeted conformance test may answer a narrow API question with less intervention than full exploration.

profiles.NAME: Mined regularities as hypotheses with independent promotion conditions

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: A finite-trace regularity is a candidate with stated language and coverage; universal invariant status requires an additional sound argument under explicit program/environment assumptions.
Promoting a reconstructed behavior into a requirement, acceptance criterion or permissible action requires an identifiable independent normative basis and a checked interpretation of it.

For LLM output h, task t, reference/oracle o, evaluation E, use d, this profile makes explicit the candidate-rule language, evidence scope and independent intended-rule authority. Apply it only to the property’s stated claim and ceiling: Task-specific published experiments with documented limitations; no universal or timeless LLM capability judgment.

profiles.APPLICATION_STATUS: No user target or production system evaluated by this research. Source cases and constructed discriminators are labeled.

CONTENT.CANDIDATE_LANGUAGE: Daikon searches chosen predicates over instrumented values; temporal miners select automata or pattern templates. The candidate grammar, program points and event vocabulary define what can be discovered. A missing rule may reflect trace coverage or an unavailable template, not absence of the intended rule.
CONTENT.EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Finite executions and traces, instrumentation and selected programs/tests. Static evidence may prove/refute a dynamic candidate or supply complementary relations, but this lane’s detailed evidence is strongest for dynamic and temporal mining; it does not present an exhaustive static-miner genealogy.
CONTENT.COVERAGE: Record executed contexts and unobserved branches, input populations, successful/failing runs, filtering and event projections. Daikon’s array-length regularity from selected test ranges illustrates accidental invariants. Perracotta failed to recover seven selected SDV rules because of coverage and five because of pattern limits.
CONTENT.INFERENCE_METHOD: Daikon instantiates templates and discards falsified candidates with statistical/other filters. Ammons et al. combine trace projection, probabilistic finite-state learning and a core extractor that prunes rare behavior. Perracotta accepts imperfect patterns at a threshold and applies heuristic/manual filtering. Frequency can prioritize investigation but does not establish correctness.

HYPOTHESIS_STATUS.FINITE_REGULARITY: All observed mapped executions satisfy p; quantifier is the available trace set.
HYPOTHESIS_STATUS.LIKELY_INVARIANT: A candidate retained by the selected inference/filtering method. Its confidence is not a calibrated probability of universal program correctness.
HYPOTHESIS_STATUS.UNIVERSAL_INVARIANT: Requires an independent proof in a specified program/model semantics, with assumptions and proof status.
HYPOTHESIS_STATUS.INTENDED_RULE: Requires an independently grounded obligation or accepted intent; even a proof that code satisfies p does not make p desirable.

CONTENT.VALIDATION: Preserve falsifiers and failed candidates. Check new executions, independent requirements and, where possible, static/formal arguments. Human/expert review must expose its own scope and disagreements rather than being called an infallible oracle.
CONTENT.OBSERVED_VERSUS_INTENDED: A common defect can be accurately mined. BH007’s pooled X11 traces did not recover the intended ICCCM timestamp rule until expert filtering/selection; this is a concrete normative-contamination case. Perracotta’s JTA interaction diagram is explicitly not itself a prescriptive specification.
PROMOTION_CONDITIONS: Identify the normative source, its scope/version and interpretation authority.
Map the intended clause to the candidate and record alternatives; introduce independently judged acceptance/rejection examples.
Use tests/proof to assess implementation conformance to that interpreted rule.
Retain dissent, proof failure and unknown coverage as distinct statuses.
CONTENT.COST_AND_EVIDENCE: Cable evaluated 17 specifications using 90 traces of 72 X11 programs and reduced user decisions in its concept-analysis traversal relative to per-trace review. An author supplied expert labels; the comparison is not a multi-participant total-time or maintenance-cost study. Perracotta reduced 7611 rules to 142 heuristically and then 56 manually judged useful; not reviewing all candidates leaves missed-useful-rule uncertainty.
CONTENT.NON_TRIGGER: An existing trusted rule with a direct test does not need to be rediscovered from usage frequency. For descriptive usage analytics, normative promotion need not occur.
