profiles.NAME: Task-scoped artifact reconstruction and reflexion discrepancies

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: A reconstruction should preserve which artifact supports each relation, its version and extraction semantics, and unresolved conflict between intended, implemented and observed views.
A reflexion model is useful when its discrepancies are interpreted relative to the high-level view, extracted relation and mapping; an absence is not automatically a missing implementation feature.
Candidate rejected: a single recovered graph can be treated as a complete universal account of a software/organizational system merely because it is explicit and internally consistent.

profiles.APPLICATION_STATUS: No user target or production system evaluated by this research. Source cases and constructed discriminators are labeled.

CONTENT.SOURCES: Source code, binary, generated code, build graph, configuration, logs, deployment inventory, tests, documentation and interviews are possible evidence classes; actual coverage must enumerate what is available. Chikofsky–Cross distinguishes analysis/recovery from reengineering alteration and design recovery’s use of domain/external knowledge.
CONTENT.FRESHNESS: Every artifact/extractor/map binds to a version and environment. Repository source, deployed binary and current feature flags may differ. This lane did not inspect a user repository or infer facts about one.
CONTENT.CORRESPONDENCE: State what each edge means: lexical reference, possible call, build dependency, observed interaction or intended relation. Resolve names and generated/deployed entities explicitly. Static possibility is not observed execution; an absent runtime observation is not impossibility.
CONTENT.CONFLICTS: Keep intended architecture, implemented structure, observed execution and researcher abstraction separate. If artifacts disagree, record alternative explanations such as stale documentation, an unused branch, extractor loss or genuine drift; do not simply select the easiest source.
CONTENT.INFERRED_STRUCTURE: A reflexion view takes high-level relation H, extracted source relation S and map m. R=m(S); convergences are R∩H, divergences R−H, absences H−R. This exact set result does not determine the intended semantics. Unmapped functions can manufacture apparent absences.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY: Reflection, dynamic loading, plugins, generated code, conditional compilation, feature flags and distributed ownership can leave relations unobserved or outside a static extractor. The resulting graph may still be useful for a bounded question.
CONTENT.VALIDATION: Inspect contributing source tuples and independently selected slices; review semantic differences with relevant experts. Architecture recovery comparisons need a reference architecture and metric domain. BH014 explicitly allows multiple legitimate architectures; BH015 shows severe metric pathologies if element universes or graph structures violate assumptions.
CONTENT.INTENDED_CONSUMER: An engineer tracing an architectural discrepancy, planning a change or finding relevant code. NetBSD’s virtual-memory slice in the reflexion study intentionally excluded unrelated I/O; its boundedness is part of the method’s usefulness.
CONTENT.COST_AND_COMPARATOR: Compare a caller/dependency list or manually checked slice with a full recovery effort. Small mapping specifications and fast computations in BH005 do not measure all engineer interpretation/maintenance time. A complete universal system graph is rejected as an unqualified adoption promise.

profiles.NAME: Process logs and situated practice as different evidence domains

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: Promoting a reconstructed behavior into a requirement, acceptance criterion or permissible action requires an identifiable independent normative basis and a checked interpretation of it.
Candidate rejected: a single recovered graph can be treated as a complete universal account of a software/organizational system merely because it is explicit and internally consistent.
A discovered process model inherits event semantics, case/object association, timing and missingness assumptions; a log is evidence of recording, not automatically all real work or required policy.
Process-model quality is a purpose-relative vector; one fit/complexity score cannot establish the model’s suitability for prediction, diagnosis or conformance.
A representation of human work must retain perspective, elicitation conditions, interpretive limits and the separate authority needed to intervene or impose it as an obligation.

profiles.APPLICATION_STATUS: No user target or production system evaluated by this research. Source cases and constructed discriminators are labeled.

CONTENT.WHOSE_BEHAVIOR_IS_REPRESENTED: Process discovery represents recorded events under chosen case/object semantics. Suchman’s 1985 copier study represents particular pairs of first-time users in a situated task, observed by video and transcript. ACTA represents selected experts’ elicited cognitive demands in specific tasks. None is a complete account of all organizational members or internal mental states.
CONTENT.WHOSE_PERSPECTIVE_IS_MISSING: Unlogged work, nonparticipants, alternative departments/roles, unsuccessful or excluded cases, and observers unable to see interactions outside the apparatus. Record which omissions are known and which are unknown.
CONTENT.EVENT_SEMANTICS: Distinguish event identity, activity label, occurrence time, recording time, case/object association and selection. A log can omit invisible work or duplicate a shared event when flattened into case-centric traces. Object-centric models preserve multiple associations but do not recover unrecorded work automatically.
CONTENT.FORMAL_PROCESS_BOUNDARY: The alpha-algorithm recovery theorem is conditional on a sound structured workflow-net class, its completeness definition and exclusions including short loops. It is not a theorem that arbitrary enterprise logs uniquely identify a real process. Object-centric examples in BH019 are constructed illustrations, not a company field evaluation.
CONTENT.QUALITY_TRADEOFF: Fitness, precision, generalization and simplicity answer different questions. A flower model can fit all observed traces while admitting too much; memorization can fit a log while generalizing poorly. A consumer’s loss and purpose must determine acceptable tradeoffs.
CONTENT.MEASUREMENT_AND_ELICITATION_LIMITS: Suchman’s matrix contrasts actions available to human observers with the narrower machine-observable subset; plans serve as resources for situated action rather than complete executable accounts. ACTA’s task diagram, knowledge audit and simulation interview reveal cognitive demands, but its streamlined method loses some detail and its small evaluation did not establish exhaustive elicitation or reliability of every elicited item.
CONTENT.EMPIRICAL_DESCRIPTION_VS_INTERPRETATION_: A record of occurrences is descriptive; selecting categories and explaining work is interpretive; agreeing a process is negotiated rule-making; enforcing it requires separate institutional authority. A diagram or log-conformance score cannot convert these statuses.
CONTENT.INTERVENTION_LEGITIMACY: Recording/model deployment may change visibility, incentives or work practice. Authority, affected perspectives and contestability must be assessed for the actual intended use. The primary organizational-politics follow-up Suchman 1995 was located only at abstract/bibliographic level, so this lane does not claim a complete historical account of institutional agency from that source.
CONTENT.RECENT_RESPONSE: BH036 adds object-centric quality categories and relationships and uses one real-data applicability assessment plus six purposively sampled practitioner/vendor interviews. Respondents report ignore/proactive/reactive/unfixable strategies. This supports issue relevance and practice diversity, not a controlled effectiveness estimate.
CONTENT.NON_TRIGGER: Where a narrow machine interface is the only claim, do not invent an organizational model. Where participants contest meanings, an explicit unresolved account may be preferable to premature executable enforcement.

TRANSFORMATION_STAGES.LOST_OR_INTRODUCED: Model class, priors, thresholds and unseen behavior assumptions; several hypotheses may fit equally.

CONTENT.PRESERVED_CLAIM: State preservation relation locally at each step; compose only if the codomain/domain and assumptions match. I/O-to-Mealy semantic correspondence is proved for output-determined and other specified classes, not for arbitrary asynchronous systems.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY: Keep alternative event labels, competing automata and unresolved meanings when available evidence does not discriminate. Compression or category normalization can make an ambiguous source look falsely definite.
CONTENT.ROUND_TRIP_LIMIT: A lossless OCEL/XML/JSON serialization can restore fields; it cannot reverse an inferred case interpretation, recover unlogged work or reconstruct a discarded alternative. A graph serialization round-trip is not semantic preservation.
CONTENT.COUNTEREXAMPLE: CONSTRUCTED: two orders share one shipment event; flattening duplicates it and a mined sequence appears to show two shipments. An explicit object/event relation resolves that particular ambiguity, while unrecorded manual handling remains unknown. EMPIRICAL FRONTIER: ATLAS prunes/compresses external action models; those transformations do not identify an agent’s internal belief states.

PROPERTY_SPECIFIC_DEPENDENCE.DEPENDENCE: An identification claim must be indexed by target class, available information and success criterion; changing any of these can change learnability.
No-counterexample evidence inherits the test domain or sampling assumptions; it becomes exact equivalence only with the additional completeness and target-in-domain argument.
An abstraction is adequate only for a stated observable claim; symbolic predicates and registers address different data distinctions and retain theory-specific learnability limits.
The model, observation and guarantee must use matching timing/nondeterminism/probability semantics; an extension removes only the limitation it explicitly addresses.
A finite-trace regularity is a candidate with stated language and coverage; universal invariant status requires an additional sound argument under explicit program/environment assumptions.

For graph G, claimed universe U, extraction e, external witnesses W, this profile makes explicit the guarantee target, quantified assumptions, correspondence and withheld promotion. Apply it only to the property’s stated claim and ceiling: Analytical rejection of the universal promise supported by formal/empirical counterexamples; no claim that all graphs are useless.

Each material transformation must state its source/target bearer, transformation kind, preserved claim, introduced assumptions and loss; serialization reversibility alone does not establish semantic fidelity.
Candidate rejected: an LLM interface can be treated as an exact behavioral/semantic oracle or a generally faithful automatic system reconstructor without independent validation.
Modeling effort should be justified by the decision it improves and the actual comparator; measured local query/label savings must not be promoted to unmeasured total lifecycle benefit.

GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: Eventual stable correct hypothesis on every admissible presentation when the class/result permits it

GUARANTEES.TARGET: Error measure under a fixed sampling distribution
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Match distribution and error notion to the consumer; do not relabel distributional agreement as universal equivalence.

GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: For every M in F, agreement on complete T implies equivalence
GUARANTEES.REGIME: Finite suite with potentially large cost
GUARANTEES.ACCESS: Reliable reset/output and established M in F
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Provide the missing target-domain membership premise; test-suite completeness alone is insufficient.

GUARANTEES.TARGET: IOTS output behavior on the table-related trace scope
GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: Under/overapproximation under selected ioco relation and completeness information
GUARANTEES.ACCESS: Output/completeness queries; repetition bounds need assumptions
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Do not inflate table-relative inclusion into global model equality.

GUARANTEES.TARGET: Conditional output distributions under sampled contexts
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Zero observations can be compatible through lack of information; that is not evidence of equal distributions.

GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: The theorem’s race-avoiding symbolic/concrete query assumptions
GUARANTEES.REGIME: Finite query algorithm; factorial timer dependence
GUARANTEES.ACCESS: Concrete realization and equivalence testing needed beyond symbolic prototype
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Prototype used symbolic queries and model equivalence; noisy live timing requires a new implementation/evidence argument.

GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: Recovery under the complete-log definition and class restrictions
GUARANTEES.ACCESS: Correct event/case semantics and hidden/duplicate/short-loop restrictions
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Establish net class/log premises; arbitrary enterprise logs do not inherit the theorem.

GUARANTEES.TARGET: Reflexion set partition for supplied H,S,m
GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: Every finite relation tuple in those inputs
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: Semantic adequacy of the view/map is separate from calculation correctness.

GUARANTEES.KIND: Common supervisory controller from DES data
GUARANTEES.TARGET: All deterministic finite plants consistent with positive and known-impossible negative strings
GUARANTEES.QUANTIFIERS: One supervisor enforces prefix(K_D) for all consistent plants, under theorem premises
GUARANTEES.REGIME: Finite language data, known alphabet/control partition; all states marked
GUARANTEES.ACCESS: Reliable positive/negative labels, nonempty K_D=prefix(D) intersect E
GUARANTEES.TRANSFER_OBLIGATION: The uncontrollable-extension test uses prefix(K_D), not K_D. More data can also change K_D and therefore the target obligation. Nonblocking/partial observation and real experiment permission are not supplied.

CONTENT.TRANSFER_RULE: No total confidence ordering compares these guarantees. Match the bearer, quantifiers, data generation, oracle/access and decision. A proof over a model certifies that model-level claim, with correspondence to a live target as a separate obligation.

UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.CLASS_UNCERTAINTY: Whether the target is representable in the chosen DFA/register/timed/process class.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.OBSERVATIONAL_UNCERTAINTY: Hidden state, timing, reset, missing events, mapper ambiguity and mislabeled traces.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.STATISTICAL_UNCERTAINTY: Sampling variation under a specified probability model; state any interval/test assumptions.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.ORACLE_UNCERTAINTY: Whether a teacher answer or claimed completeness premise is correct.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.INTERPRETIVE_UNCERTAINTY: Meaning of recovered relations, labels or participant accounts.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.NORMATIVE_UNCERTAINTY: Which requirement or authority governs desired behavior.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.CURRENTNESS_UNCERTAINTY: Whether evidence remains bound to the present implementation/environment.
UNCERTAINTY_CLASSES.DECISION_UNCERTAINTY: Whether remaining model error can change the downstream choice.

CONTENT.CALIBRATION: A statistical compatibility test or Angluin’s sampling theorem has a local probabilistic meaning. Dynamic-invariant confidence, LLM verbal certainty, test nonfailure and human plausibility are not automatically calibrated probabilities of semantic correctness.
CONTENT.MISSINGNESS: MISSING means a needed value was not supplied; UNKNOWN means the question cannot be resolved from available evidence; INAPPLICABLE means the actual scope makes the question irrelevant. None is interchangeable with FAIL or probability zero.
CONTENT.COUNTEREXAMPLE: In the stochastic learning source, zero observed outcomes may be considered compatible because there is insufficient evidence. Reporting compatibility as demonstrated equality reverses the epistemic meaning.
CONTENT.REPRESENTATION: Prefer a vector of typed uncertainty and explicit alternative candidates to one opaque confidence score. A finite output-set bound, a theorem premise and an unresolved authority dispute must remain distinguishable.
CONTENT.NEXT_DISCRIMINATORS: Obtain a reset-sensitive trace, a concrete value crossing an abstraction boundary, a missing event/object association, an independent requirement clause or a genuinely held-out environment according to the active uncertainty. Collecting more of the same uninformative traces may not help.

CONTENT.VALID_TIME: Bind claims to target, build, configuration, environment, observation window, model version, mapper/extractor, reset mechanism and normative source version where relevant. A file timestamp alone is not enough to establish validity.
CONTENT.INVALIDATION_DEPENDENCIES: An implementation change can invalidate traces; a mapper change can invalidate labels and inferred states; an oracle/test-domain change can invalidate a conformance conclusion; an intent change can invalidate acceptance rules without changing observed behavior. A source-only edit irrelevant to the modeled slice may not require complete relearning if irrelevance is established.
VALIDATION_LEVELS: Finite observation consistency with retained counterexamples.
Independent or held-out behavior under a declared sampling/coverage design.
Decision outcome comparison with acquisition, correction and maintenance costs.
CONTENT.FALSIFICATION: A reliable in-scope differing trace can refute equivalence or a candidate invariant. A missing trace does not refute a universal claim by itself; neither does it establish the claim. Checker timeout/proof-search failure is UNKNOWN absent an actual counterexample.
CONTENT.FRONTIER_BOUNDARIES: Register-learning model relearning and synthetic stochastic protocol models are not live-target external validation. FormalBench variants improve semantic robustness checks but do not supply an audit of model-training contamination. ATLAS tests new runs in the same 12 environments. ArchAgent uses documentation/expert judgments whose completeness is not independently established.
CONTENT.RENEWAL_RULE: Re-enter validation when a changed dependency could alter the claim or consumer decision. Preserve the older evidence/version instead of overwriting it as if current. Retire the model when no consumer or obligation justifies its renewal cost.
CONTENT.FOUR_VALUED_VERDICT: PASS is only at the stated claim/evidence scope; FAIL requires a concrete contradiction or violated necessary premise for that asserted claim; UNKNOWN preserves unresolved premises; INAPPLICABLE requires a false applicability guard. Every property predicate has its own operational meanings.

CONTENT.DECISION: Examples are finding a safety violation, locating an architectural discrepancy, extracting a useful API rule or deciding a process intervention. Define the consumer before choosing full identification, a partial model or no added artifact.
CONTENT.UNCERTAINTY_BEFORE_AND_AFTER: State which live alternatives can change the decision. More graph nodes or a higher fit score need not remove a decision-relevant alternative. One replayed counterexample can settle a rejection decision while full equivalence remains unknown.
CONTENT.TOTAL_COST: Acquisition/instrumentation, mapper construction, experiments and resets, compute/query costs, expert review, correcting false candidates, interpretation, version renewal, and downstream losses from wrong decisions. Missing human repair or maintenance costs are UNKNOWN, not zero.
CONTENT.CONSEQUENCES: False assurance can be more costly than an explicit unknown. Conversely, exhaustive reconstruction can consume resources without changing the action. The objective/constraint/authority governing a decision is not validated merely because a model ranks options.
CONTENT.COMPARATORS: A recorded example, lookup table, direct measurement, targeted test, existing specification, bounded slice, partial hypothesis or no new machinery. Compare on the same decision, acceptable error/effect limits and lifecycle horizon.

CONTENT.REUSE_HORIZON: Estimate how many decisions and versions will reuse the representation. A maintained contract may pay off over many changes; a one-time incident can be better served by a trace and explanation.
CONTENT.RETIREMENT_RULE: Retire or reduce the representation when no named consumer/obligation remains, when a cheaper adequate substitute preserves the protected decision, or when renewal costs exceed justified benefit. Re-entry follows a new material uncertainty or obligation.
CONTENT.CEREMONY_DISPOSITION: Reject mandatory explicit state-machine diagrams and complete universal graphs as unconditional prescriptions. Retain diagrams, graphs and formal models when a particular mechanism and consumer justify them.

It does not establish a general exact semantic reconstructor, zero-cost correction, independent normative authority or reliable transfer across arbitrary unseen production environments.

profiles.TITLE: Nonlinear model palette and operating-point choice

STRUCTURE.NARX: Finite histories of measured inputs/outputs passed to a nonlinear static function. Linear-in-parameter bases can simplify fitting, but finite history and output invertibility remain restrictions.
STRUCTURE.NARMAX: Extends nonlinear input/output parameterization with moving-average/noise terms. The 1984 report is a historical witness only here; its sufficient-condition proof was not read.
STRUCTURE.BLOCK_ORIENTED: Hammerstein places a static nonlinearity before linear dynamics; Wiener reverses that order. Sensor/actuator interpretations are possible but not guaranteed by topology alone. Parallel and feedback structures increase flexibility and estimation burden.
STRUCTURE.VOLTERRA_WIENER: Kernel expansions represent nonlinear memory; finite degree/memory and regularization trade truncation bias against rapidly growing parameters. The roadmap’s fading-memory approximation account is not a universal representation of arbitrary hysteresis/discontinuity.
STRUCTURE.NONLINEAR_STATE_SPACE: Can retain latent dynamic memory not exposed by a finite measured-output regressor; estimation and initialization are often nonconvex.

profiles.MODES: One local regime may suffice; saturation, contact and hysteresis can require additional structure or discrete modes.
profiles.LATENT_VARIABLES: Physical hidden states, encoder states and lag coordinates have different semantics; equivalence/anchor obligations are preserved.
profiles.OBSERVATION_CONDITIONS: Specify observed channels, input access, noise placement, sampling and whether measured outputs reset prediction.
profiles.IDENTIFIABILITY: Representation adequacy and informative trajectories are separate from optimizer convergence. A selected nonlinear family can remain observationally ambiguous.
profiles.OPTIMIZATION_LIMITATIONS: Joint structure/parameter selection and nonlinear stochastic likelihoods can have local minima; linear-in-coefficient subproblems do not remove dictionary bias.
profiles.PHYSICAL_CONSTRAINTS: Grey-box structure can reduce dimension but becomes a source of bias if approximated physics omits overflow, saturation or memory.
profiles.VALIDATION_BY_REGIME: Test declared amplitudes, frequencies, histories, mode boundaries and rollout horizons separately. Report unknown extrapolation rather than aggregate it away.
profiles.UNJUSTIFIED_GLOBAL_COMPLEXITY_EXAMPLE: A narrow stable operating point with a tolerance-satisfying linear baseline does not acquire value merely from a global neural model.
profiles.LINEARIZATION_ERASES_RELEVANT_FAILURE_EX: Pick-and-place impacts or cascaded-tank overflow can be precisely the transition needed for the decision; a local smooth approximation outside them is insufficient.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Roadmap synthesis plus selected benchmarks; no universal complexity ranking or all-NARMAX theorem inspection.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.TITLE: Switched dynamics, hidden modes and partially observed realizations
profiles.STRUCTURE: Distinguish arbitrary switched ARX, state/input-partitioned piecewise-affine models, jump-Markov models, and HMM-style stochastic latent processes.
profiles.MODES: Measured, inferred or stipulated labels; a fitted cluster is not necessarily a physical regime. FR004 specifically requires measured iid switching.
profiles.LATENT_VARIABLES: FR004 hides continuous state but observes switching; FR005 learns observable operators for hidden-state probabilities.
profiles.OBSERVATION_CONDITIONS: Mode logs and continuous measurements must be described separately; rank/conditioning and positive mode probabilities are material.
profiles.IDENTIFIABILITY: Realizations may be identifiable only up to similarity/permutation; hidden switching and state-triggered switching are outside FR004’s guarantee.
profiles.OPTIMIZATION_LIMITATIONS: Mode assignment, number, dynamics and partition estimation are coupled; noiseless algebraic results do not automatically cover noisy mode discovery.
profiles.PHYSICAL_CONSTRAINTS: Common quadratic contraction is a theorem hypothesis in FR004, not a generic synonym for practical stability.
profiles.VALIDATION_BY_REGIME: Report per-mode behavior, transitions and rare-mode coverage; validate output-sequence distributions at stated horizons for HMMs.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Conditional theorem and tutorial evidence. No mature universal hidden-mode finite-sample guarantee established by this branch.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.TITLE: Bayesian inverse recovery of dynamic quantities
profiles.NATIVE_TRADITION: Inverse problems and Bayesian analysis; imported into identification where the unknown dynamics/parameters enter a forward map.
profiles.INFERENCE_TARGET: Posterior measure or regularized solution over specified unknowns; target functional may be more identifiable than full state/parameter vector.
profiles.ASSUMPTIONS: Forward/potential regularity, prior support, noise model and discretization approximation; exact theorem hypotheses are not replaced by a generic Bayesian label.
profiles.OBSERVATIONAL_EQUIVALENCE: Nullspaces or multiple parameterizations can persist despite a unique penalized minimizer or stable posterior.
profiles.INTERVENTION_EVIDENCE: Not supplied by Bayesian well-posedness; additional experiment design or causal assumptions may be needed for action use.
UNSUPPORTED_EXTRAPOLATIONS: Stable posterior implies correct model class.
Regularization proves data-determined unique physical recovery.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: FR006 theoretical results concern the stipulated inverse model and metric.

profiles.TITLE: Observed-policy prediction and intervention targets
profiles.NATIVE_TRADITION: Causal graphical/structural modeling; related to control experiments but not identical to predictive system identification.
profiles.INFERENCE_TARGET: A specified intervention distribution or invariant mechanism, not merely P(output|observed input/history).
profiles.ASSUMPTIONS: Intervention definition, confounding/selection structure, measurement reliability and transport invariances.
profiles.OBSERVATIONAL_EQUIVALENCE: The two constructed X=U,Y=X and X=U,Y=U systems agree observationally but disagree under do(X=1).
profiles.INTERVENTION_EVIDENCE: Randomization, structural/graphical identification or other justified intervention evidence must be named; none is manufactured for a target agent.
UNSUPPORTED_EXTRAPOLATIONS: Prediction under a closed-loop policy proves validity after changing the policy.
External agent traces uniquely reveal beliefs or objectives.
ASIA is evidence identifying agent internals.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Pearl supplies causal semantics; agent-internal limitation is an analytical boundary, not a new empirical psychology claim.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.TITLE: SINDy and weak-form sparse discovery
profiles.REPRESENTATION: Sparse linear combination of candidate nonlinear functions in specified state/coordinate variables; weak variants fit integrated identities.
profiles.INDUCTIVE_BIAS: Few active dictionary terms, chosen coordinate simplicity, test-function smoothness and threshold/regularization preferences.
profiles.INFORMATION_REQUIREMENTS: Sufficiently informative measured state or justified latent reconstruction; derivative/integral accuracy; trajectories that distinguish competing supports.
profiles.CONSTRAINTS: Library coverage, feature conditioning, sampling, noise dependence, boundary terms and legitimate tuning information.
profiles.EMPIRICAL_SCOPE: Canonical ODE demonstrations and three nonlinear benchmark critiques; DecAEvolve comparison uses one fixed polynomial/Fourier SINDy configuration, which wins oscillator2.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Support ambiguity, coordinate dependence, hidden variables, derivative bias and off-regime error; sparse syntax is not uncertainty calibration.
profiles.CLASSICAL_WIN: FR023 Table5 oscillator2 reports SINDy OOD NMSE 1.45e-8 versus DecAEvolve 1.64e-5 under that protocol.
profiles.HYBRID_ADDED_VALUE: FR010 physical hidden-state reconstruction improves tank fits over naive observed-output libraries, at the cost of stronger priors.
profiles.UNDECIDED: No universal sparse-versus-neural/LLM winner; the required library and informative data are decisive.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Reported comparisons were inspected, not rerun. True-coefficient threshold tuning in FR009 limits blind-recovery extrapolation.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.TITLE: DMD, finite Koopman lifts and HAVOK
profiles.REPRESENTATION: Finite snapshot operator A=YX^+; selected observable lift; possible reconstruction; HAVOK adds a measured delay-coordinate forcing channel.
profiles.INDUCTIVE_BIAS: Approximately linear dynamics in chosen features, low-dimensional spectral representation and sometimes low-rank delay structure.
profiles.INFORMATION_REQUIREMENTS: Observable span and rich data for the desired spectral components; explicit forcing timing; reconstructive features if state recovery is claimed.
profiles.CONSTRAINTS: Finite closure differs from an infinite Koopman operator. FR028 linear consistency means ker(X) is contained in ker(Y), sufficient for finite-pair AX=Y but not genuine nonlinear spectral correspondence.
profiles.EMPIRICAL_SCOPE: Special exact constructions and published examples; no global neural-lift guarantee or general autonomous chaos prediction follows.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Finite data, rank, dictionary omission, topology, reconstruction and forcing errors are separate.
profiles.MATHEMATICAL_CORRECTION: FR012 disproves a universal multi-equilibria obstruction; FR013 restores a restricted result with path-connectedness, continuity, precompactness and countable limit sets.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Theorems apply to their exact domains; HAVOK validation is conditional on supplied forcing from new measurements.
profiles.RECONCILIATION_DISPOSITION: RETAIN_SCOPED_PROFILE_INSTANCE; shared primary kind does not make two example contexts identical.

profiles.TITLE: Structured operator inference
profiles.REPRESENTATION: Polynomial reduced state dynamics in a projection basis, fitted from projected full-model snapshots.
profiles.INDUCTIVE_BIAS: Known polynomial structure and selected low-dimensional basis.
profiles.INFORMATION_REQUIREMENTS: Full-state snapshots, derivative estimates and full-column-rank design matrices.
profiles.CONSTRAINTS: The original theorem chooses reduced dimension/time step existentially and compares with intrusive reduced operators.
profiles.EMPIRICAL_SCOPE: Nonintrusive surrogate modeling for computational systems; not arbitrary partially observed physical identification.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY: Projection truncation, derivative error, conditioning, structural mismatch and simulator-to-plant discrepancy.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: No unconditional stable small-order or external-plant correctness guarantee.

profiles.TITLE: Proportionate model/twin lifecycle investment
profiles.DECISION: A named design, maintenance, control, diagnosis or allocation choice whose outcome can change because of the model.
profiles.UNCERTAINTY_BEFORE_AFTER: State the uncertainty relevant to that choice before modeling; estimate what observations/modeling reduce and what remains assumed. Do not substitute parameter variance for decision uncertainty.
profiles.TOTAL_COST: Data collection, sensors, experiments, expert work, compute, verification, integration, interpretation, monitoring, updates, drift and wrong downstream decisions.
profiles.CONSEQUENCES: Consumer-specific loss and nonmonetary constraints; economic forecasts are hypotheses until observed outcomes support them.
profiles.COMPARATOR: No added model, direct measurement, bounded rule, lookup table, existing specification, simple regression or cheaper local model.
profiles.REUSE_HORIZON: Explicit deployment and reuse period with scenario uncertainty; future possible reuse is not unlimited free benefit.
profiles.RETIREMENT_RULE: Update or retire after material assumption/regime/consumer changes, loss of validation or dominance by a cheaper adequate option; preserve enough provenance for safe re-entry.
profiles.AUTHORITY_BOUNDARY: A model can rank options without validating the objective, feasibility constraints or decision authority.
profiles.EVIDENCE_CEILING: FR025 provides economic modeling, not a local ROI trial; FR026 is workshop consensus, not a mandatory universal standard.
